We prove a finer connection between these two formal systems; namely, given any formula in the language of second order arithmetic, that formula is provable in the aforementioned extension of ZFC if and only if the same formula, when viewed as a type in Lean, is inhabited.

papers.title: Energy-rate equidistribution for adaptive SSAV--BDF2 integration of gradient flows
papers.abstract:
We develop an adaptive time-stepping strategy for scalar auxiliary variable (SAV) schemes combined with variable-step BDF2 discretization for gradient flows. The strategy selects step sizes based on the instantaneous energy dissipation rate and enforces monotonicity of a computable symmetric energy through a step rejection mechanism.
  We show that the step-size rules used in practice correspond to equidistributing a monitor function along the energy curve, connecting energy-adaptive time stepping to the classical theory of r-adaptive mesh methods. The monitor $g = |\dot{E}|$ is asymptotically optimal as it minimises the leading-order maximum symmetric-energy discrepancy for a given number of steps. A combined monitor that switches to $g = \sqrt{|\dot{E}|}$ near equilibrium caps step growth without degrading this error bound. The arclength parameter $\beta$ used in prior work is shown to be the ratio of the largest permitted step to the energy-error tolerance.
  The controller is paired with the SSAV--BDF2 discretization. Accepted steps satisfy monotonicity of the symmetric energy, from which we deduce a bound on the physical energy that is uniform in the number of steps, $\sup_n E(u^n) \le E(u^{0}) + \tau_1 + O(\Delta t_{\max}^2)$, and the scheme achieves second-order global accuracy under standard step-ratio restrictions. Numerical experiments on Cahn--Hilliard, Ohta--Kawasaki, Phase--Field Crystal, and functionalized Cahn--Hilliard models confirm the theory and demonstrate the method's efficiency.

papers.title: Fefferman--Chang-type atomic decompositions for product Hardy spaces associated with Schr\"odinger operators
papers.abstract:
We establish a geometric (Fefferman--Chang-type) atomic characterization of the two-parameter Hardy space associated with a pair of Schr\"odinger operators $L_i=-\Delta+V_i$ on $\mathbb R^{n_i}$, $i=1,2$. The space is defined by the product conical square function. We assume comparability of neighbouring covering cubes, a local bound on the potentials, and decay of the semigroup mass at large scales.
  We prove that the Hardy norm is equivalent to a sum of classical local product Hardy norms at scales determined by the adapted coverings. This localization formula yields an atomic decomposition whose atoms satisfy size and partial cancellation conditions, with cancellation required only below the corresponding local scales. Both the atoms and their rectangular components remain supported inside fixed enlargements of the covering rectangles.
  The proof combines one-parameter Schr\"odinger Hardy space characterizations with standard vector-valued arguments and a localized product atomic decomposition with uniform control of scales and supports. The assumptions cover the model case of reverse H\"older potentials $V\in RH_q$, $q>n/2$, as well as potentials outside every $RH_q$ class, $q>1$, including half-space indicators and exponential potentials.

papers.title: Local Optimality of the d-cube for Laplacian Eigenvalues
papers.abstract: For each $d \ge 2$ we prove that the unit $d$-cube $\square_d \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ is, on the class $\mathcal{P}$ of convex polytopes combinatorially equivalent to a $d$-cube, (i) a strict local minimizer of the scale-invariant isoperimetric ratio $I(\Omega) = \tfrac{P(\Omega)^d}{|\Omega|^{d-1}}$, with $P$ the perimeter, (ii) a strict local minimizer of the volume-normalized first Dirichlet eigenvalue $\bar\lambda(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\lambda_1(\Omega)$, and (iii) a strict local maximizer of the volume-normalized first Neumann eigenvalue $\bar\mu(\Omega) = |\Omega|^{2/d}\mu_1(\Omega)$. The method is a shape-derivative Hessian analysis adapted to the hyperoctahedral symmetry of the cube. In symmetry-adapted coordinates on the parameter space --- the decomposition into irreducible representations of the hyperoctahedral group --- each Hessian is block-diagonal, with four scalar eigenvalues, which we give in closed form in $\pi$, rational coefficients, and a few universal series-constants. The first Neumann eigenvalue is not differentiable at $\square_d$, since its lowest cluster splits under perturbation. The Neumann case therefore works with a smooth auxiliary functional, whose Hessian is computed by second-order perturbation theory of the cluster; the coupling to modes outside the cluster enters at the same order. Finally, we show that extremality of $I$, $\bar\lambda$, and $\bar\mu$ does not hold in high dimensions for a particular multilinear perturbation that leaves $\mathcal{P}$ by breaking convexity. All results are local; we discuss why a global statement, available for quadrilaterals (Endo and Osting, 2026), appears out of reach for $d \ge 3$.

papers.title: A smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres with Bernoulli geodesic flow
papers.authors: Keith Burns, Tomas Gedeon, Yuping Ruan
papers.abstract: We construct a smooth Riemannian metric on an arbitrary product of spheres whose geodesic flow is Bernoulli with respect to the Liouville measure.

papers.title: Classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebras on solvable Lie conformal algebras of rank two
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a complete classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebra structures on solvable Lie conformal algebras which are free of rank two as $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-modules up to isomorphism. We obtain ten mutually non-isomorphic normal-form types and determine the precise equivalence relations among the parameters within each family. Moreover, we also characterize the Novikov conformal algebras among the classified left-symmetric conformal algebras, thereby obtaining a complete classification of compatible Novikov conformal algebra structures in the same setting.

papers.title: An explicit elementary proof of no Landau--Siegel zeros
papers.abstract: We give an elementary proof of the absence of Landau--Siegel zeros with the explicit constant $c=1/100$. For every primitive quadratic Dirichlet character $\chi$ of conductor $q\ge3$, each real zero $\beta\in(0,1)$ of $L(s,\chi)$ satisfies $(1-\beta)\log q>c$. The proof combines integer coefficient counting, polynomial congruences, a paired-tail hyperbola estimate, and a logarithmically weighted comparison of positive sums. All required constants are explicit, and one choice of parameters covers every conductor. The argument uses elementary arithmetic and real summation and integration, without separate zero computations for small conductors.

papers.title: $\SL_3$ dual pairs
papers.authors: Petar Baki\'c, Wee Teck Gan, Gordan Savin
papers.abstract: We study the exceptional theta correspondence for dual pairs of the form $\SL_3\times G$ inside $p$-adic groups of type $E_n$, $n=6,7,8$. We establish Howe duality for lifts of all Whittaker-generic unitarizable representations of $\SL_3$. Our dual pair is in a see-saw relationship with a dual pair of the form $G_2 \times H$ such that $G/H$ is a rank-two symmetric space. Using the theta correspondence for $\SL_3 \times G$, we prove a multiplicity-one result for $H$-invariant functionals on representations of $G$.

papers.title: Finiteness theorems for Cayley permutation classes
papers.abstract: We prove that every hereditary Cayley permutation class with finitely many simple members has a finite basis and an algebraic generating function. We first show that every simple Cayley permutation of length at least two contains a simple pattern obtained by deleting one or two letters, and that the only exceptional Cayley permutations are the simple parallel alternations and their symmetries. We then characterize substitution-closed classes by the simplicity of their basis elements and show that classes with finitely many simple members are partially well ordered. Given the simple members and the basis of such a class, we construct a finite system of functional equations and compute an annihilating polynomial.

papers.title: Comb Tensor Network Finite-Difference Time-Domain Algorithms for 2D and 3D Electromagnetic Simulations
papers.authors: Jonathan Tabares, Erika Ye, Yang Liu
papers.abstract: This paper presents efficient 2D and 3D finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) algorithms augmented by the comb tensor network (CTN) representation of the field and auxiliary quantities. The proposed CTN-FDTD algorithm leverages superior compressibility of CTN compared with quantized tensor train (QTT), and rank-reduction strategies including local and global smoothing techniques to achieve logarithmic memory requirement and computation (per time step) cost. Numerical examples validate these complexities and demonstrate the applicability of CTN-FDTD using a variety of source excitation, frequency and permittivity profiles in both 2D and 3D. Remarkably, CTN-FDTD can simulate 35 trillion spatial grid points in 3D with low memory and computation costs on one computation node, whereas standard FDTD would require 281 TB memory to store each of its 31 3D arrays. Moreover, CTN-FDTD was applied to realistic 2D photonic crystal structure simulation with one million grid points and 3D scattering analysis with 8.6 billion grid points.

papers.title: A note on the proof of Barnette's conjecture
papers.abstract: Barnette's conjecture states that every cubic 3-connected bipartite planar graph has a Hamiltonian cycle. We present a digested exposition of OpenAI's generated proof of Barnette's conjecture \cite{openai-barnette}.

papers.title: Discovery of Singularities in Partial Differential Equations Using Adaptive Numerical Discretizations
papers.authors: Allen Yang, Lucas Amoudruz, Petros Koumoutsakos
papers.abstract: We compute self-similar singularity profiles of partial differential equations (PDEs) using adaptive numerical discretizations based on optimizing a discrete loss (ODIL). The fields are represented in overlapping local Chebyshev patches joined with a mapped asymptotic patch. After factoring out the leading power laws of solution ansatzes, their limiting amplitudes at infinity are determined by the optimization, eliminating domain truncation and prescribed far-field conditions. Adaptive refinement is guided by Chebyshev-coefficient decay, and the nonlinear least-squares problem is solved using automatically differentiated Gauss--Newton iterations with Levenberg--Marquardt damping. The method achieves O(10^{-14})-level accuracy for Burgers profiles, residuals of O(10^{-14}) to O(10^{-10}) for the generalized De Gregorio family, and of O(10^{-8}) in a local region for the two-dimensional Boussinesq equations. These results demonstrate that ODIL can identify singularity profiles for PDEs with high accuracy using adaptive numerical methods, complementing ongoing efforts that rely on artificial intelligence.

papers.title: Entropy bounded compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for hyperbolic conservation laws
papers.authors: Deepak Kumar, Pratima Rai, Arvind Patel
papers.abstract: In this paper we introduce a compact stencil Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin method for the Euler equations of compressible gas dynamics, which preserves a minimum entropy principle similar to that introduced by Tadmor for entropy solution of the Euler equations [4]. Compact stencil RKDG, introduced by Chen et al. in [15], is a variant of standard RKDG method which is known for its smaller stencil size and parallel efficiency. The main challenge is that the cRKDG method has to be expressed in Butcher form and not every Runge-Kutta method of this form is a convex combination of forward-Euler steps. Therefore, in order to establish this property we leverage the bound preserving framework of the cRKDG schemes [8], an entropy bounded limiter [6] and the classical positivity preserving limiter. In the last section numerical experiments are provided to demonstrate the robustness of the method.

papers.title: An F-Type Normal-Reference Calibration for High-Dimensional Covariance Testing
papers.abstract: An F-type normal-reference calibration is developed for testing equality of two high-dimensional covariance matrices with unknown means. The test statistic is a ratio whose numerator measures the Frobenius covariance discrepancy and whose denominator estimates its null expectation. Their difference is the complete Li-Chen statistic. Under suitable moment and trace conditions, we establish a Gaussian-reference approximation. After standardization, the statistic and its reference share the normal or nonnormal limits determined by a convergent normalized spectrum. The reference is a ratio of independent chi-square-type mixtures. Applying Welch-Satterthwaite matching to its two components gives an ordinary F approximation, with degrees of freedom estimated from independent four-observation blocks. The effect of estimating the population means is controlled by an exact expansion, and local-power and consistency results are established. The ordinary F approximation is asymptotically valid under a diffuse spectrum, whereas a covariance spike can produce a nonvanishing approximation error. Simulation studies examine empirical size and power under normal and nonnormal sampling. Averaging the trace estimates over fixed partitions improves their stability, but does not remove size inflation in the strongly correlated settings.

papers.title: When Language Models Misinterpret Uncertainty in Earth System Mechanism Attribution
papers.abstract: Mechanistic attribution in Earth system science requires quantifying uncertainty and communicating its implications. Here, we develop an uncertainty-aware mechanistic attribution pipeline that constructs probabilistic fingerprints from ensemble estimates, including covariance-aware separation of competing mechanisms, and an evidence ladder that systematically varies the information provided to language models (LLMs). We evaluate this framework in an idealized stochastic system and a coupled El Ni\~no model using controlled interventions and ensemble data assimilation. In the idealized system, numerical separation increases GPT-4o's intervention-label agreement from 0.80 to 0.98, but not GPT-4o-mini's. In the coupled system, both LLMs identify seven of eight fingerprint-ambiguous events when given full fingerprints with verbal interpretations; GPT-4o's false ambiguity reports decrease from 10/82 to 1/82, without consistent gains in intervention-label agreement. For eight historical ENSO events, the uncertainty-aware condition agrees with the model-inferred mechanism labels in seven cases. These findings distinguish uncertainty assessment from its communication.

papers.title: The linearity Conjecture
papers.abstract: The Linearity Conjecture states that in the projective plane PG(2,$q$), $q=p^h$, every minimal blocking set (w.r.t. lines) is a linear point set over some subfield of ${\mathbb F}_q$. This paper contains the proof of the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\ne 3,4$, where $e$ is the exponent of the blocking set. The text contains 3 concatenated parts. In Part 0, we give a guide for reading Parts 1 and 2. Part 1 develops a great part of the method, and the case $p^e=2$ is solved. In Part 2 we prove the Linearity Conjecture for $p^e\geq 5$.

papers.title: Drinfeld presentation of affine iquantum groups via iHopf algebras
papers.abstract: Affine quantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}$ and affine iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ admit two complementary descriptions: a Serre-type presentation and a Drinfeld (current) presentation. While iquantum groups $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ are typically defined via the Serre presentation, their Drinfeld presentations are substantially more subtle and less well understood. In this paper, we give a conceptual derivation of the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ starting directly from the Drinfeld presentation of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, working within the framework of iHopf algebras. This approach leads naturally to the definition of iquantum affinization associated with arbitrary Kac-Moody algebras $\mathfrak{g}$. We further show that, in this general setting, these iquantum affinizations can be realized as coideal subalgebras of quantum affinizations with respect to the Drinfeld coproduct. Finally, in the affine case, we describe the imaginary root vectors $\Theta_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$ explicitly in terms of the root vectors $\psi^\pm_{i,r}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}$, thereby extending the results of Li and Prze\'zdziecki for certain affine types of $\widetilde{\mathbf {U}}^\imath$.

papers.title: A Study in Solution Models for SAT using the PBNF-transform
papers.abstract: In this article, we use the PBNF-transform, or Polynomial Boolean Normal Form, described earlier in two articles and now extended to higher arity, to solve Boolean satisfiability problems (SAT), which are part of the P versus NP problem. SAT consists of a statement of conjunctions of clauses, and in our SAT-solving models, we dualize the logical equations, inverting the problem by \emph{multiplying} letters (literals) in the transferred clauses, now phrases: $pqrs\cdots s_{\ell}$, and using a binary iterated composition based on \emph{adding polynomials} for the conjunctions in our solution formula. We obtain Polynomial Boolean Equations, PBE=0, by also renaming the truth value $1\mapsto 0$(T). To find a solution, we look for repeating literals in the clauses to factor out. With reversed literal repetition, we can even reduce the CNF to the sum of the transformed clauses.

papers.title: Supercritical magnetic ray transforms in hyperbolic space: the complexification method from the transport-twistor lens
papers.abstract: We present new inversion formulas for the unattenuated and attenuated magnetic ray transforms in the Poincar\'e disk, in the case of a constant, supercritical magnetic field. Our approach mirrors earlier complexification approaches by Novikov (Ark. Mat., 2002) and Bal (J. Math. Pures Appl., 2005), and a second feature of this article is to connect the approach with the Transport Twistor framework recently introduced by Bohr-Paternain (J. \'Ec. polytech. Math., 2023; arXiv:2606.25173).

papers.title: The reverse Ritz inclusion: computable bounds on the pseudospectra of an operator by those of a finite-rank compression
papers.abstract: We consider a bounded operator on a separable complex Hilbert space, reached only through its action on vectors and that of its adjoint, and split it along a subspace of finite dimension into a compression, a far block acting on the complement, and the two couplings between them. Given upper bounds on the norms of the couplings and of the far block, we show that outside a disc a pseudospectrum of the operator lies in a pseudospectrum of the compression, with an explicit loss in the level; this reverses the classical inclusion of the Ritz values in a pseudospectrum of the operator. The same bounds, with the smallest singular value of the shifted compression, bound the resolvent of the operator, count its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity inside every contour outside the disc on which a computed inequality holds, and enclose its spectral projector; no normality, self-adjointness or positivity is used.

papers.title: High-Order Fully Discrete Entropy-Stable DG Methods with Compact Explicit Single-Step Time Discretizations
papers.authors: Yuchang Liu, Yan Jiang, Mengping Zhang
papers.abstract: We develop a unified framework for high-order, fully discrete entropy-stable discontinuous Galerkin (DG) methods with compact explicit single-step time discretizations. At the end of each time step, the preliminary DG polynomial is scaled toward its cell average to enforce a strong cell entropy inequality while preserving conservation. This correction is feasible if and only if the updated cell average satisfies a weak cell entropy inequality, which standard third-order strong-stability-preserving Runge--Kutta DG updates can violate at arbitrarily small positive CFL numbers. For compact single-step schemes, including compact Runge--Kutta, Lax--Wendroff, and ADER-DG methods, we derive an explicit interval of feasible numerical entropy fluxes at each interface and prove that it is nonempty under a CFL condition. Projecting a compatible high-order target flux onto this interval guarantees the weak cell entropy inequality and preserves single-step high-order accuracy on smooth solutions, including near nondegenerate extrema. The limiter also enforces multiple entropy inequalities simultaneously. We also establish a Lax--Wendroff-type theorem. Numerical experiments for scalar conservation laws and the compressible Euler equations demonstrate high-order accuracy, multi-entropy control, and robustness for strong shocks.

papers.title: Matrix Triangle Inequalities: Past, Present, and Future
papers.abstract: This survey provides a concise overview of matrix triangle inequalities. Classical topics, such as inequalities for unitarily invariant norms, are revisited from a different perspective, with a particular emphasis on unitary orbit inequalities and various notions of matrix moduli. The exposition progresses from elementary results to much more recent developments, highlighting the evolution of the subject and its ongoing directions of research.

papers.title: Spin-Clifford Bundles and Spin Connections on the Hyperbolic Clifford Algebra - Part I
papers.authors: E. Notte-Cuello, J. M. Hoff da Silva
papers.abstract: We develop the theory of spinor fields associated with the hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathbb{R}^{H}=\mathcal{C}\ell(H_V)$, which is associated with hyperbolic space $H_V=V\oplus V^{*}$. Algebraically, we exhibit an explicit real primitive idempotent which, unlike the Lorentzian case, remains primitive after complexification and generates the ideal of Witten superfields. We also describe the chirality decomposition and the hyperbolic spin group. Geometrically, we construct a canonical hyperbolic spin structure on every oriented manifold, showing that no topological obstructions arise beyond orientability and we study the associated spinor bundles, spin-Clifford bundles and ideal spinor subbundles. Finally, we introduce the isotropic extension of an arbitrary linear connection to $TM\oplus T^*M$, which is always compatible with the hyperbolic metric, and the associated hyperbolic spin connection, whose well-definedness, compatibilities, curvature and explicit form are established, providing the geometric framework for Dirac operators on the hyperbolic Clifford algebra, which we will present in a forthcoming article.

papers.title: Rigid and $\tau$-locally free modules via Taft algebras
papers.abstract: We show that rigid modules are $\tau$-locally free for a large family of 1-Iwanaga--Gorenstein algebras. This family includes many cases of the algebras introduced by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer in their Inventiones paper "Quivers with relations for symmetrizable Cartan matrices I: Foundations", hence answering a question posed by Geiss--Leclerc--Schr\"oer for many new cases. Our result is achieved by introducing coactions of Taft algebras and applying the recent theory developed by the first-named author and Coulembier.

papers.title: Very tight embeddings of subspaces of \(L_p\) for \(0<p<1\)
papers.abstract: For \(0<p<1\) and \(\mu>1\), every \(d\)-dimensional subspace of \(L_p\) embeds linearly into \(\ell_p^{\lfloor\mu d\rfloor}\) with distortion at most \(C(p,\mu)(\log(d+2))^{1/p}\). If its Rademacher type \(q\) constant is at most \(T\), where \(p<q\leq2\), the distortion is at most \(C(p,q,\mu)T\), independently of \(d\). We also give explicit bounds as \(\mu\downarrow1\). This answers the question of Johnson and Schechtman concerning the extension of their very tight embedding theorem below exponent one. The proof combines compression at a lower exponent with a change of density that preserves the number of coordinates, and applies over both scalar fields.

papers.title: Localizing Restriction Categories
papers.abstract:
The localizing/separating factorization, which is the analogue, for restriction categories, to the surjective/embedding factorization for topoi, is developed at both the mere restriction category and join restriction category level. The factorization system at both the ordinary and join level is approached using the notion of a density, which is a stable and universal suborder of the restriction order. The main technical results of the paper construct the join localization and establish its basic properties. 
  The paper gives several examples of localizations. In particular, examples of localization on commutative rigs are provided which give a way to construct categories of schemes. The Zariski spectrum and the Pierce spectrum are, in particular, developed.

papers.title: Return Time Sets of Minimal Points for Countable Group Actions
papers.abstract: For a countably infinite discrete group $G$, we study subsets of $G$ that contain a neighbourhood return-time set of a minimal point in a $G$-flow $X$. For $e\in F\subseteq G$, we characterize this property by the existence of $e\in A\subseteq F$ such that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A):=\{t\in G:Kt\subseteq A\}$ is right syndetic for every finite $K\subseteq A$, and equivalently by the support of a minimal binary configuration in the Bernoulli shift $2^G$. Additional conditions on $\operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ characterize realization by minimal flows that are weakly mixing of all finite orders or strongly mixing: for every such $K$, the former requires that for each finite $H\subseteq G$ there is $c\in G$ with $HcH\subseteq \operatorname{Int}_K(A) \operatorname{Int}_K(A) ^{-1}$, whereas the latter requires that $\operatorname{Int}_K(A)\operatorname{Int}_K(A)^{-1}$ be cofinite. We also construct, for every compact metrizable minimal $G$-flow, a free minimal, strongly mixing Cantor flow disjoint from it.

papers.title: Classification of binary, ternary and quaternary Hermitian LCD codes
papers.abstract: We extend the complete classifications of linear complementary dual (LCD) codes from length 15 to length 19 in the binary case, from length 10 to length 15 in the ternary case and from length 12 to length 13 in the quaternary Hermitian case. The classification rests on a reduction of the monomial equivalence of LCD codes to graph isomorphism on the coordinates, combined with canonical augmentation.

papers.title: Computable presentations of separable Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: For every right-c.e.\ real $p\in(1,2)$, $L^p[0,1]$ has a computable presentation. The proof combines an effective stability modulus for almost isometric embeddings with a Fra\"{\i}ss\'e-style construction in which the exponent varies. In the same range, if $\ell^p$ has a computable presentation, then $p$ is computable. Combining these with the known results gives the computable presentability classification for all separable Lebesgue spaces. We also formulate an effective Fra\"{\i}ss\'e theorem for Banach spaces and apply it to obtain a computable presentation of the Gurarij Banach space.

papers.title: Collinear motions in constant curvature spaces, and coplanar motions in $\mathbb{R^4}$
papers.authors: Carlos Barrera-Anzaldo, Abimael Bengochea, Connor Jackman, Ernesto P\'erez-Chavela
papers.abstract:
A collinear motion of an $n$-body problem is one in which the $n$-bodies always lie along some, possibly moving, geodesic during their evolution.
  We prove that every collinear motion of $n\geq 3$ bodies in a constant non-zero curvature space is necessarily contained in some fixed constant curvature space of dimension at most three. For natural systems admitting energy and angular momentum integrals, we further show that every such motion is necessarily a relative equilibrium: evolving under uniform rotation while maintaining constant mutual distances.
  These results extend certain classical results on collinear motions in Euclidean spaces, initiated by P. Pizzetti, to general spaces of constant curvature. The same methods also yield a partial answer to a question of A. Wintner. Namely, we show that any concave and always coplanar motion in the Euclidean 4-body problem, where the moving plane containing the bodies sweeps out an $\mathbb{R}^4$, must be self-similar: maintaining constant mutual distance ratios over the motion.

papers.title: Non-aware computable presentations of randomizations
papers.abstract: Let 2 be the two-element structure in the empty signature. We build a computable presentation Q of the Borel randomization $2^{[0,1)}$ in which neither constant random variable is a computable point. Consequently, Q is not aware. This gives a negative answer to a question of Cuervo Ovalle and Goldbring \cite{CG}. We also construct a countable structure $M$ with no computable presentation but $M^{[0,1)}$ has a computable presentation. This answers another question and establishes the necessity of the awareness condition stated in one of the main theorems in \cite{CG}.

papers.title: Asymptotics of local height pairing without Hodge conjecture
papers.abstract: We remove the assumption of the Hodge conjecture from the asymptotic formula for the Archimedean local height established in our previous work. We also remove other minor assumptions. We achieve this by exploiting the cohomological nature of Beilinson's local intersection index rather than arguing motivically.

papers.title: Scattering theory for bulk and surface waves in an impedance half-space, II: local perturbations, the scattering matrix and an inverse problem
papers.abstract: We study the Robin, or impedance, Laplacian on a half-space of dimension $n \ge 3$ which is perturbed inside a fixed ball. The boundary may be deformed, and obstacles may be present in the interior or attached to the boundary, in any combination and with no smallness assumption. Outside the ball the configuration is the flat impedance half-space of Part I, with constant impedance $\alpha > 0$, where a bulk channel and a surface channel propagate at every positive energy and only the surface channel propagates on the band $(-\alpha^2,0)$. We prove a limiting absorption principle, valid at every positive energy and outside a discrete set of embedded eigenvalues in the band. We construct the generalized Fourier transform and prove its completeness by a stationary argument which constructs no wave operator and reduces completeness to the uniqueness of the scattering solution at each energy. We then obtain the scattering matrix, its unitarity and a two-channel optical theorem. The main result is a uniqueness theorem for the inverse problem. Under two geometric conditions on the pair, the scattering amplitude at a single positive energy determines the perturbation completely, and the argument does not distinguish a deformation of the boundary from an obstacle. It follows that no nontrivial perturbation satisfying the same conditions is invisible at any positive energy. On the surface band the corresponding statement is reduced to one explicitly stated question about the exterior Robin problem.

papers.title: Explicit Measurable Counterexamples to Finite-Difference Equations
papers.abstract: We study finite-difference operators of the form \[ D(f,h)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f(b_kh), \] where the coefficients may be complex and the nodes are real. Ash, Catoiu, and Cs\"ornyei characterized the finite differences for which \[ D(f,h)=o(h)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad f(h)=o(h) \] holds for every measurable real-valued function. We extend their counterexample theorem to complex-valued functions defined on \(\mathbb C\). Except for the same exceptional four-term configuration, we construct a Lebesgue measurable function \(f\) such that \[ D(f,h)=0\qquad\text{for every }h\in\mathbb C, \] while \(f(h)\not=o(1)\) as \(h\to0\). The counterexamples are supported on countable multiplicative subgroups. The construction is based on zeros of Laurent polynomials and multiplicative characters, and avoids the infinite-dimensional linear-algebra argument used in the earlier proof.

papers.title: Soft-Update MSA for Nonconvex Stochastic Optimal Control: Theory and Algorithms
papers.abstract: For the method of successive approximations (MSA), a fundamental challenge is that the stochastic maximum principle (SMP) provides an optimality condition rather than a descent rule. To overcome this difficulty for nonconvex stochastic control problems, we develop a soft-update MSA (SU-MSA) with a second-order-adjoint correction of the Hamiltonian and a neural realization called DeepSMP. Both an explicit stepsize rule guaranteeing cost descent and the convergence of the algorithm are established. Moreover, the global SMP condition is asymptotically satisfied when the corrected Hamiltonian is convex, while in a special case the cost is further proved to converge to the global optimum. To extend SU-MSA to high dimensions, we develop DeepSMP using a differentiable smooth approximation of the corrected Hamiltonian and analyze the convergence of the resulting objective and its gradient. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Explicit meromorphic solutions of certain types of nonlinear differential-difference equations
papers.abstract: Our main purpose is to determine all meromorphic solutions, in explicit form, of the nonlinear differential-difference equations \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z)f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z} \end{equation*} and \begin{equation*} f^{n}(z)f'(z)+q(z){\rm e}^{Q(z)}f(z+c)=p_{1}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{1}z}+p_{2}{\rm e}^{\alpha_{2}z}, \end{equation*} where $n\geq 3$ is an integer, $q(z)$ and $Q(z)$ are nonzero polynomials with $Q(z)$ nonconstant, and $c,~p_{j},~\alpha_{j}(j=1,2)$ are nonzero constants satisfying $\alpha_{1}\neq \alpha_{2}$. We sharpen the result in the cited literature, as illustrated by specific examples.

papers.title: Weighted boundedness of maximal operator associated with invertible linear transformations on variable Lebesgue spaces
papers.authors: Gonzalo H. Iba\~nez Firnkorn, Lucas A. Vallejos
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the boundedness of $M_{A^{-1}}$, the maximal operator involves an invertible matrix, on the weighted variable spaces $L^{p(\cdot)}(w)$, where the weights are in an appropriate class. In general, we obtain the necessary conditions for the weight classes and exponents. However, for certain types of invertible matrices, we characterize the weights such that the boundedness holds.

papers.title: The dual complex and RC-invariant functors
papers.abstract: We extend the dual complex of a simple normal crossings divisor to a homotopy type invariant $\mathcal{D}(X)$ of arbitrary complex varieties, and we prove that it is contractible when $X$ is connected and of klt type. In fact, the dual complex belongs to a broader class of invariants, which we call RC (rationally connected)-invariant functors. We prove a rigidity theorem governing the behavior of such functors with respect to rationally connected fibrations.

papers.title: Asymptotically Sharp Length Thresholds for \texorpdfstring{$q$}{q}-ary Codes with Distances \texorpdfstring{$2$}{2} and \texorpdfstring{$4$}{4}
papers.authors: Valjakas Djaljapayan, Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Wei-Hsuan Yu
papers.abstract:
For an integer $q\ge5$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of a $q$-ary Hamming space of length $n$ in which every two distinct words have distance $2$ or $4$. Set \[ N(q)=\left\lceil\max\left\{2q+1,
  \frac{17+\sqrt{8q^2+96q-95}}2\right\}\right\rceil. \] We prove that $A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2$ for every $n\ge N(q)$. In particular, $N(q)=2q+1$ for $q\ge26$. An explicit code of size $q(n-2)$ shows that the least eventual threshold $N_*(q)$ satisfies $N_*(q)\ge2q-1$; consequently $2q-1\le N_*(q)\le2q+1$ for every $q\ge26$. The argument applies to arbitrary integer alphabet sizes, without a linearity assumption. Its main ingredients are synchronization of symbols on intersecting supports, weighted bounds for $2$-intersecting families of four-sets, and a joint estimate for the weight-two and weight-four layers in a common-three-core configuration. No computational verification is required.

papers.title: The Ternary and Quaternary Cases of the $\{2,4\}$-Distance Code Conjecture
papers.authors: Yen-Chi Roger Lin, Valjakas Djaljapayan, Wei-Hsuan Yu
papers.abstract:
For an integer $q\ge2$, let $A_q(n,\{2,4\})$ be the largest cardinality of an unrestricted $q$-ary code of length $n$ in which any two distinct words have Hamming distance $2$ or $4$. We prove that \[
  A_q(n,\{2,4\})=1+\binom n2
  \qquad(q\in\{3,4\},\ n\ge6), \] thereby settling the two remaining alphabet sizes in the conjecture of Boyvalenkov, Delchev, Zinoviev, and Zinoviev; the binary case was settled previously. The quaternary result implies the ternary result by alphabet inclusion. For $n\ge16$, the quaternary upper bound is proved combinatorially. After normalizing one word to zero, the weight-four supports form a $2$-intersecting family; exact support intersections force symbol synchronization and restrict support multiplicities. We combine the nontrivial intersection theorem with matching arguments and a three-coordinate projection lemma. The finite lengths $6\le n\le13$ are handled by a complete Hamming-isometry reduction to exact clique decisions, and $n=14,15$ by a smaller exact weighted-clique relaxation. All finite decisions are reproduced by two standalone integer-only C++17 verifiers provided as supplementary source files.

papers.title: Retraction-Free Nonsmooth Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold: Subgradient and Proximal Landing Methods
papers.authors: Zilong Cui, Tongxin Hu, Bin Gao, Ran Gu
papers.abstract: We develop three retraction-free Landing methods for nonsmooth composite optimization over the Stiefel manifold, combining an (approximately) tangential direction with an infeasibility-reducing normal direction. The subgradient Landing method, with normal stepsizes parameterized by $\alpha\in[0,1]$, has best-iterate complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-4})$ for surrogate stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2/(2-\alpha)})$ for feasibility. For $\alpha=0$, it converges locally $R$-linearly under local weak sharpness and mild assumptions. The proximal gradient Landing method computes a tangential direction by solving a proximal subproblem and combines it with the same normal direction. Moreover, the inexact proximal gradient Landing method allows the proximal subproblem to be solved approximately and applies an explicit correction to control violations of the tangency condition. Both proximal methods have outer-iteration complexity bounds $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-2})$ for stationarity and $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-1})$ for feasibility, and every accumulation point is first-order stationary. Under an additional asymptotic Bregman-error condition and the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz property of a suitable auxiliary function, the primal sequence of the inexact method converges to a first-order stationary point. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of all three methods. On the tested sparse principal component analysis instances, the inexact method has favorable running times, and both proximal methods maintain small feasibility residuals.

papers.title: Comprehensive Resolution of the Gauss-Fourier Conjecture for the First Kind of Zeros
papers.abstract: For over two centuries, the esteemed mathematicians Gauss and Fourier conjectured that each real critical point of the rational function $p^{'}(s)/p(s)$ is associated with a pair of non-real zeros of the real polynomial $p(s)$. The conjecture remains unresolved. The real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ that are real multiple zero of $p^{'}(s)$ are defined as the second kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. In addition to the second kind of zeros, the other real zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ are referred to as the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$. We demonstrate that the first kind of zeros of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ emerge from the intersection of root loci emitted from non-real zeros of $p(s)$, thereby providing a comprehensive geometric interpretation of their relationship. Moreover, each first kind of zero of $(p^{'}(s)/p(s))^{'}$ is connected via root loci to a pair of conjugate non-real zeros of $p(s)$. This establishes the precise geometric relationship conjectured by Gauss and Fourier, fully resolving their original problem for first-kind zeros and completing a foundational chapter in polynomial theory. We have proven Gauss-Fourier conjecture about the first kind of zeros.

papers.title: Norm-Euclideanity in cyclic fields
papers.abstract: Consider a cyclic number field of prime degree $p$. For a fixed degree, there are only finitely many such fields which are norm-Euclidean. When $p=2$ or $3$, these have been completely determined. If instead $p>3$, one can bound the discriminant of such fields from above. We substantially sharpen these upper bounds via an explicit Burgess-type criterion and describe a method for completely resolving other small prime cases.

papers.title: Sharp convergence rate of the estimation error of LASSO via the Feature Space Decomposition method
papers.abstract: In this paper, we use the Feature Space Decomposition (FSD) method to establish an explicit, non-asymptotic, instance-optimal convergence rate for the estimation error of the LASSO in the Gaussian linear regression problem for any signal, any diagonal covariance and any regularization parameter above $\sigma_\xi/\sqrt{N}$ where $\sigma_\xi$ is the noise variance and $N$ the number of data.

papers.title: First-order differential constraints for the nonlinear wave equation:wave fronts, admissible nonlinearities and exact solutions
papers.abstract: We construct exact solutions of the nonlinear wave equation in three space dimensions by the method of linear determining equations: first-order constraint functions are found as solutions of the linear determining equation, the differential constraints obtained by setting them equal to zero are integrated, and the resulting ansatz is substituted into the equation. Lie point symmetries are a special case, and the solutions obtained generically have no symmetry. The determining equations tie the admissible nonlinearity to the geometry of the constraint: arbitrary on characteristic hyperplanes, cubic on light cones, and, for a pair of constraints, exponential on light cones and quintic on the cylindrical fronts of a line source. Among the solutions are smooth bounded sine-Gordon walls and vortex configurations whose shape varies arbitrarily along a front, the fields of point sources moving on arbitrary trajectories for the cubic and Liouville equations, with an exact nonlinear analogue of the Larmor formula for the power radiated in the cubic case, and smooth finite-energy solutions of the cubic equation with any prescribed number of toroidal nodal surfaces.

papers.title: Pluripotency and Anosov Dynamics
papers.authors: Shin Kiriki, Xiaolong Li, Kodai Yamamoto
papers.abstract:
We study two notions of pluripotency for dynamical systems. Strong pluripotency refers to the possibility of reprogramming, by arbitrarily small perturbations, the forward orbits of points in a set of positive Riemannian volume so that they track a prescribed orbit in a uniform time-averaged sense. In contrast, pluripotency, also called ``statistical pluripotency" in this paper, requires only asymptotic agreement of empirical measures. Strong pluripotency implies statistical pluripotency, but the converse need not hold.
  For $C^r$ transitive Anosov diffeomorphisms, $r\ge2$, we prove that strong pluripotency fails for every nonempty reference set. On the other hand, statistical pluripotency holds for a nonempty reference set if and only if it is contained in the basin of the unique SRB measure. This basin is invariant and has full Riemannian volume, but contains no periodic points. These results reveal a sharp distinction between the two notions even within uniformly hyperbolic dynamics.

papers.title: Couplings with prescribed maxima: A short proof of the quasi-copula characterization
papers.abstract: We provide a short probabilistic proof of the classical characterization of multivariate quasi-copulas, addressing the call for a simpler and more transparent proof expressed by Sempi (2017). Our approach is based on a coupling construction for random variables with fixed marginal distributions and a prescribed distribution of their maximum. In our main result, we show that such a coupling exists if and only if the maximum is stochastically no smaller than each component and the distribution of the maximum is dominated by the sum of the marginal measures. The construction applies to arbitrary distributions and relies only on a decomposition of the maximum law and monotone quantile couplings. A direct consequence of our main result is the existence of copulas with prescribed values along an increasing track.

papers.title: Octonionic and Monogenic Completions of Harmonic Functions
papers.abstract: Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a domain, with $n\ge2$. We characterize the real-valued harmonic functions that can occur as prescribed real components of monogenic functions. For any fixed nonzero real Clifford module $M$ and any fixed unit vector $s\in M$, a smooth real-valued function $h$ can be written as $h=\langle F,s\rangle$ with $F$ monogenic if and only if the $(n-1)$-form $*dh$ is exact. Consequently, every real-valued harmonic function on $\Omega$ admits such a representation if and only if $H_{\mathrm{dR}}^{n-1}(\Omega)=0$. In dimension eight, the same exactness criterion characterizes the real parts of octonionic regular functions and yields the corresponding equivalence with $H_{\mathrm{dR}}^7(\Omega)=0$. The proofs use global solvability of the Poisson equation and elementary identities for differential forms.

papers.title: Adaptive Restart under Unknown KL Geometry in Stochastic Weakly-Convex Optimization
papers.authors: Binh T. Nguyen, Khoa D. Nguyen, Bao Thai Huynh
papers.abstract: KL geometry accelerates restart schedules in stochastic weakly-convex optimization, but the schedule depends jointly on an unknown and potentially nonunique geometric description. We introduce CARP-KL, a certified portfolio that adapts over valid KL descriptions while using the same primitive stochastic-subgradient oracle for both optimization and candidate selection. Over declared polynomial parameter ranges, CARP-KL competes with every affordable valid description and preserves the known-description polynomial Moreau-stationarity rate up to logarithmic factors, without objective values, an exact proximal map, direct Moreau-gradient access, or a bounded-domain assumption. Controlled experiments quantify the finite-budget price of this universality. The portfolio repeatedly contains strong candidates, while certification consumes a substantial share of the oracle budget and finite-sample ranking limits their recovery. A common conservative gap bound further reduces the portfolio from $O(\log^3 T)$ to $O(\log^2 T)$ candidates with an explicit scale-mismatch penalty. The theory and diagnostics together establish certified unknown-geometry adaptation and pinpoint selection as the principal practical frontier of the current construction.

papers.title: On a finite group in which every non-nilpotent maximal invariant subgroup of order divisible by $p$ is normal
papers.authors: Jiangtao Shi, Fanghua Li, Na Li
papers.abstract: Let $A$ and $G$ be finite groups such that $A$ acts coprimely on $G$ by automorphisms. For any fixed prime divisor $p$ of $|G|$, we prove that if every non-nilpotent maximal $A$-invariant subgroup of $G$ of order divisible by $p$ is normal then $G$ has a Sylow tower and $G$ is $q$-nilpotent or $q$-closed for each prime divisor $q$ of $|G|$.

papers.title: NP-Hardness of Generalized-Tur\'an Graph Modification Problems
papers.authors: Lior Gishboliner, Yevgeny Levanzov, Asaf Shapira
papers.abstract: For graphs $G, T$ and a graph-family $\mathcal{H}$, let $ex(G,T,\mathcal{H})$ denote the maximum possible number of copies of $T$ in an $\mathcal{H}$-free subgraph of $G$. Alon and Shikhelman conjectured that for every family of graphs $\mathcal{H}$ with $\chi(H) > s$ for every $H \in \mathcal{H}$, it is NP-hard to compute $ex(G,K_s,\mathcal{H})$, and even to approximate it up to additive error $n^{s-\delta}$ on $n$-vertex graphs, for any fixed $\delta > 0$. The case $s=2$ was established in a breakthrough result of Alon, Shapira and Sudakov. We prove the Alon-Shikhelman conjecture for finite families $\mathcal{H}$. In particular, we obtain an elementary proof of the Alon-Shapira-Sudakov result when $\mathcal{H}$ is finite.

papers.title: Non-Uniqueness of Weak Solutions to the Unforced Two-Dimensional Euler Equations with Vorticity in $L^1\cap L^p$, Part I: A Compactness Criterion and the Linear Analysis
papers.abstract: This paper and its companion Part II prove that the incompressible Euler equations in the plane, without external force, admit two distinct renormalized weak solutions with the same initial vorticity $f$, where $f$ is radial and nonnegative and lies in $(L^1\cap L^q)(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every $q<\infty$ but is not bounded. One solution is radially symmetric and stationary. The other is $3$-fold rotationally symmetric, is equimeasurable with $f$ at every time, and departs from $f$ in finite time; the two solutions are distinct in $L^\infty_t(L^1\cap L^q)_x$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^2$ for every $q\in(4/3,\infty)$ and every sufficiently large $T$. In this first part we prove two ingredients. One is a compactness criterion: for a radial datum, a sequence of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric solutions with converging data, whose non-radial moment is bounded below at some bounded time, has a subsequence converging to a second distinct renormalized weak solution. The other is the linear analysis for the building blocks of our multiscale datum. We show that the linearization of the Euler equations around the basic building block plus a small point vortex has an unstable eigenvalue in a space of $3$-fold rotationally symmetric perturbations. This latter argument depends on rigorous interval arithmetic that we discuss more fully in Part II.

papers.title: On the Open Problem in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition
papers.abstract: We prove that, for $n \in \mathbb{Z}^+$ not a perfect square, the only pairs of positive integers $\{a, b\}$ for which there exists $r \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $r^a + \sqrt{n}$ and $r^b + \sqrt{n}$ are both rational numbers are those of the form $\{a, a\}$ or $\{g, 2g\}$ (with $g$ odd). This resolves an open question presented in the 2023 Simon Marais Mathematics Competition.

papers.title: Aleshin graphs are expanders
papers.abstract: We prove that the Aleshin level graphs are two-sided expanders. We establish linear diameter bounds for Belaterra and Aleshin graph families. At level $n$, the diameters of the Bellaterra and undirected Aleshin graphs are a $|V_n|=2^n$. This improves the quadratic diameter bounds of Malyshev and Pak to the correct order of growth. For the Aleshin graphs we obtain a normalized spectral gap of at least $1-2\sqrt2/3$ and an edge-expansion constant of at least $3-2\sqrt2$, thereby establishing a Malyshev--Pak's Conjecture with explicit constants. An exact calculation at level ten also proves that the undirected Aleshin graphs are not Ramanujan for any $n\geq10$.

papers.title: Two-Timescale Antenna Positioning for Pinching-Antenna System Based on Statistical Channel Information
papers.authors: Jingze Ding, Zijian Zhou, Bingli Jiao, Rui Zhang
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a two-timescale antenna position optimization framework for the pinching-antenna system (PASS). The proposed framework exploits statistical channel state information (CSI) to determine large-timescale pinching-antenna (PA) positions over the entire waveguide, and utilizes instantaneous CSI to refine PA positions at the small timescale within a local region. This approach effectively captures the benefits of large-timescale PA positioning for long-term system performance and small-timescale PA movement for real-time adaptation to fast channel fluctuations. For the single-user case, we derive closed-form solutions for the optimal large-timescale PA positions, and further analyze a performance upper bound together with the conditions for achieving this bound, which guide the small-timescale position refinement. For the multi-user case, an upper bound on the minimum rate among all users is derived. To maximize their minimum rate, we develop an element-wise search algorithm for large-timescale PA positioning and a projected gradient ascent method for small-timescale position refinement. Simulation results show that the proposed scheme closely approaches the derived bounds and consistently outperforms conventional schemes by reducing path loss via large-timescale PA positioning and suppressing inter-user interference through small-timescale local movement.

papers.title: Affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequalities and optimal star bodies
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish an affine fractional Orlicz--Sobolev inequality by replacing the Euclidean fractional Orlicz seminorm with an energy obtained by minimizing over origin-symmetric star bodies of prescribed volume. Under finite lower and upper power growth assumptions, a subcritical upper growth bound, and a monotonicity condition on $t^{n/s+2}\Phi''(t)$, the resulting inequality has the same best constant as its Euclidean counterpart. The power case recovers the affine fractional Sobolev inequality of Haddad and Ludwig with the corresponding Luxemburg normalization. To establish this inequality, we investigate the underlying geometric extremal problem. For every nonzero smooth function of compact support, the existence and uniqueness of an optimal star body are proved under the growth assumptions alone, and its radial function is characterized by an equation involving $\Phi(t)+(s/n)t\Phi'(t)$. We also establish an anisotropic rearrangement inequality, together with its equality conditions under additional strictness assumptions. Moreover, the normalized local limit is investigated. The optimized energies converge to the local energy, and the radial functions of the minimizing bodies converge uniformly on the sphere. The limiting modular is determined by $\overline\Phi(t)=\int_0^t\Phi(\tau)\,d\tau/\tau$. Finally, we compare optimization over star bodies with optimization in the affine orbit.

papers.title: Learned smoothing in operator-adapted multigrid: controlled accuracy gains and computational limits
papers.abstract:
Learned multigrid components are often evaluated at a fixed iteration budget, but such comparisons do not distinguish local approximation gains from practical solver efficiency. We study this distinction for high-contrast elliptic problems on unstructured finite element meshes. A learned V-cycle uses operator-dependent transfers, Galerkin coarse operators, near-kernel deflation and an energy-norm safeguard; only its smoothers are trained. The architecture represents a specified class of fixed polynomial smoothers and is positively homogeneous in the load. On fresh conductive-channel problems, one learned pass reduces the energy error by factors of 5.7-6.1 relative to the same cycle with four-step Jacobi-preconditioned conjugate-gradient smoothing; the corresponding factors are 1.38-1.45 for insulating barriers.
  In a separate fixed-input test on channel problems, the fine-level learned smoother attains a smaller energy-norm error than the exact minimum over a five-dimensional Krylov space of its own input on 97-100 of 100 fresh inputs for each position and training initialization; this does not establish superiority over all polynomial-smoothed cycles. When the classical smoothing budget is increased, the paired geometric-mean accuracy crosses that of the learned cycle between 8 and 14 steps per smoothing call on channels and between 5 and 8 on barriers. The measured CPU implementation offers no computational advantage over the tested classical solvers, and load changes and floating islands further restrict its accuracy.

papers.title: The Laplace transform of the stationary measure of the open KPZ equation in the shock region
papers.abstract: The stationary increment measure of the open Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded interval can be represented as the independent sum of a Brownian motion and another process defined via an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative with respect to the measure induced by a Brownian motion. In the fan region, its finite-dimensional Laplace transform was previously expressed in terms of the continuous dual Hahn process. The main contribution here consists of computing the finite-dimensional Laplace transform for a range of parameters in the shock region by an analytic continuation argument. As an application, we provide a direct proof of the convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the increment height function of open WASEP under the stationary measure in the shock region, by computing the convergence of finite-dimensional Laplace transform without relating to the open KPZ equation.

papers.title: On Arithmetic-Progression Biases in Random Partitions: Limiting Laws and the Li-Zhao Conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $\cR=\{r+jm:j\geq0\}$ and $\cS=\{s+jm:j\geq0\}$ be disjoint arithmetic progressions of positive integers, and choose a partition of $n$ uniformly at random. We determine the limiting probability that the number of parts in $\cR$ is larger than the number of parts in $\cS$. More precisely, if $a=r/m$ and $b=s/m$, then this probability converges to $I_{1/2}(a,b)$, the regularized incomplete beta function. We prove the stronger distributional statement that, after multiplication by the partition saddle-point parameter, the difference of the two numbers of parts converges to $m^{-1}(\log G_b-\log G_a)$, where $G_a$ and $G_b$ are independent gamma variables. The proof uses the Boltzmann conditioning device for random partitions, a $q$-gamma evaluation of the unconditioned characteristic function, and a uniform Fourier estimate showing that conditioning on the total size does not change the limit. We also evaluate the finite-truncation limit studied by Li and Zhao. The two evaluations coincide, proving their conjecture on the commutation of the truncation and large-size limits.

papers.title: Whole-space eventual log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation
papers.abstract: We study eventual strict log-concavity and level-set geometry for the multidimensional Fisher-KPP equation with nontrivial, nonnegative, smooth compactly supported initial data, without assuming radial symmetry or convexity of the initial superlevel sets. Our main result is that there exist $T>1$ and $c>0$ such that $D_x^2\log u(t,x)\le -(c/t)e^{-\beta_*t}\mathrm{Id}$ for all $t\ge T$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^N$, where $\beta_*=2(\sqrt2-1)$. Consequently, after a single waiting time, $u(t,\cdot)$ has exactly one critical point, a nondegenerate global maximizer, and every level set $\{u(t,\cdot)=\lambda\}$ with $0<\lambda<\max_x u(t,x)$ is a smooth closed strictly convex hypersurface with positive principal curvatures. For levels in any fixed closed interval $K\subset(0,1)$, the level sets are radial graphs $\rho=R_\lambda(t,\omega)$, with every principal curvature bounded below by $(1-C\log t/t)/(2t)$ for all sufficiently large $t$. Unlike log-concavity, ordinary concavity exhibits a threshold determined by the inflection level of the critical travelling wave: for each fixed level above it, $u$ is eventually strictly concave on its superlevel set, whereas below it concavity eventually fails. Our proof proceeds by establishing estimates in four overlapping spatial regions. In the fixed-front region, we combine a one-sided estimate for second angular derivatives with radial and mixed derivative bounds to obtain curvature control without differentiating the Lipschitz directional phase. In the remaining regions, absorptive comparison in the invaded interior, leading-edge barriers and blow-up arguments through the diffusive scale, and Gaussian amplitude estimates combined with parabolic regularity in the exterior yield the required logarithmic-Hessian bounds.

papers.title: Aspects of quadratic Chabauty via modular forms
papers.abstract: We develop algorithms to construct a basis of de Rham cohomology for modular curves and a matrix representing the Hodge filtration required in the quadratic Chabauty method. We do this without requiring an explicit plane model of the curve and instead compute these objects in terms of modular forms. Our approach works for any modular curve; to demonstrate its efficiency, we implement our method for nonsplit Cartan modular curves.

papers.title: Hidden Convexity of the Joint Range of Three Quadratic Forms and Applications
papers.authors: Tuan Ngoc Hoang, Huy Quang Nguyen
papers.abstract:
We investigate a hidden convexity phenomenon for triples of homogeneous
  quadratic forms. We give a complete characterization of the convexity of
  the upper image obtained by adding the nonnegative orthant to their joint
  range. More precisely, the upper image is convex if and only if either a
  nonzero nonnegative linear combination of the three associated matrices is
  positive semidefinite, or the three quadratic forms admit a common strict
  negative direction. In particular, the upper image is convex whenever one
  of the three quadratic forms is convex. As applications, we establish the
  convexity of an associated value function and derive a generalized S-lemma
  for implications involving two quadratic inequalities and a strict theorem
  of the alternative for quadratic systems.

papers.title: A flat geodesic with a periodic asymptote
papers.abstract: We construct a closed surface of genus $2$ with nonpositive Gaussian curvature and a complete nonperiodic flat geodesic asymptotic to a flat closed geodesic. The metric is of class $C^{3,1/3}$ and its curvature is of class $C^{1,1/3}$, but not $C^2$. Thus the periodic-asymptote obstruction for smooth surfaces does not extend to $C^1$ Gaussian curvature.

papers.title: Finite-Query Coherent Projection of Black-Box Conditional Predictions
papers.authors: Yuyang Wu, Fanyu Zhou, Jinfeng Zhou, Guangying Lyu
papers.abstract: Local conditional predictions from a black box need not admit a common joint distribution. We study two aspects of their coherent projection: finite-access precision and directional fidelity. For arbitrary deterministic binary conditional tables, we establish matching expected minimax excess conditional-Kullback--Leibler risk $\Theta(\min\{R\sqrt{d/B},d^2/B\})$ under independent uniform exact-table queries, with repeated draws charged, for a local bounded pairwise joint class. The result holds for sufficiently large $d$, $R\sqrt d\le M_0$, and $Cd^3\le B\le(d2^{d-1})^{1/3}$, where $M_0$ is fixed. A moment estimator attains the upper bound. The main technical contribution is a matching lower-bound construction that respects shared pairwise interactions and frozen exact-table responses, with comparison to the best projection of the same realized table. We then examine directional fidelity in a computable hard-marginal formulation that preserves direct black-box marginals. A preregistered TabPFN-v2 case study combines a Car anchor with a frozen two-dataset, three-split extension. All $1{,}152$ extension optimization instances pass independent numerical checks at registered tolerances. Directional contrasts are dataset-dependent and asymmetric: optimizing one direction need not improve the other. Together, the analyses distinguish accurate approximation of a selected projection from improvement in conditional directions outside its fitted objective.

papers.title: Complete Determination of the Gallai--van der Waerden Number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\)
papers.abstract:
This paper completely determines the Gallai--van der Waerden number \(\mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)\) for all integers \(r\ge 3\):
  \[
  \mathrm{GW}(3;3,3)=\mathrm{GW}(4;3,3)=9,\qquad
  \mathrm{GW}(r;3,3)=r\quad (r\ge 5).
  \]

papers.title: Fuglede's conjecture holds in $\mathbb{F}_{p}^{d}$ for $p=2,\,d=8$ and $p=11,\,d=3$
papers.abstract: Fuglede's conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_p^d$ says that a nonempty set tiles by translation if and only if it is spectral. We prove the conjecture in $\mathbb{F}_2^8$ and $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$. Over $\mathbb{F}_2$ we show more generally that the Fourier support of a nonconstant indicator of density different from one half contains a plane. Consequently every spectral set of density one quarter has a subspace tiling complement. This supplies one of the dimension-eight reductions left by Kadowaki; the others are completed using classified Hadamard matrices and perfect binary codes. In $\mathbb{F}_2^9$ we prove that every tile is spectral and that every spectral set has power-of-two cardinality. All spectral cardinalities except $64$ are shown to tile, and we give further reductions of the remaining case. We also construct a spectral set of density one eighth whose Fourier support contains no three-dimensional subspace. For $\mathbb{F}_{11}^3$ we extend the geometric method of Fallon, Mayeli, and Villano by using moment identities, polynomial plane profiles, weighted incidence counts, and exact finite computations. The computations and their verification programs are described in the appendices.

papers.title: Generalized MLS and LS-SVR for Allen-Cahn Equations on Spheres
papers.authors: Vahid Mohammadi, Mehdi Dehghan, Stefano De Marchi
papers.abstract: This work extends least-squares support vector regression (LS-SVR) based on the generalized moving least squares (GMLS) approximation to the numerical solution of partial differential equations on spheres. We show that the proposed approach constructs a kernel-based approximant in its dual form and establishes its connection with the associated reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Furthermore, solving the PDE through the proposed LS-SVR framework is shown to be equivalent to solving a smoothing problem or a kernel ridge regression problem in the corresponding RKHS. As applications, the method is employed to solve the Allen-Cahn equation and its conservative counterpart on spheres. An implicit first-order operator-splitting scheme is used to separate each model into linear and nonlinear subproblems. The linear subproblem is discretized by the backward differentiation formula and approximated at each time step using LS-SVR derived from a GMLS-based collocation formulation, while the nonlinear part is treated analytically. The resulting scheme is shown to admit a unique numerical solution at every time step. For the conservative Allen-Cahn model, a correction procedure is incorporated to preserve mass. Numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed framework.

papers.title: Weighted odd-cycle transversals and fractional colorings of planar graphs
papers.authors: Xiaolan Hu, Jiaao Li, Zhouningxin Wang
papers.abstract:
We bound fractional chromatic numbers by establishing a connection with low-weight odd-cycle transversals. Let $\ell\geq 3$ be an integer and let $G$ be a graph of odd girth at least $\ell$ whose odd-cycle covering polyhedron is integral. For every nonnegative weight vector $w=(w_v)_{v\in V(G)}\in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{V(G)}$, we obtain a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ such that $G-Z$ is bipartite and $w(Z)\leq\frac{mad(G)}{2\ell}w(V(G))$. Here, $w(S)=\sum_{v\in S}w_v$ for any $S\subseteq V(G)$, and $mad(G)$ denotes the maximum average degree of $G$. Consequently, if $mad(G)<2\ell$, then $G$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{4\ell}{2\ell-mad(G)}$.
  As applications, we prove that, for every positive integer $k$, every $n$-vertex planar graph of girth at least $2k+3$ has fractional chromatic number at most $\frac{2k+1}{k}(1-\frac{1}{kn+1})$, establishing the girth version of Naserasr's fractional coloring conjecture with a strict inequality. For $k=1$, we furthermore prove that the upper bound $\frac{3n}{n+1}$ holds for every $n$-vertex triangle-free planar graph and this is attained for infinitely many values of $n$.

papers.title: On adjoint double shuffle relations and adjoint reduction relations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a positive answer to Jarossay's question under the adjoint reduction relations. Namely, we prove that the extended double shuffle relations together with the relation $\!\!\!\mod \pi^2$ are equivalent to the adjoint double shuffle relations together with the adjoint reduction relations.

papers.title: Probabilistic and game thresholds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a finite set and $\mathcal{F} \subseteq 2^X$ a non-trivial increasing property. We show that the bias-threshold $b(\mathcal{F})$ for the Picker-Chooser $\mathcal{F}$-game satisfies $b(\mathcal{F}) \ge \alpha / p_c(\mathcal{F})$, where $p_c(\mathcal{F})$ is the threshold for the property $\mathcal{F}$ and $\alpha > 0$ is an absolute constant. This proves that Picker-Chooser games satisfy one-sided ``probabilistic intuition''. The proof is based on the notion of influence from the theory of boolean functions.

papers.title: Stationary Half-space Geometric Last Passage Percolation without Random Shift
papers.abstract: We derive exact formulas for the diagonal distribution of half-space geometric last-passage percolation with a two-parameter family of stationary initial conditions throughout the phase diagram. Unlike previous results, our formulas remove the random shift at the origin. Under critical scaling, we obtain new formulas for the half-space stationary KPZ fixed-point distribution at $x=0$ in the high-density and maximal-current phases. In the low-density phase, we derive a new representation and show that it matches the corresponding formula from the stationary log-gamma polymer.

papers.title: On $C^2$ circle diffeomorphisms with rotation numbers of constant type
papers.abstract: For every irrational rotation number $\alpha$ of constant type and every $q>1$, we construct a $C^2$ circle diffeomorphism $F$ arbitrarily close to the rigid rotation $R_\alpha$ in the combined $C^2$ and $B^2_{2,q}$ topology whose normalized conjugacy is not Lipschitz. We also prove that $F''\in B^0_{2,1}$ implies global $C^1$ conjugacy. Thus the thresholds in the Besov summability and weak Dini scales are $q=1$ and $\gamma=1/2$, respectively. These results complement Herman's Baire category theorem on the residual existence of $C^2$ diffeomorphisms without $C^1$ conjugacy by providing quantitative counterexamples and sufficient conditions for differentiable conjugacy.

papers.title: Analytification and tropicalization via hyperfields and definable types
papers.authors: Pablo Cubides Kovacsics, Mariana Vicar\'ia, Jinhe Ye
papers.abstract: We study the analytification and tropicalization of algebraic varieties over valued fields via Jun's spaces of hyperfield points. Our main new objects are a family of power-tropical hyperfields $H_n$ and their inverse limit $H$, recording at each level the class of a leading term modulo $n$-th powers of the residue field. They yield an enhanced tropicalization of the associated space $X(H)$, strictly finer than the Berkovich one exactly when the multiplicative group of the residue field is non-divisible: it specialises to the Berkovich analytification when the residue field is algebraically closed, to the real analytification of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu when it is real closed, and to a new $p$-adic analytification when it is $p$-adically closed. Over henselian valued fields of equicharacteristic $0$ we then construct a model-theoretic avatar of $X(H)$: the space $\widehat{X}_T$ of definable types orthogonal to the value group, which sharpens the geometry in the spirit of Hrushovski and Loeser and recovers their space over algebraically closed valued fields. We show that $\widehat{X}_T$ is strictly pro-definable, satisfies a model-theoretic Payne theorem, and definable compactness in such spaces satisfies a Heine-Borel type characterization. As an application, we analytify $p$-adic semi-algebraic sets and prove a strong density theorem for their tropicalizations, the exact $p$-adic counterpart of the real one of Jell-Scheiderer-Yu.

papers.title: Weyl chambers, asymptotic expansions, and blowup analysis of explicit Toda solutions
papers.abstract: Blowup analysis is a central part of geometric analysis, and systems of PDEs such as Toda systems exhibit particularly rich blowup behavior. In [Nie25], the author constructed explicit families of radial Toda solutions whose blowup masses correspond to arbitrary elements of the Weyl group of the underlying Lie algebra. In this paper, we study these families within the framework of blowup analysis developed by C.-S. Lin and his coauthors. The key is an asymptotic analysis of the solution family that distinguishes Cartan elements in the interior of a Weyl chamber from those lying on its boundary faces. We prove a uniform upper bound for $u_i^{\lambda,H}(r)+2\log r$, so that the selection estimate holds with the center at the origin. We show that the successive bubbling scales for slow decay are determined by the intersections of the ray $H+tq_\mu$ with root hyperplanes. At each crossing, rescaling and the face asymptotics identify the limiting profiles as explicit solutions of the corresponding Levi-Toda subsystems. The masses of these successive bubbles, computed using [KLNW24], account for the entire blowup mass. Examples in type $A_2$ demonstrate this identification and exhibit both separated scalar bubbles and a simultaneous full-system bubble.

papers.title: Quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the quermassintegral inequalities for capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball in hyperbolic space. We construct a locally constrained nonlinear curvature flow that preserves the $k$-th quermassintegral while monotonically increasing the $l$-th quermassintegral for any $(1\leq l<k\leq n)$. Using this flow, we establish a full family of the quermassintegral inequalities for horo-convex capillary hypersurfaces in a horoball with contact angle $\theta\in(0,\pi/2]$. Moreover, we weaken the horo-convexity to convexity and obtain the quermassintegral inequalities for convex capillary hypersurfaces between the $n$-th and $l$-th quermassintegrals.

papers.title: Schatten limits for semi-commutators in Toeplitz quantization on Fock space
papers.abstract: We solve a problem posed by Hu and Virtanen by characterizing, for every $0<p<\infty$, the bounded symbols $f$ for which $T_f^{(t)}T_g^{(t)}-T_{fg}^{(t)}$ tends to zero in the unnormalized Schatten $p$-norm or quasi-norm as $t\to0^+$ for every fixed bounded $g$. The setting is weighted Fock spaces over $\mathbb C^n$ with weights whose real Hessians are uniformly positive and bounded. Only constants satisfy the limit when $p<2n$; at $p=2n$, it is equivalent to the weak real gradient belonging to $L^{2n}(\mathbb R^{2n})$. When $p>2n$, the limit is characterized by relative weak compactness in $L^1(\mathbb R^{2n})$ of normalized local mean oscillation densities. For $p\ge2$, uniform convergence over $\|g\|_\infty\le1$ is equivalent to vanishing density mass. A continuous compactly supported counterexample for $p>2n$ shows that bounded density mass and convergence for $g=\bar f$ do not imply convergence for every fixed bounded $g$. The symbol classes are weight-independent unital algebras, yielding limits for finite Toeplitz products and commutators; quantitative H\"older estimates also give finite-rank approximation bounds. The Gaussian case transfers to anti-Wick quantization by unitary equivalence. On compact K\"ahler manifolds with positive line bundles, we prove a H\"older sufficient condition, including the endpoint, for each fixed bounded second symbol. A projective-line example shows that trace norm convergence can fail for a smooth first symbol and a fixed bounded second symbol. The proofs combine local holomorphic approximation, Schatten and Sobolev estimates, singular integral methods, and the Dunford--Pettis criterion.

papers.title: Hasegawa-Mima equation as limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system
papers.authors: Federico Butori, Franco Flandoli, Yassine Tahraoui
papers.abstract: We prove that the Hasegawa-Mima equation (HME) is the limit of a magnetized pressureless Euler-Boltzmann system in a special scaling regime. The proof relies on the derivation of a uniform estimate independent of the scaling parameter, using the particular structure of the singular system and the identification of a combination of the unknowns that compensates for fast oscillations in time. We also show that HME allow us to investigate a conditional property of inverse energy cascade and drift waves.

papers.title: A Modified Direct Eigenvalue Swapping Algorithm with Guaranteed Stability
papers.abstract: For a given matrix \( A \) in the real Schur form, the eigenvalue swapping algorithm is used to swap two adjacent diagonal blocks. In LAPACK, this operation is performed by the subroutine~\texttt{SLAEXC}/\texttt{DLAEXC}, which is based on a direct swapping algorithm proposed by Bai and Demmel in 1993. In this work, we present a thorough error analysis of a modified direct swapping algorithm. By a carefully designed pivoted Givens QR factorization, this algorithm can achieve an error bound of the form \( O( \boldsymbol{u} \lVert A \rVert ) \) under mild assumptions, where \( \boldsymbol{u} \) is the unit roundoff. We present empirical evidence to illustrate the superior stability of our algorithm over existing approaches.

papers.title: OpenAI partially disproves Littlewood's 1961 $L^\alpha$-flat theorem
papers.abstract: We present a counterexample, produced by OpenAI, to Littlewood's 1961 theorem on $L^\alpha$-flat polynomials. The theorem asserts that no $L^\alpha$-flat polynomials exist within the class of trigonometric polynomials of the form$$\sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m \cos(m\theta+\alpha_m), \qquad n \in \mathbb{N}^*,$$satisfying$$k\, n^2 \sum_{m=1}^{n} a_m^2 \;\leq\; \sum_{m=1}^{n} m^2 a_m^2,$$where $k$ is an absolute constant (alternatively expressed on the right-hand side as $K = 1/k$). We show that OpenAI's counterexample is contained within the class of hyper-lacunary sequences. Consequently, it offers only a limited refutation, as such sequences fail to satisfy an implicit assumption of Littlewood's theorem. We also discuss broader questions surrounding this counterexample and provide a brief historical overview.

papers.title: When are metrizable linear subspaces of topological vector spaces finite-dimensional?
papers.authors: Vladislav V. Maksimov, Evgenii A. Reznichenko
papers.abstract: We study conditions that imply finite-dimensionality of metrizable or Frechet-Urysohn linear subspaces of topological vector spaces (TVS).
