The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_\gamma v,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_\gamma\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(\gamma/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group $G_\gamma\cong\mathrm{SO}(3)$ contains the automorphism group of $\mathcal A_\gamma$. For $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$ the groups $G_{\gamma_1}$ and $G_{\gamma_2}$ generate $\mathrm{SO}(V)\cong\mathrm{SO}(4)$. For the six ways of ordering and bracketing the product of $i,p,p$ in $\mathcal A_\gamma$, two map the unit circle in ${\rm span}\{j,k\}$ to a point and, for $\gamma>0$, four map it to ellipses.
  As an application, we derive a Hamiltonian model of a classical spin on $H_\gamma$ whose multiplication-induced quadratic energy is isotropic for $\gamma=0$ and anisotropic for $\gamma>0$. It conserves spin length and, for fixed $\gamma$, energy, and satisfies an exact work identity when $\gamma$ varies in time. Numerical experiments with periodically varying $\gamma$ indicate both regular and irregular spin dynamics.

papers.title: Effective Dual Subgradient Methods Through Sequential Subgradient-Aligned Rays
papers.authors: Hansi Abeynanda, Chathuranga Weeraddana, Carlo Fischione
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient subgradient-based framework, referred to as the sequential subgradient-aligned rays (SSAR) method, for improving the convergence performance of the dual subgradient method. In particular, the proposed method identifies and exploits a finite sequence of rays, when available, as the dual subgradient method evolves, along each of which a subgradient of the negative dual function remains constant and aligns with the ray. While the dual variable iterates remain on each identified ray, a constant stepsize associated with the ray is employed, with the associated constant stepsizes decreasing from one ray to the next. This approach yields constant decrements in the negative dual function values while the dual variable iterates remain on the associated rays, enabling the dual variable iterates to progress more quickly toward a dual optimal solution. We then show that the proposed SSAR method can be leveraged to improve the performance of the dual decomposition method for minimizing the average of local loss functions associated with multiple agents that share a common decision variable, a widely used problem formulation in many large-scale real-world applications. In particular, the SSAR method improves the convergence performance of the corresponding dual decomposition method while also reducing its communication cost. Numerical experiments on a least squares regression problem and a logistic regression problem using real datasets are conducted to evaluate the performance of the SSAR method.

papers.title: Conservative Finite Element Methods for Kirchhoff-Type Equations
papers.authors: Benjamin D\"orich, Felix Krumbiegel, Jemal Rogava, Andreas Rupp, Zurab Vashakidze
papers.abstract: We construct and analyse a fully discrete scheme for a Kirchhoff-type nonlinear integro-differential equation in two spatial dimensions with time-dependent coefficients. The scheme combines a symmetric three-layer time discretization of Crank--Nicolson type with a conforming finite element method of arbitrary polynomial degree $p$ and a Picard iteration for the nonlinearity. We prove that the Picard iteration is well defined and, that the iterates converge to the Ritz projection of the exact solution measured in fractional-power norms of the discrete Laplacian. Running the same energy argument in the unshifted norms, and under the same hypotheses, we then obtain the optimal order $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p+1} + \tau^2 )$ in $L^2$ and $\mathcal{O} ( h^{p} + \tau^2 )$ in $H^1$ for the full error. For the homogeneous problem with constant coefficients, the exact solution of the scheme moreover preserves a discrete energy identically. Numerical experiments with manufactured solutions reproduce the predicted second order in time and the full spatial order $h^{p+1}$ in the $L^2$-norm.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for the Entropic Central Limit Theorem in the Log-Concave Case
papers.abstract: Let $\mu$ be a log-concave isotropic probability measure on $R^d$ , and let $\mu^n$ denote the law of the normalized sum of $n$ independent random vectors with law $\mu$. We prove that \[ H(\mu^n|\gamma)\leq \frac{C}{n} \min\left\{1+\log(ed)^2H(\mu|\gamma)\ ,\ d\right\}. \] Compared to the previous best known bound, our estimate replaces the polynomial dependence on the dimension by a polylogarithmic one. The proof relies on a new combination of the De Bruijn identity with Eldan's stochastic localization process.

papers.title: Mixed-Precision Coalesced Matrix-Free Multigrid with Vertex-Patch Smoothing
papers.abstract: I present a geometric multigrid solver for the Poisson equation with continuous cubic elements in three dimensions, smoothed by a multiplicative vertex-patch Schwarz method with exact local solves. All fields are kept in persistent cell-wise storage, where every cell holds its own copy of each shared degree of freedom. The patch smoother yields a continuous solution without any exchange between cells. On the GPU, the patch update is computed in registers, one cell per thread, and the cells of a patch exchange data by warp shuffles, so shared memory is avoided almost entirely. Despite the low occupancy that this design implies, the arithmetic of the patch update runs close to the FP32 peak. Fast diagonalization, merged transforms, and a reflection symmetry of the patch then reduce the arithmetic until a sweep moves its data at $87\%$ of the bandwidth of a plain device copy. The hierarchy therefore runs in single precision inside a double-precision outer iteration. Rounding the unassembled residual destroys the cancellation between opposite-sign copies of shared degrees of freedom; exchanging the copies between cells in double precision performs this cancellation before rounding, without changing the dual vector they represent. With this \emph{rebalancing}, the cycle converges as in double precision and independently of the mesh size, the error converges at the optimal rate down to the precision of the solve, and the solver reaches over $400$ million degrees of freedom per second on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU.

papers.title: A semiampleness result for hyperk\"ahler fourfolds and smoothings of Lagrangian subvarieties
papers.authors: Andreas H\"oring, Vladimir Lazi\'c, Christian Lehn
papers.abstract: We give a geometric proof of the following statement: let $X$ be a smooth hyperk\"ahler fourfold such that the Picard group is generated by a line bundle $L$ that is nef, non-trivial, and not big. If the Kodaira dimension of $L$ is non-negative, some positive multiple defines a Lagrangian fibration. The proof requires a number of tools which are of independent interest, including an analogue of Voisin's unobstructedness result and a smoothing result for singular Lagrangian subvarieties.

papers.title: Water Transport on 3-Spiders: Unbounded Lengths of Shortest Optimal Strategies
papers.authors: Guanheng Chen, Ran Tao, Tianyi Tao
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. An averaging operation selects a nonempty connected vertex set and replaces the weights of its vertices by their arithmetic mean. For a nonnegative initial weight function $\omega:V(G)\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ and a target vertex $x$, let $t(G,x,\omega)$ denote the minimum number of averaging operations needed to attain the maximum reachable weight at $x$. Gollin et al.[1] proved, using the Axiom of Choice, that a finite optimal strategy exists for every finite graph, every nonnegative initial weight function and every target vertex; see Tao [2] for a simplified proof. We prove that the lengths of shortest optimal strategies on $3$-spiders have no uniform finite bound. In particular, these lengths cannot be bounded in terms of the maximum degree of the graph.

papers.title: Douglas-Rachford splitting method for nonconvex stochastic optimal control
papers.authors: Fran\c{c}ois Caffier (IFPEN, DISCO), Paul Malisani (DISCO), Laurent Pfeiffer (DISCO)
papers.abstract: Motivated by the numerical resolution of stochastic optimal control problems, particularly those involving nonlinear dynamics, we investigate the convergence properties of the Douglas-Rachford splitting algorithm in a nonconvex and infinite-dimensional setting. We introduce an extension of the method that applies when one component of the objective function is continuously differentiable with a locally Lipschitz gradient, while the other is weakly lower semicontinuous with a bounded domain.

papers.title: Functions determining $(q+3)/2$ directions over the finite field with $q$ elements
papers.abstract: Let $q=p^n$, where $p>2$ is prime. We prove that every $q$-set $U\subseteq\mathrm{AG}(2,q)$ determining exactly $(q+3)/2$ directions is affinely equivalent to the graph of $x^{(q+1)/2}$. For $n\ge2$, we also prove that a $q$-set determining at most $(q+p)/2$ directions is either an affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linear set or affinely equivalent to this graph. The classification for $n=1$ is due to Lov\'asz and Schrijver. For $n=2$, the classification and the stated stability result follow from results of G\'acs, Lov\'asz, and Sz\H onyi and the direction theorems of Blokhuis, Ball, Brouwer, Storme, and Sz\H onyi, completed by Ball. These direction theorems establish affine $\mathbb{F}_p$-linearity for functions with fewer than $(q+3)/2$ determined directions. Our proof uses R\'edei polynomials, results of G\'acs, Lov\'asz, and Sz\H onyi on their coefficients, and an earlier polynomial comparison lemma of the author.

papers.title: Liouville-type theorems and perturbation uniqueness for stationary incompressible MHD with directional fractional dissipation
papers.abstract: We study Liouville-type theorems for stationary solutions of the incompressible magnetohydrodynamics equations in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with directional fractional dissipation $(-\partial_i^2)^{\alpha}u$ and $(-\partial_j^2)^{\beta}b$, where $n\ge 2$ and $0<\alpha,\beta\le 1$. We prove that $u\equiv b\equiv 0$ by assuming that $u\in L^{p,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $b\in L^{q,\infty}(\mathbb{R}^n)$, with suitable conditions on $p$ and $q$. The proof uses a localized fractional energy identity and does not assume finiteness of the global homogeneous Sobolev energy. The method also applies to the case of full fractional dissipation. For the system with common-directional fractional dissipation, we prove stationary uniqueness for compactly supported perturbations of arbitrary smooth transverse shear backgrounds when $0<\alpha,\beta<1$. We also establish a quantitative uniqueness criterion for perturbations of backgrounds with bounded gradients that are not necessarily compactly supported, for all $0<\alpha,\beta\le 1$, assuming directional localization.

papers.title: Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona)
papers.abstract: We propose a new regression method named Direct Inference on Admissible Sets (Diona) that directly uses samples to estimate the state and its derivatives at a query point, along with their admissible bounds, without long global training. By casting the values and derivatives at the query and neighbouring samples as latent variables in a constrained optimisation problem, the burden of long training loops becomes one of on-demand local solves. We establish Diona's theoretical properties including finite-sample coverage and, in the noiseless case, convergence to the true state and derivatives under dense sampling. In a nonlinear regression benchmark on six functions of three to eight dimensions, Diona was more accurate than a Gaussian process (GP) on noiseless data especially with denser data sets. Furthermore, as with GP, it produced uncertainty bounds that contained the true value at more than 95% of query points in four functions. Diona's time to a first prediction after a data set update was three to four orders of magnitude shorter than that of the GP, and two to three orders shorter than that of a neural network, which was more accurate but offers no uncertainty quantification. This low latency is paid for by on-demand predictions, so this latency advantage applies when relatively few predictions are needed between data updates.

papers.title: Positive sectional curvature on exotic spheres in infinitely many dimensions
papers.abstract: We show that there exist exotic spheres with metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature in infinitely many dimensions: in every dimension $n\equiv3\pmod4$ with $n\geq11$ and $n\not\equiv255\pmod{256}$. Previously, every known closed simply connected manifold of positive sectional curvature in a dimension above $24$ was diffeomorphic to a compact rank-one symmetric space. The spheres we consider are certain homotopy spheres arising as quotients of special $S^3$-$S^3$ bundles introduced by Speran\c{c}a. These homotopy spheres are determined by an orthogonal representation $\rho$ of $S^3$ and an $S^3$-conjugation-equivariant map $\beta$, and are denoted $\Sigma_{\rho,\beta}$. By recent constructions, such spheres admit Riemannian metrics of strictly positive sectional curvature. In this paper we consider the spheres $\Sigma_{\rho_b,\beta}$ of dimension $4b+3$, $b\geq2$, where $\rho_b$ is the representation of $S^3$ on $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathbb{H}^b$ by left multiplication on the second summand. For these spheres, we show that the Eells-Kuiper invariant is the product of an integer $k(\beta)$ depending only on $\beta$ and a rational number $r_b$ given by one coefficient of a power series built from the $\hat A$- and $L$-genera. We then show that, for every $b\geq2$ with $b\not\equiv63\pmod{64}$, there is a map $\beta$ for which the Eells-Kuiper invariant does not vanish, and thus the corresponding sphere is exotic. A computer calculation also gives the dimensions $n\equiv255\pmod{256}$ below $2^{16}$.

papers.title: Polytopal substitutions and conformal dimension
papers.abstract: We introduce polytopal substitutions, a recursive procedure for constructing polyhedral approximations of self-similar topological spaces. For a class of substitutions called sub-hyperbolic, we show that the limit of these approximations is naturally homeomorphic to the limit space of the associated iterated monodromy group. We establish a relationship between the $\ell^p$-contraction coefficients of sub-hyperbolic substitutions and the conformal dimension of their limit spaces. In particular, we characterize the conformal dimension in terms of asymptotic moduli and relate these moduli to $p$-energies of graphs.

papers.title: The Cheng-Murray Conjecture on Deep Holes of Full-Length Reed-Solomon Codes
papers.abstract: For full-length Reed--Solomon codes, every received word whose interpolation polynomial has degree equal to the code dimension is a deep hole. The Cheng--Murray conjecture asserts that these are the only deep holes in dimensions $3\le k\le q-2$, except when $q$ is even and $k=q-3$. Earlier results settled the conjecture over odd prime fields and in the high-dimensional range. We resolve the remaining cases $3\le k\le\lfloor q/2\rfloor$ over every finite field $\F_q$, thereby completing the classification in all nonexceptional dimensions. Our proof combines two complementary approaches. The tangent envelope of a marked arc yields differential constraints that settle the even-characteristic range $3\le k\le q/2$ and the odd-characteristic range $3\le k\le q/3$. In the remaining odd-characteristic range, local syndrome compatibility and combinatorial counting rule out additional deep holes.

papers.title: A spectral multiplier theorem for fractional Hardy operators
papers.abstract: We consider the fractional Laplacian with added critical or subcritical Hardy potential, called Hardy operator. We prove a H\"ormander spectral multiplier theorem, i.e., the boundedness of sufficiently smooth multipliers of these Hardy operators on Lebesgue spaces. The range of admissible Lebesgue exponents is optimal, but the smoothness assumption is probably not. The proof combines the Helffer--Sj\"ostrand formula with a quantitative Jaffard lemma for operator-valued matrices.

papers.title: Triple Quantum Schubert Calculus
papers.abstract: We prove a triple quantum Pieri formula: the product of a quantum double Schubert polynomial $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)$ by a quantum factorial elementary polynomial $\widetilde{E}_{p,k}(x;z)$ in a second set of variables $z$ is a sum over chains in the quantum Bruhat graph, indexed by a quantum analogue of Sottile's relation, whose coefficients are monomials in the quantum parameters times polynomials in the differences $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and which is Graham-positive at $z=y$. At $y=z=0$ it is the quantum Pieri rule of Ciocan-Fontanine and Postnikov; at $z=y$ it is an equivariant quantum Pieri rule for the complete flag variety, indexed by chains in the quantum Bruhat graph rather than, as in the rule of Huang and Li, by the data of a reduction to classical cohomology, and proved directly. A doubled Pieri formula, positive in the same senses, treats multiplication by the quantization of a product of two elementary polynomials in the same variables, which is not the product of the quantizations: it is two iterated Pieri steps with the incompatible pairs of chains omitted. More generally, the triple quantum Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^{w,d}(y;z)$, the coefficients of $\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_u(x;y)\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_v(x;z)$ in the basis $\{\widetilde{\mathfrak{S}}_w(x;y)\}$, are polynomials in the $y_i-z_j$ with nonnegative integer coefficients; the proof of this appears as an appendix. We extend the Peterson-Woodward comparison formula and the quantum-to-classical reduction of Leung-Li and Huang-Li to the triple constants, and we describe and prove correct the algorithms of schubmult, which compute products of arbitrary quantum double Schubert polynomials well beyond the reach of previous methods.

papers.title: Short curves in homogeneous spaces of the unitary group for unitarily invariant norms
papers.abstract: Let A be a unital *-subalgebra of $M_n(C)$ and let $M = U(n)/U(A)$, with the quotient Finsler metric induced by a unitarily invariant norm on $u(n)$, normalized so that $||iP|| = 1$ for rank-one projections $P$. This family contains the unitary orbits of Hermitian matrices, in particular flag manifolds and Grassmann manifolds. We prove that if $z_0$ is a minimal lifting of a tangent vector $X$ with $||X||_{\infty} < \pi/2$, then the one-parameter group $t \mapsto e^{t z_0}\cdot o$ has minimal length among all piecewise smooth curves in $M$ joining its endpoints. The same holds in manifolds $N=SU(n)/(SU(n) \cap A)$ for every Ad-invariant Finsler norm on $su(n)$, not necessarily symmetric (i.e. the unit sphere does not need to be balanced). The proof relies on the convexity of the distance from the identity along geodesic segments, valid for all these norms. We also prove that the ball of radius $\pi/2$ around the identity, for the spectral norm, is convex along one-parameter segments. This extends known results for the p-Schatten norms with p even, and gives a new proof for the operator norm, where the result is due to Duran, Mata-Lorenzo and Recht.

papers.title: A sharpened $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate for even initial data
papers.abstract: It is well known that $u_0 \in L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ is an extremizer for the $L^8_t L^4_x$-Strichartz estimate if and only if it is a Gaussian. We show that every extremizing sequence of even functions $\{ u_n \} \subset L^2(\mathbb{R}) \setminus \{0\}$ approaches a centered Gaussian in an appropriate sense. This result follows from a certain inequality for coordinate-wise even $L^2$ functions on $\mathbb{R}^4$ conjectured by Gon\c{c}alves (2019) which we prove in this paper with the optimal constant.

papers.title: Convex Bernstein limits and sharp recovery on expanding intervals
papers.abstract: We determine when approximation by convex polynomials on expanding intervals converges to best approximation on the real line by convex entire functions of exponential type at most $\sigma>0$. For intervals of radius $(n-\gamma_n)/\sigma$, where $0\le\gamma_n<n$ and $\gamma_n=o(n)$, one margin sequence gives this limit for every convex function of polynomial growth if and only if $\gamma_n/[n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3}]\to\infty$. When this condition fails, a fixed uniformly strictly convex entire function has approximation errors with unbounded limsup. We apply the limit theorem to prove existence of the convex Bernstein constant for $|x|^\lambda$ for every $\lambda\ge1$, and identify it with an attained entire-function minimum. We also give a sufficient margin for growth bounded by $\exp(a|x|^\alpha)$, $0<\alpha<1$. For arbitrary subexponential growth on the real line, each target with finite entire-function error admits a suitable margin, whereas no single margin is sufficient for the whole class. Further results concern attainment, right continuity with respect to the exponential type, weighted growth conditions, and the endpoints of fixed-fraction approximation intervals.

papers.title: Searching for the power rangers
papers.abstract:
We develop a method for studying centralizers of generic elements in some large Polish groups. We identify a condition which enables us to show that the range of each power map is comeager; a strengthening of this condition allows us to prove that a generic element embeds in a flow (a continuous, one-parameter subgroup).
  This approach enables us to answer the question that motivated this work : we prove that a generic isometry of the Urysohn space (or the Urysohn sphere) embeds in a flow. We also obtain information on the centralizer of a generic isometry; we show that it contains an infinite-dimensional torus and that torsion elements are dense in it. To illustrate the flexibility of our method, we apply it to two other Polish groups. The first is the group of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we recover results of King and of de la Rue and de Sam Lazaro. Finally we apply our technique to the group of nonsingular automorphisms of a standard probability space, and we deduce that a generic nonsingular automorphism embeds in a flow, answering a question of Danilenko and Silva.

papers.title: Bulk stability of bimolecular stochastic chemical reaction networks
papers.abstract: We establish criteria for stability in the bulk of planar stochastic chemical reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. Using Poincar\'e compactification, we characterize the asymptotic drift and show how stochastic fluctuations can prevent escape along transversally repulsive branches of the limiting deterministic flow. We construct a Lyapunov function by combining local estimates near these branches with dissipative estimates in the neighboring regions. The criteria cover a wide class of networks and in particular apply beyond weakly reversible and strongly endotactic networks. Together with compatible boundary estimates, these criteria imply positive recurrence.

papers.title: Lipschitz clustering in normed spaces and barycentric spaces
papers.abstract: For every normed space $X$ and integers $1\le k<n$, we construct a Lipschitz retraction from $X(n)$ onto $X(k)$ with constant at most $2+8n(n-1)$, independently of the dimension of $X$. Here $X(n)$ consists of the nonempty subsets of $X$ with at most $n$ points, equipped with the Hausdorff metric. For the consecutive case $k=n-1$, a separate construction gives the sharper asymptotic bound $O(n\log n)$. These results extend to barycentric metric spaces and settle some open problems on Lipschitz retractions.

papers.title: The generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most sixteen lines is combinatorial
papers.abstract:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in $\mathbb{P}^2_\mathbb{C}$ and let $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ be its bundle of logarithmic vector fields. On a general line, $\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle$ splits as $\mathcal{O}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}(k+1-d)$ with $k=\min\{\mathrm{mdr}(\mathcal{A}),\lfloor rac{d-1}{2}floor\}$, where $\mathrm{mdr}$ is the minimal degree of a Jacobian syzygy. We prove that $k$ is determined by the intersection lattice whenever $d\le16$, answering in this range a question of Cook, Harbourne, Migliore and Nagel. Since freeness can be read off from $k$ and $c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)$, this strengthens Terao's freeness conjecture in this range; in particular we obtain a proof of Terao's conjecture for $14$ lines that uses it only for $13$ lines. For any number $d$ of lines, it follows that $\mathrm{mdr}$ is determined by the lattice whenever $\mathrm{mdr}\le6$ and $2\mathrm{mdr}\le d-3$, and that Terao's conjecture holds for every free arrangement whose smaller exponent is at most $7$.
  The proof reduces the question to critical arrangements: $2s+3$ lines, each containing at most $s+1$ intersection points, with $\mathrm{mdr}=s$. For these, the inflection polynomial of the minimal derivation factors as $Q_\mathcal{A} R$ with $R\in H^0(\mathcal{I}_Z^2(s-3))$, where $Z$ is the zero scheme of the derivation, of length $
u=c_2(\mathcal{T}\langle\mathcal{A}angle)-s(s+2)$. For $s\le5$ this forces $
u\le1$, and Chern class arguments then reduce everything to Terao's conjecture for $13$ lines. For $s=6$ we show $
u\le3$, using a Riccati equation along multiple components of $R$, Ziegler's multirestriction, and local computations verified by computer algebra; an exhaustive enumeration of the 26,265,318 candidate lattices with $
u\in\{2,3\}$ that satisfy Bojanowski's inequality completes the proof.

papers.title: The domination number of the 2-token graph of the complete bipartite graph
papers.authors: E. Acosta Troncoso, I. Caldera Caldera, L. M. Rivera
papers.abstract: For a graph $G$, the $2$-token graph $F_2(G)$ has as vertices all $2$-subsets of $V(G)$, with two such subsets adjacent whenever their symmetric difference is an edge of $G$. In this paper, we determine the domination number of the $2$-token graph of the complete bipartite graph $K_{m,n}$, for all integers $2\le m\le n$. We show that it equals $\lceil m/2\rceil+n-1$, except when $m=3$, or when $m\ge5$ is odd and $n=m+1$; in these two exceptional situations it is one less. Our arguments rely on an explicit characterization of the dominating sets of the $2$-token graph of $K_{m,n}$.

papers.title: Failure of noncommutative Rota's theorem with $L\log L$ endpoint
papers.authors: Hiranmoy Ghorui, Suman Mondal, Samya Kumar Ray
papers.abstract: We construct a factorizable Markov map $T$ on a hyperfinite finite von Neumann algebra and a positive element $x\in L\log L$ for which the sequence $T^n(T^*)^n x$ does not converge bilaterally almost uniformly. This answers a question of Anantharaman-Delaroche \cite{AD2006}.

papers.title: Boltzmann Equation and Hard Sphere Gas with Singular Initial Data: Well-posedness, Kinetic Limit, and Weak Stability
papers.abstract: We develop a local well-posedness theory for the spatially inhomogeneous 3-d Boltzmann equation with hard sphere cross-section, accommodating a class of large initial data. This class is an interpolation between the space $L_{x}^{\infty}L_v^{1}$ and $L_{v}^1L_{x}^{\infty}$ (with weight in $v$). It is notable for including data that can have infinite $L_{x,v}^\infty$-norm, entropy density. The core idea of the proof is a homogenization method based on collision geometries. As a key application, we prove the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with initial data in this space, having certain extra conditions. This is the first proof on the kinetic limit of hard sphere gases with singular initial data. We also derive weak stability estimates of Boltzmann equation and hard sphere gas within the same functional spaces.

papers.title: Some minimal characteristics and flat trajectories of a system in the N-body problem
papers.abstract: For the classical model of a system of N particles with interaction (the N-body problem) we consider some spatial problems of nonlinear programming for finding conditional minima and local extrema for the main characteristics of the system on its phase space. We prove that these conditional minima and local extrema of the system characteristics can only be achieved on flat, in general, not necessarily finite, trajectories of the system in space, (under the condition that the system angular momentum is non-zero). And then we find the basic conditions limiting the values of the integrals of motion: angular momentum and total energy of the system under which these trajectories are flat finite ("circular" or elliptical) trajectories on which the flat structure of the system is preserved in time under the certain restrictions on the values of the system's integrals of motion. And we determine also the values of the system's key characteristics on these flat trajectories. Next, in the Appendix, we consider some additional related results for a more general model of the system.

papers.title: A Sharp Gradient Harnack Estimate for the Lane--Emden System
papers.authors: Sanghoon Lee, Kui Li, Juncheng Wei
papers.abstract: We establish a sharp pointwise gradient estimate for positive entire classical solutions of the Lane--Emden system when one of the exponents lies below the Serrin exponent $n/(n-2)$. The estimate generalizes the positivity of the scalar curvature of the associated conformal metric in the biharmonic case $q=1$. The coefficient in the estimate is optimal on the critical hyperbola.

papers.title: Conway's thrackle conjecture: a new upper bound of $\frac43n$
papers.abstract: A thrackle is a drawing of a graph in the plane in which every pair of edges meets exactly once, either at a common endpoint or at a proper crossing. Conway conjectured that every thrackle has at most as many edges as vertices. We prove that every thrackle on $n\ge4$ vertices has at most $\left\lfloor4(n-1)/3\right\rfloor$ edges. The proof combines Pammer's computer-assisted verification of the conjecture for graphs on at most twelve vertices with a discharging argument in suitable plane and projective-plane embeddings.

papers.title: Upper tail large deviations of regular subgraph counts in sparse random regular graphs
papers.abstract:
For a $\Delta$-regular connected graph $H$ we obtain the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices, in the regime $np^{\Delta/2} \gg (\log n)^{1/(v_H-2)}$ and $p \ll 1$, where $p:=d/n$ and $v_H$ is the number of vertices, and also identify the typical structure of $\mathbb{G}_n^d$ conditioned on this upper tail event. For $\Delta \geq 3$, the speed and the rate function are same with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In contrast, for $\Delta=2$ (i.e.~in case of cycles), due to the degree constraint in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, although speed remains the same the rate function turns out to be different. Moreover, conditioned on the upper tail event of cycle counts in $\mathbb{G}_n^d$, we show that the random graph contains a disjoint collection of clique and biclique like structures with probability approaching to one, a stark contrast compared to the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting.
  In the complementary regime, i.e.~for $1 \ll n^{v_H}p^{e_H} \ll (\log n)^{\alpha^*_H/(\alpha^*_H-1)}$, where $e_H$ is the number of edges in $H$, $\alpha^*_H$ is the fractional independence number of $H$, and $H$ is a strictly balanced graph (and thus including the regular case), we show that the upper tail large deviations speed and rate function for the number of copies of $H$ match with those in the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi setting. In this regime, we further show that almost all of the unlabeled copies of $H$ conditioned on the upper tail event are edge disjoint.

papers.title: Sharp fractional Hardy--Maz'ya remainders on half-spaces: angular reduction and energy stability
papers.abstract:
For $d\geq2$, $0<s<1$, $p>1$, and $\tau>0$, we study the sharp half-space remainder \[
  [u]_{s,p,+}^p-\mathcal D_{d,s,p}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+}x_d^{-sp}|u|^p\,dx
  \geq\Lambda_{d,s,p,\tau}\int_{\mathbb R^d_+}
  \frac{x_d^{\tau-sp}|u|^p}{(x_{d-1}^2+x_d^2)^{\tau/2}}\,dx. \] We first obtain exact dimensional and angular reductions by an $L^p$ contraction. For $p=2$, we identify the planar sharp coefficient with the simple first eigenvalue of a singular angular operator with compact resolvent. We prove a ground-state representation and a two-sided estimate for the sharp deficit. These give quantitative stability and a Fourier--Mellin energy criterion for extremizing sequences in all dimensions. For the distance with multiplier $h(\xi)=\min\{\xi^2,1\}$, the best planar stability coefficient is not attained and is strictly smaller than the quadratic dispersion coefficient. The minimizing frequencies are nonzero when $\tau=2$ and $s$ is close to one. Finally, we prove normalized local limits for the sharp quadratic constant, each fixed fiber eigenvalue, and the dispersion coefficient.

papers.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
papers.abstract: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.

papers.title: SympFormer: Inertial Attention Blocks from Damped Hamiltonian Dynamics on Spaces of Probability Measures
papers.authors: Viktor Stein, Levin Maier, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl
papers.abstract: The attention mechanism underpins modern large language models, yet their dynamics remain only partially understood. Recent perspectives interpret attention blocks as interacting particle systems, whose mean-field limits correspond to gradient flows of energy functionals on spaces of probability densities on $\mathbb R^d$ equipped with Wasserstein-type metrics. We extend this viewpoint by deriving accelerated attention blocks from inertial, Nesterov-type damped Hamiltonian dynamics on these density spaces, developing the geometry and differential calculus needed to make the construction rigorous. In particular, we introduce a local-mobility geometry for the Otto-Wasserstein and softmax-Wasserstein settings, and a quotient Stein geometry that resolves the degeneracy of the linear-attention kernel to yield a well-defined metric and differential calculus. We provide rigorous foundations when softmax attention admits a gradient-flow formulation and when its inertial counterpart admits a damped Hamiltonian on explicitly characterized domains. For linear attention, we obtain a finite-dimensional solution theory with sharp conditions for global existence versus finite-time second-moment blow-up. We further prove a quantitative link between continuous moment blow-up and the discrete-layer depth at which token norms cross a prescribed threshold. Finally, motivated by the finite-token geometry, we propose geometric corrections to token and momentum updates. In decoder-only, nanoGPT-style experiments on TinyStories and OpenWebText, these corrections lower validation negative log-likelihood on next-token prediction relative to momentum-only controls.

papers.title: Groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers are complete co-analytic
papers.abstract: In this paper, we prove that the set of groups satisfying the minimal condition on centralizers is a complete co-analytic subset of the Polish space of countable groups. This answers a question of Wesolek and Williams.

papers.title: Triple parabolic cosets have unique Bruhat minima
papers.abstract: A folklore result says that any parabolic double coset $W_{I} w W_{J}$ in a Coxeter group $W$ is an interval of the Bruhat order, provided that $W_{I}$ and $W_{J}$ are finite. We include a self-contained proof, without assuming that $W$ is finite. Furthermore, we prove that each "triple coset" $W_{I} u W_{J} v W_{K}$ has a Bruhat minimum and -- if $W_{I}, W_{J}, W_{K}$ are finite -- a Bruhat maximum, but (in general) is not a Bruhat interval. This proves and extends a conjecture on MathOverflow #472072.

papers.title: Is Spectral Self-Supervised Learning a Minimax Optimal Method of Density Ratio Estimation?
papers.abstract: Spectral self-supervised learning is a method of density ratio estimation for the setting in which only samples drawn from the joint density of the numerator are available. The method has extensively been studied in terms of the computational properties, such as optimal solutions and connections to representation learning. However, theoretical understanding of its statistical property is still insufficient. In this work, we study three questions, namely, the minimax optimality, the applicability of the theory to regularized algorithms, and the statistical merits of density ratio estimation with data augmentation mechanisms that have recently been considered in the context of self-supervised representation learning. We first show that for general classes of H\"{o}lder continuous density ratios, there are regularized spectral self-supervised learning algorithms that yield estimators attaining the minimax optimality, up to logarithmic factors. We then prove that for subclasses endowed with a data augmentation mechanism, we obtain faster convergence rates that are also minimax optimal (up to logarithmic factors) in a weaker sense. We also present the key proof ideas tailored for self-supervised density ratio estimation.

papers.title: Hydrodynamic and Stochastic Limits of Space-Time Hawkes Processes
papers.authors: Fuqing Gao, Yingli Wang, Lingjiong Zhu
papers.abstract: We study the large-scale behavior of critical and nearly critical space-time Hawkes processes initialized by a prescribed Poisson field of past events. The density of this initial field separates three macroscopic regimes. In the high-density regime, fluctuations average out and the event measure converges to a hydrodynamic limit which is a deterministic diffusion profile. At the fluctuation threshold, random branching remains visible and produces a measure-valued stochastic limit. Below the threshold, the rescaled event measure vanishes locally even though its mean generally remains nontrivial, with rare large clusters accounting for the surviving mean. For reproduction delays with finite mean, the critical limits are described by heat flow and the occupation measure of a branching diffusion. A nearly critical perturbation introduces linear decay without changing the three-regime structure. Heavy-tailed delays lead to a different balance between time and space: the mean follows a fractional diffusion law, the stochastic limit is a superprocess occupation measure on time-space, characterized by a nonlinear fractional equation, and the past persists as a temporal memory term. We also determine how the scaling of the Poisson past must be matched to the observation scales and show that, in one spatial dimension, a shorter observation window recovers stochastic behavior hidden in the sparse regime. The results allow bounded initial profiles with possibly infinite total mass and describe the limits directly at the level of locally finite event measures.

papers.title: Quantum K-structure constants and cylindric Grothendieck polynomials for Grassmannians
papers.authors: Vassily Gorbounov, Christian Korff, Leonardo C. Mihalcea
papers.abstract: We use the partition functions of a five-vertex exactly solvable lattice model from statistical mechanics to give new combinatorial formulae for the Schubert structure constants of torus-equivariant quantum K-theory rings of Grassmannians. The proofs build on our earlier results where we identified the transfer matrices of these lattice models geometrically as multiplications by the Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$ classes of the tautological subbundle and the (dual) quotient bundle. The structure constants are solutions of a system of linear equations with coefficients given by the partition function. This system may be solved explicitly by specializing the Hirzebruch parameter $y$ to an equivariant parameter, leading to explicit formulae using Cramer's rule. Furthermore, we give an alternative combinatorial construction of the partition functions in terms of sums over cylindric set-valued tableaux, which we call cylindric Grothendieck polynomials. The latter generalise McNamara's factorial skew Grothendieck and Yeliussizov's modified Grothendieck polynomials and can be thought of as an equivariant K-theoretic version of Postnikov's toric Schur function. We also provide new polynomial representatives for equivariant K-theory classes of Richardson varieties and their variants.

papers.title: The Critical 2D KPZ Process
papers.authors: Quentin Berger, Francesco Caravenna, Jeremy Clark, Alexander Dunlap, Yu Gu, Ziyang Liu, Shuta Nakajima, Rongfeng Sun, Li-Cheng Tsai, Zuodi Xie, Nikos Zygouras
papers.abstract:
This work constructs a non-trivial solution to the ill-defined two-dimensional Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) equation at criticality: a distribution-valued stochastic process on the plane, which we call the Critical 2D KPZ Process. It arises as the limit in law of centred log partition functions of two-dimensional Gaussian directed polymers at criticality, viewed as discretised KPZ solutions. It is also a measurable function of the Critical 2D Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF) via a renormalised Cole-Hopf transformation, obtained as the limit of the centred logarithm of the spatially mollified SHF as the smoothing is removed. The Critical 2D KPZ process is non-Gaussian and its covariance displays a log-log blow-up near the diagonal. Gaussian fluctuations emerge when averaging on shrinking spatial scales.
  The results presented here were obtained through extensive interactions with generative AI (ChatGPT 5.5, 5.6 and 6); see Appendix C for more details. The proof builds on key recent and older advances in our field, combined in novel ways with substantial AI input. We view this manuscript as a "community project" that represents more than a decade's collective effort. We have worked on making the presentation as accessible as possible, highlighting the main ideas and their relations to the literature.

papers.title: Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors and local transfer in families
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a quasi-split $p$-adic group, defined over a non-archimedean local field of residue cardinality $q$, and $R$ be a $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{q}^{-1},\mu_{4p^\infty}]$-algebra. We generalize the constructions of Shahidi local coefficients and Langlands-Shahidi gamma factors to the setting of co-Whittaker $R$-representations. For classical $p$-adic groups, we prove there is a unique integral morphism of endomorphism rings of Gelfand--Graev representations, interpolating the (standard) local generic transfer to a general linear group. This yields a local transfer morphism in families, which allows us to deduce properties of the local $\ell$-adic generic transfer and congruences modulo primes $\ell\neq p$.

papers.title: The Asymptotic Number of Anticodes in Hamming Spaces
papers.abstract:
In the Hamming space $\mathbb{F}_q^n$, a $d$-anticode is a subset in which every pair of points has Hamming distance at most $d$, or equivalently, a set of diameter at most $d$. Let $m_q(n,d)$ denote the maximum size of a $d$-anticode and let $\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)$ be the family of all $d$-anticodes. We show that for fixed $q$, as $n\to\infty$, the total number of $d$-anticodes satisfies \[ |\mathcal{A}_q(n,d)|=2^{(1+o(1))m_q(n,d)} \] for $4\le d\le n-1$, except when $q=2$ and $d=n-1$.
  We also count linear $d$-anticodes, that is, subspaces of $\mathbb F_q^n$ with diameter at most $d$. For fixed $q$ and $d$, their number is polynomial in $n$. For growing $d$, we determine the exponential order as $q^{\Theta_q(d^2+d\log_q(n/d))}$ in the sublinear regime and $q^{\Theta(n^2)}$ when $d/n\to\alpha\in(0,1)$. In the near-full regime $n-d=o(n)$, we obtain the sharper count $q^{(1/4+o(1))n^2}$. A random-generator construction further improves the binary lower bound for every fixed linear diameter.

papers.title: Leafrians, Poisson structures, and Frobenius splittings on moduli spaces
papers.abstract: The Poisson $T$-Pfaffians of Bott--Samelson varieties, $G/U$, and $G/B$ produce Frobenius splittings, but only by a local, coordinate-bound argument. We isolate the local mechanism: a weighted trace pairing on the deformation space of a fat point, whose top coefficient factors over the blocks. At the members of a presentation, polyvector fields on the base $X$ transfer to the moduli space $M$. Applied to a Poisson bivector, this produces a Poisson bivector, extending Bottacin's structure from surfaces to arbitrary dimension. Applied to a top degree polyvector $s$ and wedged with a transverse Euler frame, it produces an anticanonical section on $M$, which we call the \emph{leafrian}. When $X$ is a Poisson surface, we prove that the leafrian splits the moduli of stable sheaves, of principal $G$-bundles, and of instantons if and only if $s$ Frobenius-splits the base. The mechanism itself is dimension-free. The construction also recovers and generalizes the splittings of the Lie-theoretic examples: the $r$-matrix need not satisfy the classical Yang--Baxter equation.

papers.title: Almost simple subgroups of the space Cremona group
papers.abstract: We prove that every finite almost simple subgroup that is not simple of the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space is isomorphic to one of the following: $\mathfrak{S}_5$, $\mathfrak{S}_6$, $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ or $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$. We also prove that the group of birational automorphisms of the three-dimensional complex projective space contains unique (up to conjugation) subgroups isomorphic to $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_7)$ and $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_9)$.

papers.title: Non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation
papers.abstract: We prove non-uniqueness for the forced one-dimensional Vlasov-Poisson equation on the whole space. More precisely, for every finite $p$, we construct a nonnegative ion density, smooth for positive times, and a source $S\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with $S(0)=0$, for which there exist two distinct nonnegative distributional solutions $f_\pm\in C([0,1];L^1(\R^2))$ with the same zero initial datum and with spatial densities bounded in $L^p(\R)$ uniformly in time. The result is sharp in terms of the integrability of the spatial densities: our solutions have Lipschitz electric fields, and we show that in this class uniqueness holds as soon as the spatial density is bounded.

papers.title: Nonvanishing of 2-primary Kolyvagin classes via simultaneous quadratic twists
papers.abstract: Let $E/\mathbf{Q}$ be an elliptic curve, let $K=\mathbf{Q}(\sqrt{D})$ satisfy the Heegner hypothesis with $D<-4$, and fix a modular parametrization $\varphi$ with $\varphi(\infty)=O$. Under surjectivity modulo $2^L$, with $L\ge 2$, and a cohomological exclusion condition at level $4$, we construct a finite set of primes $T$ such that, writing $d_T=\prod_{q\in T}(-q)$ and $n_T=\prod_{q\in T}q$, the $2$-Selmer dimensions of $E^{d_T}$ and $E^{d_TD}$ are $0$ and $1$. The support size is bounded in terms of the initial Selmer dimensions, independently of $L$. Inspired by the work of Tian and Tian--Yuan--Zhang on congruent numbers, we construct a point $Q_T$ on the terminal twist and identify its Kummer class with the standard mod-$2$ Kolyvagin class. Using the low-corank $2$-converse and the $2$-primary Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer formula, we prove that its index $m_T$ in the full Mordell--Weil lattice satisfies $v_2(m_T)=v_2(c_\varphi)+\mathfrak{i}(E,K)$. The optimal Manin constant theorem supplies a $2$-indivisible parametrization $\varphi_0$, for which $\kappa^{\mathrm{std}}_{n_T,1}(\varphi_0)\ne 0$ if and only if $\mathfrak{i}(E,K)=0$. When the intrinsic index vanishes, the minimum terminal support size is $R=\min\{d_2(E),d_2(E^D)\}$, and the normalized standard classes have order $2^M$ for $1\le M\le L$. Full $2$-adic Galois image then gives strong nonvanishing.

papers.title: Quantitative constructive representation of the KdV flow in $H^3$ via $L^2$-energy-preserving centered-difference Chernoff approximations and Picard iteration
papers.abstract: We give a constructive representation of the solution of the KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6uu_x$ on $\mathbb R$ for real initial data in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. The approximations couple an exact, unitary centered-difference Chernoff product for the Airy group with a skew-symmetric discretization of the quadratic term, and are computed by Picard iteration; they preserve the $L^2$ norm exactly, as does the limit. A two-mesh Cauchy argument shows that the whole sequence converges in $C([0,T];H^2)$, at rate $O(n^{-\frac{2(s-2)}5})$ for $H^s$ data ($3\leq s\leq 7$), and in $L^2$ at rate $O(n^{-6/5})$ for $H^3$ data. This scheme, to the best of our knowledge, is novel and is of independent interest. As a by-product we obtain existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, Lipschitz dependence on the data in the $H^2$ norm, uniformly on bounded subsets of $H^3$ and compact time intervals, and joint locally Lipschitz dependence of $(t,f)\mapsto S(t)f$ into $L^2$; the classical conservation laws extend the flow globally in time.

papers.title: Lenses make many points: Pure point spectrum disproves Simon's $L^2$ conjecture
papers.abstract: For every $d\ge2$ and $0\le\sigma<1/3$, we construct with LLM-assistance a smooth bounded nonnegative lens-type potential $V$ with arbitrarily small $\|V\|_\infty+\int_{\mathbb{R}^d}|x|^{1-d+\sigma}|V(x)|^2 dx$, such that $-\Delta+V$ has only pure point spectrum in $(0,\infty)$. Thus, we show that Barry Simon's $L^2$ conjecture, Problem 8 in "Schr\"odinger operators in the twenty-first century", is false.

papers.title: On the direct SLE-martingale approach to the integrability of Conformal Loop Ensembles
papers.abstract: This paper is about the derivation of "integrability results" (i.e., for example, explicit formulas for the probability of events involving a few marked points) for Conformal Loop Ensembles, that are the (conjectured) scaling limits of discrete crititical planar lattice models from Statistical Physics. We discuss the explicit solutions to the PDEs provided by the original SLE/CLE martingale approach that AI now makes it possible to uncover. This provides short and direct new proofs of a number of formulas that have recently been derived based on Liouville quantum gravity, conformal field theory or Coulomb gas methods, and also makes it possible to derive some new ones. We briefly illustrate this with the examples of the backbone exponent and annulus crossing probabilities for critical percolation, but this direct approach seems to apply to a wide class of observables of two-dimensional systems related to conformal field theories.

papers.title: On the Concordance Invariants of Cable Links
papers.abstract: We study the Beliakova--Wehrli link $s$-invariant and Cavallo's link $\tau$-invariant of coherently oriented cables. For knots satisfying extremal four-ball genus and maximal self-linking hypotheses, we establish bounds for the $s$-invariant of $(p,q)$-cables, where $p$ and $q$ are not necessarily coprime, and show that these bounds are sharp under certain conditions. For the $\tau$-invariant, we prove analogous bounds for arbitrary companion knots and exact formulas whenever $\tau(K)=\pm g_4(K)\ne 0$. Specializing to the coherently oriented cable links associated to an $n$-framed knot, we apply these bounds to the lasagna $s$-invariant of Ren and Willis. The resulting applications provide upper bounds for the lasagna $s$-invariant of knot traces and a criterion for distinguishing homeomorphic zero traces up to orientation-preserving diffeomorphism.

papers.title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
papers.authors: Jian-Rong Li, Michael Oren Perlstein, Ran J. Tessler
papers.abstract: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.

papers.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
papers.authors: Xin He, Huan Lao, Xiliang Lu, Shijun Zhang
papers.abstract: Constructing accurate and computationally tractable approximation spaces is a fundamental task in scientific computing. Partially trainable neural networks bridge fixed random features and fully adaptive representations. This paper quantifies a phase transition pattern in approximation bounds and observes analogous behavior in training errors: a rapid but smooth initial improvement followed by diminishing returns, with a sharper transition under greater initialization mismatch. Under polynomial spectral decay with exponent $\alpha>1$ and leverage compatibility, we establish a squared $L_2$ approximation rate $\mathcal{O}((\kappa_P\log(m/\delta)/m)^\alpha)$ for two-layer networks of width $m$ and trainable proportion $P$, where $\kappa_P=(P/\kappa_1^*+(1-P)/\kappa_0^*)^{-1}$. The bound holds uniformly over the unit ball of a reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) with probability at least $1-\delta$. The constants $\kappa_0^*$ and $\kappa_1^*$ quantify the fixed and trainable groups' sampling mismatches relative to the target RKHS. For spherical biased-ReLU features in dimension $d$, we verify these assumptions with $\alpha=(d+2)/(d-1)$ and $\kappa_0^*=4\sqrt{2}\tau(d+1)/d$ for initialization scale $\tau\ge1$, and $\kappa_1^*=1$ under ridge leverage sampling. For $d=5$ and $\tau=10$, a trainable proportion of approximately $4.1\%$ captures $90\%$ of the reduction in the approximation bound from $P=0$ to $P=1$. A structured three-layer example illustrates how a few trainable first-layer neurons exploit fixed downstream blocks through nonlinear composition. Numerical experiments across diverse settings, including networks with up to 15 layers, exhibit similar phase transitions in training errors.

papers.title: Collapsed translating solitons with planar wings
papers.authors: Eddygledson Souza Gama, Francisco Mart\'in, Niels Martin M{\o}ller
papers.abstract:
We study complete embedded translating solitons in R^3 with finite genus and finite entropy. We prove that such collapsed translators whose wings are all of planar type (in a weak topological sense) must be vertical flat planes.
  In particular, this implies the non-existence result for gluing and doubling constructions involving planes that was conjectured in (14) and announced in (9) as an application of the authors' techniques, under weaker assumptions than previous rigidity results by Khan and Lynch-Tinaglia in (17,19,20).
  A key ingredient is a sharp new a priori decay estimate in the exterior problem for the horizontal graphical translator equation, showing that bounded solutions to the nonlinear equation, and their gradients, are controlled by multiples of the Green's function of the linear drift Laplacian, regardless of the size of the given L^\infty data. Combined with a graphical description of the infinite ends and the Neves-Tian flux identity, this yields the main rigidity result.
  As another application, we obtain a full classification of collapsed embedded finite-genus translators of entropy lambda < 3.

papers.title: Mutual transformations of arbitrary ternary qubit trees by Clifford gates
papers.abstract: It is shown that ternary qubit trees with the same number of nodes can be transformed by the naturally defined sequence of Clifford gates into each other or into standard representation as one-dimensional chain corresponding to Jordan-Wigner transform.

papers.title: Robust Power and Sample Size Calculations in Quasi-likelihood Models: Methods and Practice
papers.authors: Shijie Yuan, Amy Cochran, Paul Rathouz
papers.abstract: Accurate power and sample size (PSS) calculations are essential for designing studies that use quasi-likelihood (QL) models, which extend generalized linear models (GLMs) to settings where the full distribution of the outcome is not specified. Traditional PSS approaches often rely on restrictive distributional assumptions, limiting their applicability when responses have non-standard distributions, variance functions are misspecified, or when predictors exhibit complex dependence structures. Building on recent advances in effect size measures for PSS - specifically, 2 Standard Deviations in the Linear Predictor (2SLiP) and Pseudo-Partial $R^2$ (P2R2) - developed with interpretability in mind, this paper extends and evaluates these effect size measures in the QL framework, keying in particular on their utility in PSS. We assess their empirical performance for the Wald test and then extend to the score test through extensive simulations across diverse outcome types, link functions, and variance structures. To illustrate practical utility, we applied these effect size measures to survey data on frontline health care workers from \citet{cahill2022occupational} to quantify the association between perceived personal protective equipment adequacy and mental health outcomes during the COVID-19 pandemic, adjusting for covariates. Our findings demonstrate that both 2SLiP and P2R2 provide robust and interpretable alternatives to traditional methods, maintaining accuracy with minimal distributional assumptions and enhancing the flexibility of PSS for realistic study designs.

papers.title: Learning SOCP Solver Dynamics with Graph Neural Networks
papers.authors: Adam Ghalem, Lou Sala\"un, Davide Rinaldi, Fragkiskos D. Malliaros
papers.abstract: Second-order cone programs (SOCPs) are a fundamental class of convex optimization problems widely applied across engineering domains. Classical interior-point methods are robust and accurate, but their iterative nature can be costly in real-time or repeated-solve settings. This has motivated learning-based solvers that approximate optimizer solutions with neural networks. Recent work has increasingly studied graph neural networks (GNNs) for linear, quadratic, and second-order cone optimization, leveraging their ability to model sparse relational structure among variables, constraints, and objective functions. Most existing GNN-based solvers compress the optimization process into a single forward pass, predicting the optimizer directly without using the intermediate trajectory produced by classical solvers. We introduce SOCPNet, a recursive GNN framework that uses solver trajectories to learn an iterative SOCP solution procedure. A shared GNN model is applied repeatedly, refining the current iterate at each step and enabling inference for a variable number of iterations. Rather than predicting the solution in a single pass, SOCPNet learns from intermediate iterates to progressively refine its estimates using a trajectory-regularized training procedure. We evaluate SOCPNet on multiple datasets spanning standard SOCP problem classes and show that it consistently reduces the final solution error relative to a SOCP-GNN baseline. Finally, we demonstrate how trained SOCPNet models can be used in a hybrid optimization pipeline by warm-starting a classical interior-point solver, reducing solver iterations without loss of accuracy.

papers.title: Geometric chains of orbifolds with corners and singular homology
papers.abstract: We study a geometric homology theory (GHT for short). Its chains are generated by smooth maps from compact oriented orbifolds with corners to a smooth space, and two kinds of chains are set to zero: those admitting an orientation reversing automorphism, and degenerate ones, which, together with their boundaries, factor through smooth maps to orbifolds of lower dimension. Bisecting the source of a geometric chain along a hypersurface transverse to its corners changes the chain only by the boundary of an explicit prism and by prisms over its faces; cutting a geometric cycle along a regular level set of a smooth function on the target does not change its homology class. Geometric chains also behave well under products and pullbacks along fibre bundles, which overcomes some of the combinatorial rigidity of singular chains. We prove that geometric homology is naturally isomorphic to singular homology with rational coefficients for every smooth space admitting a good cover, such as smooth manifolds, orbifolds and locally finite polyhedra, and also for orbifolds with corners. The proof uses cutting operators along level sets of functions on the target, realized by explicit prisms, instead of triangulations. For continuous maps into arbitrary spaces we conjecture the same statement, and prove it for Euclidean neighbourhood retracts in degrees at most one, with surjectivity in degree two. Without the relation killing degenerate chains the comparison fails for orbifold chains: the weighted projective plane $\mathbb{P}(1,1,p)$, $p\ge5$ prime, mapped to a point is a cycle that does not bound. Applications on Morse theory and the BV structure on geometric chains of moduli spaces of bordered Riemann surfaces, following Costello and Harrelson--Voronov--Z\'u\~niga, are given.

papers.title: Moduli spaces of logarithmic connections associated with difference Painlev\'e equations of type $E^{(1)}_n$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we provide an explicit correspondence between moduli spaces of parabolic logarithmic connections on the projective line with spectral type $(2^2,1^4,1^4)$ and $(3^2, 2^3, 1^6)$, and the spaces of initial conditions for difference Painlev\'e equations with symmetry of type $E^{(1)}_7$ and $E^{(1)}_8$, respectively. Furthermore, we realize the extended affine Weyl group symmetries of the space of initial conditions in terms of connections.

papers.title: Differentially Private Synthetic Data via Generalized Moment Matching
papers.authors: Rundong Ding, Yiyun He, Yizhe Zhu
papers.abstract: We study $(\varepsilon,\delta)$-differentially private synthetic data for arbitrary databases of $n$ records in $[-1,1]^d$ under a specified integral probability metric (IPM). We introduce generalized moment matching, which estimates moments privately, fits a probability measure, and samples synthetic records. A general error theorem applies when moment error controls the target IPM. This framework extends Chebyshev moment matching for $1$-Wasserstein distance and smooth queries. We apply the framework to maximum mean discrepancy with Matern and Laplace kernels and a two-layer ReLU neural tangent kernel.We also obtain guarantees for sliced Wasserstein-$1$ and the IPM induced by norm-bounded ReLU networks. With sufficiently many synthetic records,these rates are minimax optimal up to logarithmic factors for fixed dimension.

papers.title: Bridge change-of-measure for propagator estimation of diffusions
papers.abstract: The propagator of one-dimensional diffusions has relevant applications in statistical inference and across many disciplines. Yet it is obtained in closed form only for very few simple models. Here we analyze an importance sampling strategy based on a bridge change of measure to estimate propagators: paths are generated under an auxiliary diffusion whose bridge between the two fixed boundary points is easy to generate, and the target propagator is recovered through a Radon-Nikodym derivative or likelihood ratio correction derived from Girsanov's theorem. This method overcomes the main limitations of the crude Monte Carlo estimator, which relies on binning in state space, introducing bias and becoming inefficient with rare transitions. We apply the method to a range of benchmark processes and show that the bridge-based estimator matches the accuracy of crude Monte Carlo with orders of magnitude fewer sample paths. Finally, we elaborate on discretization schemes for the Radon-Nikodym derivative and on approximations to the best-in-class change of measure, both of which increase the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: Defect flows from functional relations in the asymptotic semiring
papers.authors: Federico Ambrosino, Anatoly Konechny, Ingo Runkel, G\'erard M. T. Watts
papers.abstract: We study perturbations of topological defects by a relevant holomorphic defect field in two-dimensional conformal field theory. This produces translation invariant defects and these necessarily flow to topological defects in the infrared. Translation invariant defects form a monoidal category which extends the fusion category of topological defects. We argue that the renormalisation group flow defines a semiring homomorphism from the semiring of translation invariant defects to an "asymptotic semiring" which we construct from topological defects. The semiring homomorphism preserves functional relations, and we illustrate in the example of Virasoro minimal models that the resulting relations in the asymptotic semiring constrain the defect flow endpoints. The companion paper [1] contains a detailed study of such defect flows in several minimal models, both numerically and analytically.

papers.title: 3D de Sitter from complex Virasoro TQFT: Observers and knots
papers.authors: Jeevan Chandra, Diego Liska, Boris Post
papers.abstract: The Euclidean saddles of 3D Einstein gravity with positive cosmological constant are spherical three-manifolds. When one adds a heavy observer, the backreacted saddles are spherical cone manifolds, with a conical singularity along the observer worldline. We propose exact gravitational partition functions at fixed topology on a class of spherical cone manifolds that undergo hyperbolic-to-spherical transitions as the cone angles increase. Our construction relies on a careful analytic continuation of the product of two Virasoro TQFT partition functions. We test the proposal by showing that the exact partition functions exponentiate in the semiclassical limit to the spherical volume, in agreement with the gravitational on-shell action. This leads to a spherical volume conjecture for the product of continued Virasoro TQFT amplitudes. As further evidence, we relate the theta and tetrahedron graph amplitudes to the two-point function and out-of-time-ordered four-point function of operators on a massive observer's worldline. In appropriate limits, we recover the static patch scalar two-point function with finite observer backreaction and the semiclassical effects of observer recoil. In addition, we analyze examples with knotted worldlines and reproduce their spherical volumes. We also apply our prescription to Seifert manifolds, which are off-shell in AdS$_3$ gravity but admit dS$_3$ saddles, and find agreement with their spherical volumes semiclassically. Finally, using Dehn surgery on torus knots and links, we obtain partition functions on smooth spherical three-manifolds.

papers.title: Quantum field theory and four-manifolds: Perspectives from physics and geometry
papers.authors: Niklas Garner, Martijn Kool, Jan Manschot, Yuuji Tanaka
papers.abstract: These lecture notes are based on lecture series by the authors for the Summer School 2025 on ``Physical mathematics of quantum field theory" at the University of Massachusetts Amherst organized by Owen Gwilliam, Chris Elliott, and Matteo Lotito. The lectures centred around algebraic structures arising from twists of supersymmetric quantum field theories, correlation functions of topologically twisted supersymmetric gauge theories, and their mathematical counterparts as intersection-theoretic invariants associated to moduli spaces of instantons, semistable sheaves, or Higgs sheaves on four-manifolds or complex projective surfaces.

papers.title: Dynamic Active Fleet Sizing of Heterogeneous UAV Relays for Post-Disaster Communication Networks
papers.abstract: Uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems are increasingly used to provide temporary connectivity when ground communication infrastructure is damaged by disasters such as hurricanes and wildfires. However, the amount of aerial support required changes as ground networks recover and communication demand evolves. We focus on dynamically adjusting the number and allocation of actively deployed UAVs within a fixed available fleet. We develop a model predictive control (MPC) framework for dynamic fleet sizing of heterogeneous UAV relays during post-disaster communication recovery. The framework accounts for communication demand, ground network recovery, heterogeneous UAV operation, UAV energy availability, and backhaul capacity, which limits how much relayed traffic can be transmitted to the external communication network. The resulting formulation is a convex quadratic program that supports efficient online fleet sizing and deployment decisions. We evaluate the framework using seven historical disaster recovery case studies based on Federal Communications Commission reports, together with four backhaul scenarios and sensitivity analyses. Results show that required active UAV fleet size varies considerably throughout recovery, while backhaul capacity and fleet composition affect communication performance, highlighting the value of adapting active fleet size over time.

papers.title: Polynomial pathwidth for graphs vertex-coverable by few shortest paths and algorithms for quasi-shortest path covers
papers.authors: Li-Hsuan Chen, Florent Foucaud, Ling-Ju Hung, Ralf Klasing, Lucas Lorieau, Peter Rossmanith
papers.abstract:
We study how covering a graph by a small number of shortest or approximately shortest paths/walks constrains its treewidth and pathwidth. A path or walk is $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest for $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$ if each contiguous segment has length at most $\alpha$ times the distance between its endpoints plus $\beta$.
  For graphs vertex-covered by $k$ shortest paths, we establish the first known polynomial pathwidth bound of $O(k^3)$. For edge-coverage, we improve the previously known $O(k^4)$ upper bound to $O(k^2\log k)$. As a main ingredient of the proofs, we first show that if the vertices of a graph can be covered by $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks, then its treewidth is $O_{\alpha,\beta}(k^2)$; this is a consequence of the fact that such graphs have linear metric growth and the technique developed in [Campbell et al., E-JC 2023]. To obtain the above pathwidth upper bounds, we combine this result with techniques from the literature in a nontrivial way.
  On the other hand, we show that there exist connected bipartite cubic graph whose edges can be covered by $k$ shortest paths and whose pathwidth is $\Omega(k\log k)$, providing the first superlinear lower bound. For graphs covered by $k=2$ $(\alpha,0)$-quasi-shortest paths with $\alpha>1$, we show that, unlike treewidth and unlike the case $\alpha=1$ and $\beta=0$ of exact shortest paths, the pathwidth may be unbounded.
  Finally, for every fixed rationals $\alpha\geq1$ and $\beta\geq 0$, we give XP algorithms with a running time of $n^{f(k,\alpha,\beta)}$ for some function~$f$ that decide whether the vertices of a graph can be covered by at most $k$ $(\alpha,\beta)$-quasi-shortest paths or walks. The algorithms combine our treewidth upper bounds with an algorithmic meta-theorem from [Dreier et al., LICS 2025].
  [abstract shortened to meet the arXiv requirements]

papers.title: Normal Matrix Model and Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We present a two-matrix model with a normal matrix with eigenvalues confined to contours in the upper half plane coupled to a Hermitian matrix. This generalizes the matrix model proposed by Jens Hoppe which corresponds to a single horizontal line. We solve the saddle point equations for several lines and show that the large-N free energy can be expressed in terms of hyperelliptic integrals. We show that the model describes a Coulomb gas in the presence of an infinite conducting boundary.

papers.title: Optimal Multitask Representations Under a Rate Constraint: An Information Bottleneck Analysis
papers.abstract: Which pretraining objective yields the best representation for downstream tasks under an information budget? We formalize this problem as a multitask information bottleneck, using a mutual information constraint to model incomplete information retention. For Gaussian inputs and tasks, we characterize optimal representations and show that a weakly task-aligned specialist can outperform a reconstruction generalist at low rates but lose at high rates. We also construct task families for which every fixed Gaussian prediction objective incurs arbitrarily large relative regret, driven by reversals in optimal allocation priorities. Conversely, the average task information matrix defines an objective with a uniform relative-regret bound controlled by maximum task SNR. CelebA and dSprites experiments illustrate that compression can change which pretraining objective performs best, and even task-aware training can reverse which downstream task is better preserved as rate increases.

papers.title: LLM2Cert: LLM Synthesis of Certificates with SMT/Lean Verification
papers.authors: Zhipeng Cao, Peiyang Song, Nikolaus Vertovec, Weiru Cui, Zhihao Yang, Mingkang Liu, Luxia Lin, Bai Xue, Alessandro Abate
papers.abstract: Lyapunov functions and barrier certificates give state-space guarantees of stability and safety, but synthesizing and verifying them---especially for nonlinear, high-dimensional systems---remains an open challenge. Existing pipelines verify candidates with numerical solvers (sum-of-squares programs), interval methods, or satisfiability-modulo-theories (SMT) solvers, which often require relaxations, are conservative, or scale poorly with model dimension and nonlinearity. These limitations have also shaped benchmark design: standard test suites are dominated by low-dimensional polynomial systems chosen to suit what solvers can handle rather than what engineering applications require. We address both sides of this challenge. First, we introduce DynaCertBench, a benchmark of 105 instances: 80 non-redundant systems curated from the literature, extended with high-dimensional and control-constrained variants and new nonlinearly coupled systems, comprehensively spanning stability, region-of-attraction, forward-invariance, and safety tasks. Second, we present LLM2Cert, an LLM-driven framework that synthesizes candidate certificates and verifies them against their proof obligations: each obligation is routed to an SMT solver or directly to the Lean Proof-Repair agent. On DynaCertBench, LLM2Cert verifies 81 of 105 instances ($77.1\%$), a $17.1$ percentage point improvement over one-shot proposal without feedback. On the 81 fixed certificates, LLM2Cert verifies 22 that All-SMT leaves unresolved. Code and data are available at https://github.com/FormalCert-AI/llm2cert.

papers.title: Dynamics of the Liquidity Profile in Concentrated Liquidity Provision: An SPIDE Approach
papers.authors: Cheuk Yin Lee, Jimmy Risk, Shen-Ning Tung, Tai-Ho Wang
papers.abstract: We model the dynamics of the liquidity profile in Uniswap~V3 and other concentrated-liquidity automated market makers with a stochastic partial integro-differential equation (SPIDE). The profile, the aggregate of all provider positions across tick space, evolves under a degenerate Sturm--Liouville operator, which encodes mean-reverting concentration around the market price, coupled with a Hilbert--Schmidt integral operator, which captures nonlocal redistribution driven by provider repositioning. We establish existence and uniqueness of the mild solution in a weighted $L^2$ space built on the Gegenbauer eigensystem, and reduce the SPIDE to a coupled system of linear stochastic differential equations whose low-order modes describe the level, slope, and curvature of the profile. Pairing the SPIDE with a log-price process yields tractable expressions for pool reserves, pool value, and loss-versus-rebalancing under Ornstein--Uhlenbeck-type and Black--Scholes-type noise. A finite-rank calibration in a fixed reference frame, applied to three Uniswap pools, gives interpretable estimates and lowers active-band forecast error relative to a martingale benchmark on the two pools compatible with the stationary specification. On the third pool, out-of-sample diagnostics are consistent with nonstationarity, which motivates price-aware and time-varying extensions.

papers.title: Optimal Mixing for Local Edge-Coloring Dynamics on Trees
papers.abstract:
We study the mixing time of two local Markov chains for uniformly sampling proper edge colorings of trees. For a tree with $n$ vertices and maximum degree $\Delta$, we establish optimal mixing-time bounds for the single-edge Glauber dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+2$ and for the neighboring-edge heat-bath dynamics when $q\ge\Delta+1$. Both chains mix in $O_\Delta(n(\log n+\log(1/\varepsilon)))$ steps, uniformly over the number of colors $q$. These bounds are tight in their dependence on $n$ for fixed $\Delta$.
  Our proof establishes log-Sobolev inequalities through local color release, reusable recoloring buffers, and component entropy mixing. The two dynamics require different local constructions: a two-spare-color buffer for single-edge updates and a second-layer controller for neighboring-edge updates. The resulting entropy analysis applies to general bounded-degree trees, including regimes where worst-case spatial mixing fails.

papers.title: Multiple Stopping and Exercise Boundaries for American Put Options
papers.abstract: This article studies a finite-horizon American put option with up to $m$ exercise rights under the risk-neutral Black--Scholes model, where consecutive exercises must be separated by a prescribed refractory period $\delta>0$ and unused rights may expire. For each number of remaining rights, we show that optimal exercise is characterized by a single exercise boundary and that these boundaries are ordered by the number of remaining rights.
