We prove optimality of the first boundary-hitting time and establish local Lipschitz continuity of the exercise boundaries within each open deadline strip. Away from the deadlines, we derive smooth fit, the associated quasi-variational inequality and free-boundary formulation, an early-exercise-premium representation, recursive Volterra-type boundary equations, and a verification theorem. We also extend the recursive formulation to an independent random termination time, thereby allowing for exogenous termination of the option contract.

papers.title: Global Convergence of Detailed Balanced Mass Action Systems
papers.authors: Haoran Lv (BitMiracle AI Lab), Chengjin Ni (BitMiracle AI Lab), Manqin Wang (BitMiracle AI Lab), Shenli He (BitMiracle AI Lab)
papers.abstract: We give a self-contained proof that, for a finite detailed balanced mass-action system with positive rate constants, each positive stoichiometric compatibility class contains exactly one positive equilibrium and every positive trajectory converges to it, together with a Lean 4 formalization of the complete argument from persistence to convergence. Boundedness and persistence come from the barrier argument of OpenAI (2026) for weakly reversible systems: an arbitrary-tolerance affine approximation yields a finite-minimum barrier whose superlevel sets confine trajectories and give one logarithmic bound for all solutions from a given initial state. The Horn-Jackson dissipation identity identifies the positive equilibria as an exponential family with parameters in the orthogonal complement of the stoichiometric subspace, which gives uniqueness in each class. A bounded-speed descent argument replaces LaSalle's invariance principle; it uses neither uniqueness of solutions nor continuous dependence on initial data, and it places every cluster point in that family. The route given here is direct and elementary, and its main theorem is checked by the Lean kernel against explicit definitions. The proofs, the Lean development, and the manuscript were produced in ClawsGO Science, an agent harness that packages a complete research environment: Claude Opus 5.5 made the research decisions, GPT 6 Astra carried them out, and the Lean kernel checked every formal step.

papers.title: Surface Defects in the $\mathcal{N}=2$ Lens Space Index and Elliptic Integrability
papers.abstract: We determine the surface-defect difference operators of the 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ lens space index for class $\mathcal{S}$ theories of type $A_{N-1}$ on $(\mathbb{S}^3/\mathbb{Z}_r)\times\mathbb{S}^1$. For generic fugacities $(p,q,t)$ and arbitrary rank $N$, orbifold order $r$ and discrete holonomies, their coefficients are finite products of theta functions with nomes $p^r$ and $q^r$. After an explicit gauge transformation, Gaussian in the holonomies, each operator factorizes into two elliptic Ruijsenaars--Schneider-type operators with step $pq$, one with nome $p^r$ and one with nome $q^r$, acting on variables glued along a lattice. Using this factorization and a Wronski-type relation, we prove that all the operators commute. We also establish a sufficient criterion for self-adjointness with respect to the bilinear vector multiplet pairing. It applies to the basic mixed operator and, in suitable parameter chambers, to the pure $p$- and $q$-type operators; for general mixed operators the contour prescription remains open. These results support the expectations from S-duality.

papers.title: Stiff source terms inside ADER-DG method
papers.authors: I. S. Popov, A. P. Popova
papers.abstract: ADER-DG numerical method with the LST-DG predictor, when used to solve hyperbolic equations with stiff source terms, exhibits properties characteristic of IMEX computational schemes. With increasing stiffness, characterized by the parameter $z = \nu{\Delta t}^{n} < 0$, the maximum of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}$ of the ADER-DG numerical method increases. In the region of strong stiffness $|z| \gg 1$, a linear increase in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z) \sim |z|$ occurs. In the region of small source terms $|z| \ll 1$, the results $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ transform into known results for the problem $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(0)$ without source terms. In the transition region $|z| \sim 1$, a range of insignificant decrease in the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(z)$ is discovered. In the linear case, instability is violated precisely when one of the matrix eigenvalues reaches $\lambda = -1$, regardless of the phase $\theta$ of the numerical solution. A rigorous stability theory of the ADER-DG numerical method for stiff problems for arbitrary degree $N$ of basis polynomials is constructed. The stability condition is simplified to solving a polynomial equation for the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}$. Highly accurate dependencies of the Courant number $\mathrm{CFL}_{\rm max}(N, z)$ of the ADER-DG method on the parameter $z$ are obtained. A rigorous direct proof of the approximation of the ADER-DG method is presented. Approximation orders $p = N+1$ for arbitrary degrees $N$ are rigorously derived. A set of numerical experiments is carried out to apply the ADER-DG method to solving both a linear advection-reaction equation and the system of Euler equations for a two-component reacting medium. The results obtained in these calculations confirm the theoretical results well.

papers.title: From Turing Patterns to Spike Self-Replication and Nucleation in a Growing-Domain Tulip Breaking Virus Model
papers.abstract: A recently proposed reaction-diffusion model for the tulip breaking virus (TBV) has been shown to generate striped pigmentation patterns on growing tulip petals. In this paper, we investigate the formation of localized spike patterns in this model in the asymptotic limit of small viral diffusivity. It is known that two distinct bifurcation mechanisms can occur which generate new spikes as the domain half-length $L$ slowly increases: spike self-replication and spike nucleation. Self-replication occurs through a saddle-node bifurcation of the inner spike core problem, whereas nucleation is associated with a fold of the nonlinear outer problem. Using matched asymptotic expansions, we derive critical conditions for these mechanisms and construct phase diagrams that predict which mechanism occurs first as $L$ increases, or whether nucleation is absent. We further combine these results with a Turing instability analysis of the homogeneous steady state to obtain a phase diagram of pattern-forming mechanisms. An interesting finding is that, for the TBV model, the Turing-unstable region lies entirely within the parameter regime where spike nucleation is possible. These results provide further insight into the mechanisms underlying the formation and evolution of pigmentation patterns in virus-infected tulips.

papers.title: Inverse KLT kernel of AdS string-amplitude building blocks from the intersection matrix
papers.abstract: We develop a topological and combinatorial interpretation of the Kawai--Lewellen--Tye (KLT) relations for $n$-point AdS string-amplitude building blocks, which are disk integrals with multivariable multiple polylogarithm insertions and sphere integrals with their single-valued counterparts. Building on the framework of twisted de Rham theory over a noncommutative ring, we reformulate the problem in terms of associahedral chambers of the moduli space loaded with solutions of the Knizhnik--Zamolodchikov equation. We construct regularized twisted cycles and express their intersection pairings through local monodromies and Drinfeld associators, which control transport between fusion-tree normalizations. Organizing the intersection contributions by common boundary faces yields the intersection matrix, which is identified with the inverse KLT kernel by the twisted period relation. The field-theory limit of the inverse KLT kernel is also given.

papers.title: Sequential Monte Carlo Sampling of Feasible Regions Represented by R-Functions
papers.abstract:
Feasible-region sampling and volume estimation become increasingly inefficient when constraints define only a small fraction of a convenient bounding domain. We combine R-functions, which encode compound feasibility as a continuous signed field, with sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) samplers. The proposed construction exploits not only the sign of the R-function, which determines exact feasibility, but also its continuous negative values outside the feasible set, which provide graded information on constraint violation. Logistic intermediate distributions use this information to guide particles progressively towards feasibility, while the final target distribution remains uniform on the feasible region.
  Experiments on intersections and unions, including disconnected cases of hyperballs, show substantial variance reductions relative to direct rejection sampling, with the statistical advantage generally increasing as the feasible fraction decreases. For sufficiently small feasible regions, these advantages persist even after accounting for computational cost. To isolate the benefit of continuous R-function information, we also compare the proposed method with an SMC sampler with a region-only (RO) construction that uses the same sequential particle machinery but retains only binary feasible/infeasible information. We demonstrate that the R-function-informed SMC method concentrates particles in the feasible region earlier and produces lower-variance volume estimates than RO.

papers.title: Array Rotation in Near-Field ISAC: Communication, Detection, and Estimation Under Low-Complexity Transmit Architectures
papers.abstract: This paper studies near-field integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) with a rotatable base-station array under an exact spherical-wave propagation model. For a general transmit covariance, we derive a Cram\'er--Rao bound (CRB) decomposition that separates target-side geometry from transmit-covariance-dependent terms. We then specialize the framework to two representative low-complexity architectures: a single-stream superposition architecture, and a dual-waveform split architecture design. We characterize the communication-, detection-, and estimation-optimal rotations for each architecture using the exact finite-array model. In addition, we show how a second-order approximation yields compact approximate expressions for the optimal rotation angles. We also study uncertainty in the target state used for beamforming design through a correlated Gaussian perturbation model, and derive approximations of the optimal robust rotation angles for target sensing and detection. The analysis shows that the two architectures behave differently under rotation: the single-stream design can align communication and detection tasks, whereas the dual-waveform design exhibits a direct communication--detection tradeoff and can incur a larger communication loss when sensing is prioritized. Numerical results show clear gains over a fixed array orientation, especially for range estimation, and close agreement between the approximate and exact rotation choices. Detection is less affected by target-state errors than estimation in the considered cases.

papers.title: Timelike Supersymmetric Geometries in Seven-Dimensional Supergravity
papers.abstract: Seven-dimensional supergravity poses a uniquely intricate supersymmetry problem, combining topologically massive higher-form gauge dynamics, distinct Clifford algebra properties, and rich geometric structures. We first establish the complete formulation of the maximal Cartan-gauged theory in terms of the gauge-invariant higher-form flux, including both the bosonic action and supersymmetry variations. This formulation, which also makes the smooth ungauged limit manifest, is achieved by requiring a consistent truncation to the minimal Cartan-gauged theory in the equal-charge limit. We construct the complete bilinear system for a timelike Killing vector, where additional internal orientation of the symplectic-Majorana spinor arises already in the scalar sector, uniquely among pure minimal ungauged theories. In the equal-charge sector, we decouple the algebraic constraints into SU$(3)$-isotypic components, and analyse the differential bilinear relations, determining the permitted dilaton gradient, fluxes, fibration twist and intrinsic torsion of the base. We prove that with gauging and active Cartan flux, the complex scalar bilinear vanishes identically. We also construct a Killing gauge for the higher-form potential compatible with the self-duality condition. We show that with gauging but no active Cartan flux, the Killing vector also acts as a generator of the gauged R-symmetry, and the base structure is enlarged from SU$(3)$ to U$(3)$. We find that BPS-flow solutions realize this setting. With supersymmetry, we isolate a single independent component of the 3-form equation across an exhaustive four-class partition for both theories within this setup. Applied to known and proposed solutions in both theories, this classification exposes unexplored sectors and provides an accessible toolbox for constructing and testing solutions and developing new geometric and holographic applications.

papers.title: Large Language Models Meet Bayesian Optimization: Towards Self-evolving Wireless Digital Twins
papers.authors: Yingzhuo Sun, Haoyun Li, Ming Xiao, Francisco J. Ferrao, Berna Ozbek
papers.abstract: Wireless digital twins (DTs) are increasingly integrated with artificial intelligence to support online modeling, prediction, and network optimization. However, most existing approaches perform adaptation within predefined learning or optimization structures, which may become unsuitable when wireless tasks and operating conditions change. In this article, we investigate the integration of large language models (LLMs) and Bayesian optimization (BO) to extend wireless DTs from online adaptation towards algorithm-level self-evolution. We introduce an LLM-assisted BO framework in which BO provides a stable and sample-efficient optimization backbone, while the LLM determines whether selected BO components should be retained or adapted based on the current task and accumulated optimization experience. In simulations, we apply the framework to Gaussian process (GP) kernel discovery for a multi-user wireless beam-selection problem. Simulation results show that the LLM-discovered kernel improves the final BO performance by 19.7% on the training tasks compared with the strongest standard kernel baseline. The results demonstrate the potential of combining LLM flexibility with structured BO for self-evolving wireless DTs.

papers.title: Deep ReLU Networks Can Fail the Best Approximation Property for Continuous Target Functions
papers.abstract: We construct a continuous function on $[-1,1]^2$ for which the infimum of the $L^2$-approximation error over the class of ReLU networks with two hidden layers and architecture $(2,2,1,1)$ is not attained. This counterexample shows that deep ReLU networks do not satisfy the best approximation property in general, even for continuous target functions. Our findings contrast with existing results for shallow neural networks, where ReLU is one of the few activation functions that guarantee the existence of global minima in typical regression tasks. The proof is based on the fact that the breaklines for neurons in the second hidden layer can bend, which breaks the symmetry arguments used in the one-hidden-layer case.

papers.title: Model Predictive Control of Wind Turbines: A Model-Oriented Review of Prediction Models, Control Objectives, and Nonlinear Aerodynamic Formulations
papers.authors: Roya Khalili-Amirabadi, Mohsen Jalaeian-Farimani, Mahdi Ghane
papers.abstract: Model predictive control (MPC) has been applied to wind-turbine regulation with markedly different internal prediction models, ranging from linearized low-order turbine models to nonlinear, aeroelastic, floating, and data-driven predictors. This review organizes the literature primarily by the model propagated by the controller and treats model order, predictor representation, MPC formulation, control objective, and validation plant as separate descriptors. Primary studies show that low-order linear or piecewise-affine predictors are attractive for constrained power and speed regulation, whereas flexible drivetrain, structural, and floating models are needed when drivetrain twist, tower motion, blade loads, or platform dynamics are explicit control quantities. Nonlinear and economic MPC studies further demonstrate coordinated pitch/torque control across broad operating regions, while preview, repetitive, and data-driven formulations address wind prediction, periodic loads, and model mismatch. Particular attention is given to aerodynamic pitch dependence: variable-pitch turbine dynamics can be non-affine with respect to applied pitch, and the term NMPC alone does not prove that the original nonlinear pitch map is retained inside the optimizer. The review therefore adopts a conservative, equation-based classification for direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation. Here, direct nonlinear applied-pitch propagation means that the applied pitch at each prediction step is evaluated inside the original nonlinear aerodynamic map, rather than replacing that dependence by a linearized, scheduled, piecewise-affine, or learned surrogate. The literature supports a remaining integration challenge at the intersection of flexible drivetrain prediction, nonlinear aerodynamic pitch treatment, explicit constraints and load objectives, and validated adaptive or learned model correction.

papers.title: Exact stress-tensor generators distinguish integrable continuations
papers.authors: H. Babaei-Aghbolagh, Song He, Zahra Pezhman
papers.abstract: The same leading $T\bar T$ interaction can coexist with sharply different strong-field responses, even within causal, classically integrable sigma models. We reconstruct exact autonomous stress-tensor generators for prescribed one-scale Courant--Hilbert families in two dimensions. Separating the invariant stress scale from a signed trace ratio reduces reconstruction to one scalar inversion on each invertible physical branch. The resulting profile determines both the deformation law and the relation between local energy density and pressure. For generalized Born--Infeld and logarithmic models, the leading interactions coincide, yet pressure saturates in the former and grows without bound in the latter. Their exact generators are respectively quadratic and nonpolynomial, the latter involving Lambert $W_{-1}$. A regular Legendre transformation gives the same profile in the auxiliary potential formulation. The flows commute locally with root-$T\bar T$ within a common smooth branch and retain a common classical Lax form. Exact reconstruction thus quantifies the nonlinear freedom left by leading-order matching.

papers.title: Deep Learning for Random Objects in Metric Spaces: Beyond Manifold Assumptions
papers.authors: Marcos Matabuena, Xiaokai Luo, Oscar Hernan Madrid Padilla
papers.abstract: Deep learning (DL) methods have substantially improved predictive performance across a wide range of downstream prediction tasks, enabling new discoveries in multiple domains. However, principled DL methods for non-Euclidean random objects remain relatively scarce, despite the growing importance of modern biomedical outcomes taking the form of probability distributions, random graphs, functions, and other random objects in metric spaces. Motivated by a new generation of digital and clinical biomarkers, we propose a deep learning framework for regression with random objects in metric spaces. Our approach operates directly on the metric structure of the response space, avoiding restrictive manifold or Euclidean embedding assumptions imposed by many existing methods. At the same time, it retains modern statistical guarantees under the stated statistical assumptions. We establish statistical consistency and convergence rates for the proposed estimator, and characterize conditions under which it can mitigate the curse of dimensionality for hierarchically compositional regression functions. Extensive simulation studies demonstrate competitive predictive performance, with gains over several competing approaches in multiple Euclidean and non-Euclidean configurations. Finally, we demonstrate the practical utility of the proposed framework in two digital health case studies with distribution-valued outcomes in Wasserstein spaces, using high-resolution accelerometry and continuous glucose monitoring data. Embedding-based deep-learning methods may be less suitable when no informative low-dimensional representation exists or when the learned embedding does not adequately preserve the intrinsic geometry of the response space.

papers.title: Explicit quasi-periodic solutions to the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
papers.authors: Xiaoxue Xu, Wei Liu, Junyi Zhu
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic solutions to the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation are investigated. A Lax pair of the discrete integrable equation is derived, by which we obtain a nonlinear integrable symplectic map. Resorting to this map, the Riemann theta function expressions for discrete potentials are calculated. Consequently, we get the explicit solutions for the discrete derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, whose quasi-periodic properties are illustrated through the cases of genus one and genus two.

papers.title: A second-order linear decoupled scheme with a relaxed zero-energy variable for Rayleigh-B\'enard convection
papers.abstract: We construct a second-order, linear, and fully decoupled scheme for Rayleigh--B\'enard convection between Navier-slip walls. The nonlinear terms are treated explicitly and multiplied by a scalar with exact value $1$ and no energy contributed to the continuous problem. As a result, each BDF2 step, with a rotational pressure correction, solves only constant-coefficient linear problems. For the time discretization, we prove that, for any time-step, the energy decays when the walls have equal temperatures, under a condition on the thermal weight, and the energy is bounded on finite time intervals when heated from below. Relaxing the scalar towards $1$ preserves both estimates. Energy stability does not control the accuracy of the scalar; the velocity and temperature fields are computed with its unrelaxed value, whose deviation from $1$ scales like $(E/C)(\delta t/\tau)^3$ for kinetic energy $E$, time-scale $\tau$ of the flow, and weight $C$ of the scalar equation. In our tests, choosing $C$ comparable to $E$ keeps this deviation small and doubles the largest time-step for which steady rolls are reproduced to a relative difference of $10^{-8}$. With Taylor--Hood elements, we observe second-order convergence in time, recover the critical Rayleigh numbers, and match published Nusselt numbers to within $0.5\%$. A three-dimensional implementation passes corresponding validation tests.

papers.title: Dimension-free regimes for unadjusted Langevin in ridge-separable models: A subspace robust Wasserstein analysis
papers.authors: Yuansi Chen, Francesco Pedrotti, Peter A. Whalley
papers.abstract: The Unadjusted Langevin Algorithm (ULA) is widely used for high-dimensional Bayesian inference. Classical analyses in Wasserstein-2 distance predict an asymptotic bias and a mixing time that grow with dimension, but this metric is stronger than necessary for many statistical tasks. We instead analyze the bias in subspace robust Wasserstein distance, which controls the mean and arbitrary low-dimensional marginals and is therefore well suited to observables typically estimated in practice. For ridge-separable potentials formed with i.i.d. data, we prove high-probability bounds showing a bell-shaped mixing profile as the number of data points $N$ varies relative to the dimension $d$. In the overparameterized regime, the effective dimension is the rank $N$ of the data-dependent perturbation, leading to complexity depending on $N$ rather than $d$. In the large-sample regime, Gaussian-perturbation estimates yield dimension-free complexity once $N$ is sufficiently large. In contrast, near the proportional regime $\asymp d$, we prove that dimension-free guarantees are impossible in general.

papers.title: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
papers.abstract: How much entanglement can two distant laboratories share when their connection is noisy? We relate this question to deciding which of two quantum hypotheses is present. Our one-shot bounds apply to entanglement generation over a quantum channel and to one-way entanglement distillation from a shared state. We use Cheng's trace inequality to bound the infidelity of a Petz decoder in terms of a binary hypothesis testing cost. Applying the inequality before averaging over codes reduces the error analysis to computing a second moment of random subspaces. The proof covers every integer target dimension and treats rank-deficient states explicitly. A corollary expresses the achievable entanglement through hypothesis-testing coherent information, with a single logarithmic error slack and exact integer rounding. We also prove an error-preserving conversion from entanglement generation codes to entanglement transmission codes: the target dimension decreases by only a constant factor at fixed error, and the decoder is the original decoder followed by local processing. Consequently, for both entanglement generation and entanglement transmission, arbitrary pure reference-input states yield the same coherent-information rate, second-order Gaussian correction at the original error tolerance, and explicit achievable logarithmic remainder. For commuting testing hypotheses, the logarithmic remainder improves to a constant. These results give a direct route from binary distinguishability to explicit recovery guarantees and finite-resource quantum communication rates.

papers.title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Likelihood Ratio Tests for the Power Spherical Distribution
papers.abstract: The Power Spherical distribution has been proposed as a computationally efficient alternative to the von Mises-Fisher distribution for data on the unit sphere, with reduced computational cost for simulation and a simpler normalizing constant. Despite these advantages, its statistical inference properties remain underdeveloped. In this paper, we develop a likelihood-based framework for estimation and inference for the Power Spherical distribution. Within this framework, we develop maximum likelihood estimation procedures for both the central direction and concentration parameter. Building on these estimators, we formulate likelihood ratio tests for hypotheses involving known and unknown parameters, study their asymptotic behavior, and evaluate finite-sample performance through simulation studies. The results demonstrate accurate Type I error control and good power when the asymptotic chi-square approximation is appropriate, while the parametric bootstrap provides reliable inference in small-sample settings or those where the dimension is large relative to the sample size. The findings also highlight nontrivial dependence of the power of tests for the central direction on the concentration parameter.

papers.title: Structure-preserving reduced-order models of thin panels in supersonic and hypersonic flow
papers.abstract: We build structure-preserving reduced-order models for both challenge problems of the AePW-4 High-Speed Working Group. They are a clamped thin panel at Mach 1.92 (RC-19) and a cantilever plate at Mach 5.85 (HyMAX). The published data for each case hold no time-resolved response and no repeated runs. The physics must therefore be carried by the form of the model. One construction gives two models per problem. A Ritz-Galerkin reference model describes the plate. A learned model keeps the reference model's exact potential, fits the remaining generalized forces, and trains only a dissipation that cannot add energy. Its energy balance holds for any weights by construction. On the trained model the worst relative residual is 2.2e-15. On RC-19, shock relations predict a pressure ratio of 1.521 across the panel. Pressure-sensitive paint measured the same value. Thirty runs of the learned model place the mean dominant frequency within 1.0% of the measured 236 Hz. At one periodic and one chaotic condition, the learned model reproduces the response regime of a published reduced-order model in all sixteen runs. It does so without that model's 113 Hz spectral peak, which the measurements do not show. Measured displacements can also correct the chaotic response through one more force that respects the energy balance. We tested this on synthetic data at the experiment's 5 kHz sampling rate. The state error is 1.25% of the panel thickness without noise and 3.5% with 10 micrometers of noise. On HyMAX the learned model follows the reference model's trailing-edge displacement for 65 ms with a relative error of 3.7%. These results show that a model whose structure carries the physics can match measured flutter behavior when the available data cannot train it.

papers.title: Closing All-Exp Gaps in Local Search for the Traveling Salesman Problem and Maximum Constraint Assignment
papers.authors: Sophia Heimann, Hung P. Hoang, Stefan Hougardy
papers.abstract: We prove the all-exp property for the Traveling Salesman Problem with the $2$-opt neighborhood, and for $(3,2,2)$- and $(2,3,2)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment with the flip neighborhood. The all-exp property states that infinitely many instances have an initial solution from which every sequence of improving moves to a local optimum, and hence every run of local search, has exponential length. For the Traveling Salesman Problem, the all-exp property was previously known for every $k$-opt neighborhood with $k \ge 3$, so our result for $2$-opt completes the picture for all $k$-kopt neighborhoods. In $(p,q,r)$-Maximum Constraint Assignment, each constraint involves at most $p$ variables, each variable occurs in at most $q$ constraints, and each domain has size $r$. Decreasing any of the parameters of $(3,2,2)$ or $(2,3,2)$ yields a problem in which every sequence of improving flips has polynomial length, so both Maximum Constraint Assignment results are tight. All three results settle long-standing open problems. Our proofs build on a common construction idea, which reveals a close connection between the local-search dynamics of the three problems.

papers.title: Dispersive Tree Agreements for Multi-Robot Coordination
papers.authors: Shashank A. Deshpande, Blake T. Edwards, Jonathan P. How
papers.abstract: Multi-robot coordination of nonlinear systems is naturally formulated as joint-space optimal control subject to constraints over groups of robots. Existing methods that approach joint optimality remain largely centralized, offline, and confined to collision-free motion planning, while decentralized, real-time counterparts target safe navigation without pursuing the joint optimum. This paper develops a decentralized, real-time planner that approaches the joint optimum as an anytime process. We extend a recent single-robot framework that searches dispersive trees of forward-propagated commands for differentially flat systems to coordinate a multi-robot team near-optimally. We first show that the inter-robot coupling can be effectively replaced by some local constraints, under which locally grown dispersive trees contain a near-optimal agreement. It is this structure that the robots pursue by decentralized column generation, negotiating rents on the shared space that guide the search of each robot's tree. The negotiation settles on an agreement whose near-optimality is certified at quiescence. Our protocol, WarpWeaver, implements this negotiation as an asynchronous real-time loop over a receding horizon, and demonstrates effective closure to quiesced agreements even when real-time deadlines cut the negotiation short. In simulation, WarpWeaver reduces total travel time by up to 22% against centralized offline planners on the Dynobench suite and by up to 37% against a decentralized real-time baseline, and nearly doubles the success rate of a task-specific planner on graph connectivity. Hardware experiments on six robots planning onboard demonstrate real-world implementability.

papers.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
papers.authors: Yin-Kai Yu, Zhong-Chao Wei, Zi-Xiang Li
papers.abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.authors: Hongrui Chen, Zhiyan Ding, Jianfeng Lu
papers.abstract: We propose a new method for proving $L^2$ and modified logarithmic Sobolev inequalities with constants independent of system size for quantum Gibbs samplers whose Lindblad generators satisfy Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (KMS) detailed balance. We first establish the $L^2$ logarithmic Sobolev inequality by transporting it along a temperature-dependent path from the infinite-temperature product state to the target Gibbs state while maintaining a size-independent decay rate for the sandwiched R\'enyi-2 divergence. A tensor-power argument, combined with the quantum asymptotic equipartition property, then transfers this decay bound to relative entropy, yielding the modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality. This approach provides a general framework for proving size-independent logarithmic Sobolev inequalities for quantum Gibbs samplers. We apply it to two regimes: one-dimensional quantum spin chains at every finite temperature, and finite-range quantum spin systems at sufficiently high temperature in any fixed dimension.

papers.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
papers.abstract:
Does computing a composition of total Boolean functions require the product of the randomized query complexities of its factors? We give a negative answer. There are families of total functions $f,g$ such that $R(f\circ g) =\Theta\!\left(\frac1{\log R(g)}\right)R(f)R(g)$ This result requires first separating linearized query complexity $\LR$, as well as noisy randomized query complexity $noisyR$, from standard randomized query complexity $R$. Both constructions essentially come from totalizing existing partial function separations, albeit via different techniques.
  By adapting these techniques, we also construct total functions separating every adjacent pair in the chain from sabotage $RS$, max-conflict $\bar{\chi}$, and linearised query complexity $LR$. We show that AND-of-ORs separates conflict $\chi$ from max-conflict $\bar{\chi}$ complexity and makes conflict and sabotage incomparable. Finally, randomized complexity can be smaller than its composition limit $R^*$ by the maximal factor $\Theta(\log R)$. The total--total composition separation is also formalized in Lean.

papers.title: Ricci flow of Integrable Sigma Models, Hitchin Systems and Quantum Seiberg-Witten theory
papers.authors: G. Bonelli, S. Lacroix, T. Pedroni, A. Tanzini
papers.abstract: We construct a family of integrable 2d sigma models through 4d Chern-Simons theory and show that their classical point-particle reduction corresponds to a Hitchin system. The integrable Hitchin quantisation then provides a natural candidate Hamiltonian for the one-loop reduced dynamics of the sigma models, which coincides with the Perelman operator in all cases examined. This allows us to study the corresponding spectral problems using 4d $\mathcal{N}=2$ gauge theory and 2d conformal field theory methods. For the sausage model, we derive exact quantisation conditions and compute exponentially small corrections essential for the agreement with numerical finite-volume results.

papers.title: On the $\theta$-split side of the local relative trace formula
papers.abstract: The author derives an expression for one side of the local relative trace formula, at the level of Lie algebras, by combining methods of Arthur and Harish-Chandra with the structure theory for reductive symmetric spaces.

papers.title: $\delta$-Superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras
papers.abstract: In the paper, a complete description of the $\delta$-derivations and the $\delta$-superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\neq2$ is given. In particular, new examples of nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and odd $\frac{1}{2}$-superderivations are given that are not operators of right multiplication by an element of the superalgebra.

papers.title: A new formulation of the Teichm\"uller TQFT
papers.abstract: Using the Weil--Gel'fand--Zak transform of Faddeev's quantum dilogarithm, we construct a compact state integral for positively shaped triangulations of oriented pseudo three-manifolds. The integral is labelled by a circle-valued first cohomology class of the vertex complement (a ``sector'') and takes boundary values in a line bundle over compatible boundary cocycles. We prove absolute convergence, smoothness, invariance under shape gauge transformations and under compatible shaped $2$--$3$ moves, branching independence, and a single-valued global meromorphic continuation in all shape and boundary parameters for each fixed quantum parameter. Gluing is expressed by a conditional Haar integral which retains the final cohomology class; the ordinary trace of integrated cut amplitudes computes an average of the sectors over a torus of classes determined by the cut, and is a sewing formula for every cut of a closed oriented three-manifold, but not for arbitrary pseudo-manifolds. For closed admissible triangulations, the original Teichm\"uller partition function is the normalized average of the sectors; this yields its global meromorphic continuation. A translation law relates sectors differing by twice an extending class, with phases given by linking pairings; for closed three-manifolds the sectors are supported in a distinguished coset of twice the torsion group and are determined by a single amplitude, which a nonvanishing twisted quadratic Gauss sum recovers from the original partition function.

papers.title: Homological subsets of Spec
papers.abstract: We recover some data of a module $M$ from the Ext-family $\{Ext^i_R(M,R)\}$. In this regard, we investigate homological subsets of $Spec(R)$, defined by the help of Ext-family. For example, we present a situation for which $\bigcup_{i=0}^\infty Ass(Ext^i_R(M,R))$ is infinite, thereby answering a question of Vasconcelos. We extend Grothendieck's calculation of $dim(Ext^g_R(M,R))$ and present some new situations to calculate $dim(Ext^\ast_R(M,R))$. Also, we compute support and the set of all associated prime ideals of the Ext-family in a serial of nontrivial cases.

papers.title: Random Burnside Groups
papers.abstract: Fix integers $m\ge2$ and $k\ge1$. For every sufficiently large fixed odd exponent $M$, choose $k$ independent elements uniformly from the sphere of radius $\ell$ in the free Burnside group $B_m(M)$. We prove that the quotient by their normal closure is infinite with probability at least $1-e^{-c\ell}$. More precisely, the quotient map has no nontrivial kernel element of length at most $\kappa\ell$, for constants $c,\kappa>0$. We also consider the analogue of the Gromov positive density model for the Burnside variety.

papers.title: On invariant $1$-dimensional representations of a finite $W$-algebra
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra over $\mathbf{C}$ and $G$ be the corresponding simply connected algebraic group. Consider a nilpotent element $e\in \mathfrak{g}$, the corresponding element $\chi=(e, \bullet)$ in $\mathfrak{g}^*$, and the coadjoint orbit $\mathbf{O}=G\chi$. We are interested in the set $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ of codimension $1$ ideals $J\subset \mathcal{W}$ in a finite $W$-algebra $\mathcal{W}=U(\mathfrak{g}, e)$. We have a natural action of the component group $\Gamma=Z_G(\chi)/Z_G^\circ(\chi)$ on $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$. Denote the set of $\Gamma$-stable points of $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^1(\mathcal{W})$ by $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^{\Gamma}$. For a classical $\mathfrak{g}$ Premet and Topley proved that $\mathfrak{J}\mathfrak{d}^{1}(\mathcal{W})^{\Gamma}$ are parameterized by the points of an affine space. In this paper we will give an alternative proof of this fact using completely different approach. As a corollary of our construction, we imply that for classical $\mathfrak{g}$ all $\Gamma$-invariant $1$-dimensional representations of $\mathcal{W}$ are obtained by a parabolic induction introduced by Losev.

papers.title: The symplectic isotopy problem for rational cuspidal curves
papers.abstract: We define a suitably tame class of singular symplectic curves in 4-manifolds, namely those whose singularities are modeled on complex curve singularities. We study the corresponding symplectic isotopy problem, with a focus on rational curves with irreducible singularities (rational cuspidal curves) in the complex projective plane. We prove that every such curve is isotopic to a complex curve in degrees up to 5, and for curves with one singularity whose link is a torus knot. Classification results of symplectic isotopy classes rely on pseudo-holomorphic curves together with a symplectic version of birational geometry of log pairs and techniques from 4-dimensional topology.

papers.title: A Diagnostic for Bias in Linear Mixed Model Estimators Induced by Dependence Between the Random Effects and the Corresponding Model Matrix
papers.authors: Andrew T. Karl, Dale L. Zimmerman
papers.abstract: We explore how violations of the often-overlooked standard assumption that the random effects model matrix in a linear mixed model is fixed (and thus independent of the random effects vector) can lead to bias in estimators of estimable functions of the fixed effects. However, if the random effects of the original mixed model are instead also treated as fixed effects, or if the fixed and random effects model matrices are orthogonal with respect to the inverse of the error covariance matrix (with probability one), or if the random effects and the corresponding model matrix are independent, then these estimators are unbiased. The bias in the general case is quantified, and a diagnostic for its random-effects contribution is compared to a randomized permutation distribution of the predicted random effects, producing an informative summary graphic for each estimator of interest. This is demonstrated through the examination of sporting outcomes used to estimate a home field advantage.

papers.title: Fekete Points as Norming Sets for Random Holomorphic Sections
papers.abstract: We prove that Fekete configurations associated with a positive Hermitian line bundle over a compact K\"ahler manifold are asymptotically exact norming sets for random holomorphic sections. For every fixed $a>0$, the ratio of the supremum norm of a degree-$k$ section to its maximum on the degree-$\lceil ak\rceil$ Fekete configuration converges to one in probability. This holds for any background K\"ahler form: Fekete equidistribution provides enough sampling points near the maximum of the limiting pointwise variance. We obtain polynomial upper bounds for the tail of the ratio and almost-sure norm comparisons. In contrast, when the limiting variance is nonconstant, we construct separated arrays of cardinality comparable to the section-space dimension for which the ratio converges to a constant strictly greater than one. General separated arrays still satisfy probabilistic norming inequalities with degree-independent constants, and every such array is asymptotically exact if and only if the volume form is proportional to $c_1(L,h)^n$. We also prove a discrete $L^2$ norm comparison with exponentially small exceptional probability. The norm comparisons and convergence statements hold in both the Gaussian and spherical ensembles.

papers.title: Ax-Schanuel with derivatives for mixed period mappings
papers.abstract: We prove the Ax-Schanuel property of the derivatives of mixed period mappings. We also prove the jet space reformulation of this result. The proofs use the Ax-Schanuel result for principal bundles with flat connections obtained by Bl\'{a}zquez-Sanz, Casale, Freitag, and Nagloo.

papers.title: Cluster scattering diagrams of acyclic affine type
papers.abstract: We give an explicit construction of the cluster scattering diagram for any acyclic exchange matrix of affine type. We show that the corresponding cluster scattering fan coincides both with the mutation fan and with a fan constructed in the almost-positive roots model.

papers.title: Restricted variational principle for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal formalism for Lyapunov exponents of typical one-step cocycles. We establish a variational relation between the Legendre transform of topological pressure of the generalized singular value function and measure-theoretic entropies. As a consequence, we show that the restricted variational principle of Lyapunov exponents holds for typical one-step cocycles. Furthermore, we prove a variational principle formula for the generalized singular value function.

papers.title: Locked Polyomino Tilings
papers.abstract:
A locked $t$-omino tiling is a grid tiling by $t$-ominoes such that, if you remove any pair of tiles, the only way to fill in the remaining $2t$ grid cells with $t$-ominoes is to use the same two tiles in the exact same configuration as before. We exclude degenerate cases where there is only one tiling overall due to small dimensions. It is a classic (and straightforward) result that finite grids do not admit locked 2-omino tilings. In this paper, we construct explicit locked $t$-omino tilings for $t\geq3$ on square and rectangular grids of various dimensions. We show that locked 3- and 4-omino tilings exist on finite square grids of arbitrarily large size. The result for 4-omino tilings in particular is remarkable because they are so rare and difficult to construct: Only a single tiling is known to exist on any grid up to size $40\times40$. We also find locked 5- and 6-omino tilings, and provide a computer-assisted proof that locked 7-omino tilings do not exist on any rectangular grid. In a weighted version of the problem where vertices of the grid may have weights from the set $\{1,2\}$ that count toward the total tile size, we demonstrate the existence of locked tilings on arbitrarily large square weighted grids with only 6 tiles. Finally, we construct locked $t$-omino tilings of the infinite grid for arbitrarily large $t$.
  Locked $t$-omino tilings arise as obstructions to widely used political redistricting algorithms in a model of redistricting where the underlying census geography is a grid graph. Most prominent is the ReCom Markov chain, which takes a random walk on the space of redistricting plans by iteratively merging and splitting pairs of districts (tiles) at a time. Locked $t$-omino tilings are isolated states in the state space of ReCom. The constructions in this paper are counterexamples to the meta-conjecture that ReCom is irreducible on graphs of practical interest.

papers.title: The Recursive Behavior of the Number of Irreducible Factors of Certain Rational Transformations over Finite Fields
papers.abstract: Constructing irreducible polynomials over finite fields via rational transformations is an active field of study. In this paper, we show that the method can be used for more than that. By considering normalized rational functions $Q$ that generate an invariant subfield $\mathbb{F}_q(x)^G$ of $\mathbb{F}_q(x)$, for a subgroup $G\le Aut(\mathbb{F}_q(x)/\mathbb{F}_q)$, and exploiting the factorization pattern of their rational transformations, we are able to prove that the sets arising from considering whether the rational transformation $f^Q$ has exactly $deg(Q)$ irreducible factors of the same degree as $f$, or an irreducible factor of higher degree, admit a recursive behavior, i.e. their numbers satisfy a recursive equation. These sets occasionally can be described in terms of arithmetical properties the roots of the irreducible polynomials satisfy, e.g. their roots satisfy certain trace or power/non-power conditions. These can often be translated to properties of their minimal polynomials. With that, we prove a new theorem about the number of certain irreducible factors of a class of linearized polynomials, which gives a new context to a recent paper by Granger.

papers.title: Multiple SLEs and Dyson Brownian motion: transition density and Green's function
papers.authors: Chongzhi Huang, Hao Wu, Lu Yang
papers.abstract: We consider multiple chordal Schramm-Loewner evolution (SLE) with $\kappa\in (0,4]$. Under common-time parameterization, we show that the transition density of the driving function of multiple chordal SLEs can be given by the transition density of Dyson Brownian motion and Green's function. This is a companion paper of [FWY24].

papers.title: Optimal Clustering of Multi-layer Networks under Mixture Block Models
papers.authors: Zhongyuan Lyu, Ting Li, Dong Xia
papers.abstract: We study clustering for multi-layer networks, where each observation is an undirected network measured on the same set of vertices. Under the mixture multi-layer stochastic block model (MMSBM), each network is generated from one of two stochastic block models, and the goal is to recover the latent network labels. We establish the minimax optimal network clustering error rate, which takes an exponential form and is characterized by the Chernoff information between the edge probability distributions of the component networks. We propose a novel two-stage estimator that combines tensor-based initialization, node and sample splitting, and a likelihood-based refinement. The refinement step exploits estimated node communities and achieves the minimax rate with high probability under extreme network sparsity. We further extend the likelihood-refinement framework to count-weighted networks through a mixture multi-layer Poisson block model. Numerical studies and two real-data analyses illustrate the finite-sample behavior of the proposed method and its use for both external-label benchmarking and unlabeled exploratory network clustering.

papers.title: Asymptotics of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit
papers.abstract: We study the distribution of the free path length in the periodic Lorentz gas in the Boltzmann-Grad limit. For any unimodular Euclidean lattice and any smooth initial velocity distribution, we establish an asymptotic formula for the distribution function of the free path length with a polynomial rate of convergence. The proof combines the dynamical interpretation of the free path length in terms of expanding translates of horospherical orbits on the space of affine lattices, due to Marklof--Str\"ombergsson, with the effective equidistribution results of Kleinbock--Margulis and Kim. This extends the asymptotic formula of Boca--Zaharescu for the planar case to arbitrary dimension.

papers.title: String attractors and bi-infinite words
papers.authors: Pierre B\'eaur, France Gheeraert, Benjamin Hellouin de Menibus
papers.abstract: String attractors are a combinatorial tool coming from the field of data compression. It is a set of positions within a word which captures an occurrence of every factor. While one-sided infinite words admitting a finite string attractor are eventually periodic, the situation is different for two-sided infinite words. In this article, we characterise the bi-infinite words admitting a finite string attractor as the eventually periodic words, the characteristic Sturmian words and their morphic images. For words that do not admit finite string attractors, we study the structure and properties of their infinite string attractors.

papers.title: Sampling from Spherical Spin Glasses in Total Variation via Algorithmic Stochastic Localization
papers.authors: Brice Huang, Andrea Montanari, Huy Tuan Pham
papers.abstract:
We consider the problem of algorithmically sampling from the Gibbs measure of a mixed $p$-spin spherical spin glass. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that samples from the Gibbs measure up to vanishing total variation error, for any model whose mixture satisfies $$
  \xi''(s) < \frac{1}{(1-s)^2}, \qquad \forall s\in [0,1). $$ Our algorithm follows the algorithmic stochastic localization (SL) approach introduced in (Alaoui, Montanari, Sellke, 2022) and in fact achieves a more difficult task. Namely, it (approximately) generates a sample path $({\boldsymbol y}_t)_{t\ge 0}$ from the SL process. For large $T$, ${\boldsymbol y}_T/T$ is an approximate sample from the target Gibbs measure, and hence we solve the original problem as a special case.
  We provide evidence that the condition $\xi''(s) < (1-s)^{-2}$ is sharp for the task of sampling SL sample paths. Furthermore, we prove that it is optimal within a class of generalized SL processes. Remarkably this threshold is close to the conjectured threshold for sampling from the original Gibbs measure. In particular, for the pure $p$-spin glasses it is within an absolute ($p$-independent) constant of the so-called shattering phase transition. Earlier work on related models was suboptimal by a factor diverging polynomially in $p$.
  A key step of this approach is to estimate the mean of a sequence of tilted measures. We produce an improved estimator for this task by identifying a suitable correction to the TAP fixed point selected by approximate message passing (AMP). As a consequence, we improve the algorithm's guarantee over previous work, from normalized Wasserstein to total variation error. In particular, the new algorithm and analysis open the way to perform inference about one-dimensional projections of the measure.

papers.title: Mean-field limit of non-exchangeable multi-agent systems over hypergraphs with unbounded rank
papers.authors: Nathalie Ayi (SU), Nastassia Pouradier Duteil (MAMBA, MUSCLEES), David Poyato (UGR)
papers.abstract: Interacting particle systems are known for their ability to generate large-scale self-organized structures from simple local interaction rules between each agent and its neighbors. In addition to studying their emergent behavior, a main focus of the mathematical community has been concentrated on deriving their large-population limit. In particular, the mean-field limit consists of describing the limit system by its population density in the product space of positions and labels. The strategy to derive such limits is often based on a careful combination of methods ranging from analysis of PDEs and stochastic analysis, to kinetic equations and graph theory. In this article, we focus on a generalization of multi-agent systems that includes higher-order interactions, which has largely captured the attention of the applied community in the last years. In such models, interactions between individuals are no longer assumed to be binary (i.e. between a pair of particles). Instead, individuals are allowed to interact by groups so that a full group jointly generates a non-linear force on any given individual. The underlying graph of connections is then replaced by a hypergraph, which we assume to be dense, but possibly non uniform and of unbounded rank. For the first time in the literature, we show that when the interaction kernels are regular enough, then the mean-field limit is determined by a limiting Vlasov-type equation, where the hypergraph limit is encoded by a so-called UR-hypergraphon (unbounded-rank hypergraphon), and where the resulting mean-field force admits infinitely-many orders of interactions.

papers.title: The linearized Israel-Stewart equations with a physical vacuum boundary
papers.abstract: In this article, we consider the Israel-Stewart equations of relativistic viscous fluid dynamics with bulk viscosity. We investigate the evolution of the equations linearized about solutions that satisfy the physical vacuum boundary condition and establish local well-posedness of the corresponding Cauchy problem.

papers.title: Spherical growth of reciprocal classes in the Hecke Groups
papers.abstract:
Let $r \in \mathbb{Z}$, $r>2$, and let $\Gamma_{2r} \cong (\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}) \ast (\mathbb{Z}/2r\mathbb{Z})$ be the Hecke group. Let $\mathcal{N}_\ell$ denote the set of conjugacy classes of reciprocal elements with cyclically reduced word length exactly $\ell$ in the standard generating set of $\Gamma_{2r}$.
  Let $P(x)$ be the polynomial \[ P(x) = x^{r+1} - 2\sum_{i=1}^{r-1} x^{i} - 1. \] Let $\rho$ be the unique positive root of $P$ and $C$ be a constant depending on $r.$ We prove that, as $\ell \to \infty$, \[|\mathcal{N}_\ell| \sim C\rho^{\left\lfloor \tfrac{\ell+1}{2} \right\rfloor}. \]
  Our approach exploits the free product structure of $\Gamma_{2r}$, together with a combinatorial counting function and recurrence relations arising from cyclically reduced representatives. We further show that the asymptotic growth rate of primitive reciprocal conjugacy classes of word length $\ell$ coincides with that of $\mathcal{N}_\ell$.
  This result extends previous work for odd values of $p$ and provides a uniform asymptotic bound for all Hecke groups.

papers.title: Counting stringy points on a family of character varieties
papers.abstract: We provide explicit formulas for the number of stringy points over finite fields of parabolic type A character varieties with generic semisimple monodromy. This leads to formulas for their stringy E-polynomials. In particular, they satisfy the Betti Topological Mirror Symmetry Conjecture of T. Hausel and M. Thaddeus and a refinement regarding isotypic components. Our proof is based on a Frobenius-type formula for Clifford-type settings and an analysis of it in a specific set-up related to regular wreath products with cyclic groups.

papers.title: Relative Trace Formula And Simultaneous Nonvanishing for GL_3 x GL_2 and GL_3 x GL_1 L-functions
papers.authors: Philippe Michel, Dinakar Ramakrishnan, Liyang Yang
papers.abstract: Fix a Dirichlet character $\chi$ and a cuspidal GL$(2)$ eigenform $\phi$ with relatively prime conductors. Then we show that there are infinitely many cusp forms $\pi$ on GL$(3)$ such that $L(1/2, \pi \times \chi)$ and $L(1/2, \pi \times \phi)$ are simultaneously non-zero. We achieve this by use of Jacquet's Relative Trace Formula. We derive an expression of the average over the GL$(3)$ cuspidal spectrum as a sum of a non-zero main term and two subsidiary terms which are forced to be zero for large enough level by use of a suitable test function. This modest article is dedicated to the memory of Harish Chandra, on the occasion of his hundredth birthday.

papers.title: The smallest singular value for rectangular random matrices with L\'evy entries
papers.abstract:
Let $X=(x_{ij})\in\mathbb{R}^{N\times n}$ be a rectangular random matrix with i.i.d. entries (we assume $N/n\to\mathbf{a}>1$), and denote by $\sigma_{min}(X)$ its smallest singular value. When entries have mean zero and unit second moment, the celebrated work of Bai-Yin and Tikhomirov show that $n^{-\frac{1}{2}}\sigma_{min}(X)$ converges almost surely to $\sqrt{\mathbf{a}}-1.$ However, little is known when the second moment is infinite. In this work we consider symmetric entry distributions satisfying $\mathbb{P}(|x_{ij}|>t)\asymp t^{-\alpha}$ for some $\alpha\in(0,2)$, and
  prove that $\sigma_{min}(X)$ can be determined up to a log factor with high probability: for any $D>0$, with probability at least $1-n^{-D}$ we have $$C_1n^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}(\log n)^\frac{2(\alpha-2)}{\alpha}\leq \sigma_{min}(X)\leq C_2n^{\frac{1}{\alpha}}(\log n)^\frac{\alpha-2}{2\alpha}$$ for some constants $C_1,C_2>0$. The upper bound was derived in a recent work of Bao, Lee and Xu \cite{bao2024phase2} but the lower bound is new and answers a problem posed in that paper in a weaker form. This appears to be the first determination of $\sigma_{min}(X)$ in the $\alpha$-stable case with a correct leading order of $n$, as previous anti-concentration arguments only yield lower bound $n^\frac{1}{2}$. The same lower bound holds for $\sigma_{min}(X+B)$ for any fixed rectangular matrix $B$ with no assumption on its operator norm. The case of diverging aspect ratio is also computed.

papers.title: ItsDEAL: Inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithms for weakly convex optimization
papers.abstract: This paper addresses nonconvex optimization problems via a two-level smoothing framework, where the high-order Moreau envelope (HOME) provides a smooth approximation of weakly convex cost functions. We study the differentiability and weak smoothness of HOME. Building on the inexact two-level smoothing optimization framework (ItsOPT), we propose an inexact two-level smoothing descent algorithm (ItsDEAL) by: (i) approximately solving the proximal subproblem to obtain an inexact first-order oracle for HOME at the lower level; and (ii) applying an inexact first-order method at the upper level. We derive computable sufficient conditions for lower-level inexactness, enabling approximate high-order proximal-points to be certified without access to the exact proximal-point or HOME value. In particular, we study a parameter-free H\"olderian inexact gradient method and an inexact descent method with Armijo line search, both exploiting the weak smoothness of HOME. We establish subsequential convergence under mild inexactness assumptions, and global and linear convergence under the Kurdyka--{\L}ojasiewicz (KL) property. Preliminary experiments on ridge-regularized hinge-loss classification, a high-dimensional MCP-regularized classification model, and robust matrix completion illustrate the numerical behavior of the proposed methods and the role of the HOME order.

papers.title: On the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb B_{\operatorname{dR}}$
papers.abstract: We investigate $p$-adic cohomologies of log rigid analytic varieties over a $p$-adic field. For a log rigid analytic variety $X$ defined over a discretely valued field, we compute the Kummer pro-\'etale cohomology of $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$ and $\mathbb{B}_{\mathrm{dR}}$. When $X$ is defined over $\mathbb{C}_p$, we introduce a logarithmic ${B}_{\mathrm{dR}}^+$-cohomology theory, serving as a deformation of log de Rham cohomology. Additionally, we establish the log de Rham-\'etale comparison in this setting and prove the degeneration of both the Hodge-Tate and Hodge-log de Rham spectral sequences when $X$ is proper and log smooth.

papers.title: Strategic timing of arrivals to a queueing system with scheduled customers
papers.authors: Wathsala Karunarathne, Camiel Koopmans, Jiesen Wang
papers.abstract: This paper examines a single-server queueing system that serves both scheduled and strategic walk-in customers. The service discipline follows a first-come, first-served policy, with scheduled customers granted non-preemptive priority. Each walk-in customer strategically chooses their arrival time to minimise their expected waiting time, taking into account the reservation schedule and the decisions of other walk-in customers. We derive the Nash equilibrium arrival distribution for walk-in customers. We also study the case where early arrivals are allowed and analyse its impact on equilibrium arrival patterns. By analysing various appointment schedules, we assess their effects on equilibrium arrival behaviour, waiting times, and server idle time. Finally, we compare different scheduling policies and evaluate their impact on overall system performance.

papers.title: Approximating Kemeny's constant via spectral sparsification
papers.authors: Aida Abiad, \'Angeles Carmona, Andr\'es M. Encinas, Maria Jos\'e Jim\'enez, \'Alvaro Samperio
papers.abstract: Kemeny's constant of a network quantifies the expected time for a random walk to reach a target vertex chosen according to the stationary distribution, independently of the starting vertex. The purpose of this work is twofold. First, we introduce the class of slightly regular networks, whose orthogonal degree vector is an eigenvector of the Laplacian, and derive an exact expression for Kemeny's constant for this class, extending previous results beyond regular networks. Second, we address the efficient approximation of Kemeny's constant using spectral sparsification. We establish multiplicative bounds relating Kemeny's constant of a network to that of any of its spectral sparsifiers, and use these bounds to design an approximation algorithm. While standard exact approaches based on a full spectral decomposition or on the computation of a pseudoinverse have $O(n^3)$ complexity, our method has complexity $O(n^2\log^{1+o(1)}n)$ for fixed approximation parameters, and is therefore nearly quadratic in the number of vertices even for dense networks.

papers.title: On conservative algebras of 2-dimensional Algebras
papers.abstract: In 1990 Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In case $n >1$ the algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ does not belong to well known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, Leibniz algebras). We describe $\frac{1}{2}$derivations, local (resp. $2$-local) $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations of $\mathcal{W}(2)$. We also study similar problems for the algebra $\mathcal{W}_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $\mathcal{S}_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.

papers.title: Minimal Surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with Three Planar Ends I: Holomorphicity and Uniqueness
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complete minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with three embedded planar ends parallel to those of the union of the Lagrangian catenoid and the plane containing its waist circle. We show that any complete, oriented, immersed minimal surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ with finite total curvature and genus $1$, and having these three ends, must be $J$-holomorphic for some almost complex structure $J$. If the surface is also embedded and has at least $8$ symmetries, we prove that its symmetry group has order $8$ or $12$. In each case the surface is uniquely determined up to scaling and rigid motion.

papers.title: Singular walks in the quarter plane and Bernoulli numbers
papers.authors: Alin Bostan, Lucia Di Vizio, Kilian Raschel
papers.abstract: We consider singular (aka genus $0$) walks in the quarter plane and their associated generating functions $Q(x,y,t)$, which enumerate the walks starting from the origin, of fixed endpoint (encoded by the spatial variables $x$ and $y$) and of fixed length (encoded by the time variable $t$). We first prove that the previous series can be extended up to a universal value of $t$ (in the sense that this holds for all singular models), namely $t=\frac{1}{2}$, and we provide a probabilistic interpretation of $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$. As a second step, we refine earlier results in the literature and show that $Q(x,y,t)$ is indeed differentially transcendental for any $t\in(0,\frac{1}{2}]$. Moreover, we prove that $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$ is strongly differentially transcendental. As a last step, we show that for certain models the series expansion of $Q(x,y,\frac{1}{2})$ is directly related to Bernoulli numbers. This provides a second proof of its strong differential transcendence.

papers.title: An Intersection Product for the Polytope Algebra
papers.abstract: We introduce a new multiplication for the polytope algebra, defined via the intersection of polytopes. After establishing the foundational properties of this intersection product, we investigate finite-dimensional subalgebras that arise naturally from this construction. These subalgebras can be regarded as volumetric analogues of the graded M\"obius algebra, which appears in the context of the Dowling--Wilson conjecture. We conjecture that they also satisfy the injective hard Lefschetz property and the Hodge--Riemann relations, and we prove these in degree one.

papers.title: The Sch\"utzenberger involution and colored lattice models
papers.authors: Henrik P. A. Gustafsson, Carl Westerlund
papers.abstract:
Colored lattice models can be used to describe many different types of special functions of interest in both algebraic combinatorics and representation theory, for example Schur polynomials, nonsymmetric Macdonald polynomials, and characters and Whittaker functions for representations of p-adic groups. A notable example is the metaplectic ice model of which there are actually two different variants: a Gamma and a Delta variant. These variants differ in key aspects but surprisingly produce equal partition functions, which are weighted sums over admissible configurations, and this equality is called the Gamma-Delta duality. The duality was used to prove the analytic continuation of certain multiple Dirichlet series and is highly non-trivial, especially since the number of configurations on each side of the equality can differ.
  In this paper we generalize the Gamma-Delta duality by constructing a new family of solvable, colored lattice models and prove that they are dual to existing lattice models in the literature. Besides the above metaplectic case we also get a new lattice model and Gamma-Delta type duality for (non-metaplectic) Iwahori Whittaker functions together with a crystal limit for Demazure atoms for Cartan type A. The equality of partition functions is shown using Yang-Baxter equations involving both variants of lattice models simultaneously.
  For the crystal lattice model we show that the duality refines to a weight-respecting bijection of states given by the Sch\"utzenberger involution on the associated Gelfand-Tsetlin patterns or semistandard Young tableaux. We also show how the individual steps exchanging two rows in the proof of the duality for the partition functions refines to Berenstein-Kirillov or, equivalently, Bender-Knuth involutions.

papers.title: Ultraproducts of crossed product C*algebras
papers.abstract: We study the relationship between the ultraproduct of a crossed product C*algebra $(A\rtimes_{r}G)^{\omega}$ and the crossed product of an ultraproduct C*algebra $A^{\omega}\rtimes _{r}G$ for a fixed free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb{N}$.

papers.title: A partial result towards the Chowla--Milnor conjecture
papers.abstract: The Chowla--Milnor conjecture predicts the linear independence of certain Hurwitz zeta values. In this paper, we prove that for any fixed integer $k \geqslant 2$, the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}$-linear span of $\zeta(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q)$ ($1 \leqslant a < q/2$, $\gcd(a,q)=1$) is at least $(c -o(1)) \cdot \log q$ as the positive integer $q \to +\infty$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. It is well known that $\zeta(k,a/q)+(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q) \in \overline{\mathbb{Q}}\pi^k$, but much less is known previously for $\zeta(k,a/q)-(-1)^{k}\zeta(k,1-a/q)$. Our proof is similar to those of Ball--Rivoal (2001) and Zudilin (2002) concerning the linear independence of Riemann zeta values. However, we use a new type of rational functions to construct linear forms.

papers.title: Restricted (2+1)-TQFTs supported by thickened and solid tori
papers.authors: Du\v{s}an {\DJ}or{\dj}evi\'c, Danica Kosanovi\'c, Jovana Nikoli\'c, Zoran Petri\'c
papers.abstract: A faithful $(1+1)$ TQFT has recently been constructed, but the existence of a faithful $(2+1)$ TQFT remains an open question, that subsumes the hard problem of linearity of mapping class groups of surfaces. To circumvent the latter problem we construct a subcategory of the category of 3-cobordisms, containing disjoint unions of tori and simplest cobordisms between them. On this we define TQFTs that are able to distinguish pairs of torus bundles and lens spaces, previously shown not to be distinguishable by quantum invariants.

papers.title: Conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states on uniformly hyperbolic sets
papers.authors: Bernat Bassols Cornudella, Matheus M. Castro
papers.abstract: We establish the conditioned stochastic stability of equilibrium states for H\"older potentials on uniformly hyperbolic sets. While standard stochastic stability characterises measures on attractors, we analyse the statistics of transient dynamics on non-attracting sets by conditioning small random perturbations of the dynamics to not escape from our regions of interest. We prove that as the noise intensity vanishes, the quasi-ergodic measure of the $e^\phi$-weighted process generated by $\e$-small random perturbations of the deterministic dynamics converges to the unique equilibrium state associated with the potential $\phi - \log \left|\det \left. D T\right|_{E^u}\right|$. The results are obtained via perturbative spectral analysis of transfer operators acting on anisotropic Banach spaces and topological hyperbolic dynamics arguments. Furthermore, we extend this framework globally to Axiom A diffeomorphisms with multiple basic sets using dynamical filtrations. This work provides a rigorous characterisation of natural measures on uniformly hyperbolic repellers, which are fundamental in the context of transient chaos. Our results have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: Diophantine Equations over $\mathbb Z$: Universal Bounds and Parallel Formalization
papers.authors: Jonas Bayer, Marco David, Malte Hassler, Yuri Matiyasevich, Dierk Schleicher
papers.abstract:
This paper explores multiple closely related themes: bounding the complexity of Diophantine equations over the integers and developing mathematical proofs in parallel with formal theorem provers.
  Hilbert's Tenth Problem (H10) asks about the decidability of Diophantine equations and has been answered negatively by Davis, Putnam, Robinson and Matiyasevich. It is natural to ask for which subclasses of Diophantine equations H10 remains undecidable. Such subclasses can be defined in terms of universal pairs: bounds on the number of variables $
u$ and degree $\delta$ such that all Diophantine equations can be rewritten in at most this complexity. Our work develops explicit universal pairs $(
u, \delta)$ for integer unknowns, focused on reducing the number of unknowns to $
u = 11$. This achieves new bounds that cannot be obtained by naive translations from known results over $\mathbb{N}$.
  In parallel, we have conducted a formal verification of our results using the proof assistant Isabelle. While formal proof verification has traditionally been applied a posteriori to known results, this project integrates formalization into the discovery and development process. In a final section, we describe key insights gained from this approach and its implications for mathematical practice. Our work contributes both to the study of Diophantine equations and to the broader question of how mathematics is conducted in the 21st century.

papers.title: Convergence of the Birkhoff spectrum for nonintegrable observables
papers.authors: Godofredo Iommi, Mike Todd, Boyuan Zhao
papers.abstract: We consider interval maps with countably many full branches and observables with polynomial tails. We show that the Birkhoff spectrum is real analytic and that its convergence to the Hausdorff dimension of the repeller is governed by the polynomial tail exponent. This result extends previous work by Arima on more regular observables and demonstrates how the tail behaviour influences the structure of the Birkhoff spectrum. Our proof relies on techniques from thermodynamic formalism and tail estimates for the observable and our applications are to natural observations on Gauss maps, L\"uroth transformations as well as to a the first return time for a class of induced Manneville-Pomeau maps.

papers.title: On the Gradient Domination of the LQG Problem
papers.authors: Kasra Fallah, Leonardo F. Toso, James Anderson
papers.abstract: We consider solutions to the linear quadratic Gaussian (LQG) regulator problem via policy gradient (PG) methods. Although PG methods have demonstrated strong theoretical guarantees in solving the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem, despite its nonconvex landscape, their theoretical understanding in the LQG setting remains limited. Notably, the LQG problem lacks gradient dominance in the classical parameterization, i.e., with a dynamic controller, which hinders global convergence guarantees. In this work, we study a PG method for the LQG problem by adopting an alternative parameterization of the set of stabilizing controllers and employing a lifting argument. We refer to this parameterization as a history representation of the control input as it is parameterized by past input and output data from the previous p time-steps. Under this parameterization, the infinite-history LQG optimization reduces to an equivalent static state-feedback LQR problem, allowing us to recover gradient dominance and smoothness. For finite history length p, we establish model-based and model-free convergence guarantees up to a geometrically decaying history-truncation error.

papers.title: Formal models for relative adic spaces
papers.abstract: We extend Raynaud's theory of formal models from rigid-analytic spaces over a nonarchimedean field to uniform qcqs adic spaces $X$, with no finite-type assumptions, over an arbitrary Tate affinoid base $S$. The key new ingredient is the notion of a normalized formal blow-up which takes on the role played by admissible formal blow-ups in the classical theory.

papers.title: Extremal Lyapunov exponents in random and simultaneous dynamics
papers.abstract: In this manuscript, we consider finitely many maps, all of which are defined on a compact probability space, with at least one map in the collection having degree strictly bigger than 1. Working with two different, however related, dynamics generated by this setting, we obtain an expression for the extremal Lyapunov exponents, that characterise the instability of typical orbits, as the limit of the averages of the logarithm of the operator norm of linear cocycles of generic orbits. We obtain this as a consequence to the Kingman's ergodic theorem for a subadditive sequence of measurable functions, which naturally generalises the Birkhoff's ergodic theorem, in each of the cases.
