papers.title: Semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf II: the Ran space version
papers.abstract: This paper is a sequel to arXiv:2310.0638. Let G be a split reductive group. We define the parabolic semi-infinite category on the Ran version of the affine Grassmanian Gr_{G,Ran}. We study the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf in this category. We provide several descriptions of this object, one as certain colimit, another as an intermediate extension in certain category. We relate the global and local semi-infinite categories of sheaves. We also relate the intersection cohomology sheaf of the Drinfeld compactification of Bun_P with the semi-infinite parabolic IC-sheaf.

papers.title: Remarks on Derivations on Maximal Triangular Operator Algebras
papers.abstract:
This note concerns bounded derivations on maximal triangular operator algebras on a Hilbert space. Given any bounded derivation $\delta$ on a maximal triangular algebra whose invariant lattice is continuous at 1, an operator which is shown to implement $\delta$ is constructed explicitly. For a general reducible maximal triangular algebra the same construction yields an operator which is shown to implement any $\delta$, if and only if $\delta$ obeys an additional triple product rule.
  This work is based on unpublished parts of the author's dissertation [19] and describes a variant of the proof of a more general result in [21] and is thus in effect a footnote to that work. To the best of the author's knowledge the constructive proof and triple product rule have not appeared elsewhere. The work here is not set in the context of the large body of subsequent research, and no claims are made regarding its relationship to later developments.

papers.title: Multiply Robust Conformal Risk Control with Coarsened Data
papers.authors: Manit Paul, Arun Kumar Kuchibhotla, Eric J. Tchetgen Tchetgen
papers.abstract:
Conformal Prediction (CP) provides prediction sets with formal coverage guarantees, but most existing methods assume fully observed training and calibration data. In many applications, however, outcomes, covariates, or both may be missing or coarsened. We develop a general framework for predictive inference with coarsened data by combining semiparametric theory with conformal methods.
  We introduce two complementary procedures. $(i)$ Robust Split Prediction (RSP) generalizes the doubly robust estimating-equation approach of Yang et al. [2024] beyond the classical missing outcome problem by constructing an efficient influence function based estimating equation and solving its empirical analogue. This yields multiply robust prediction sets under general coarsening patterns. $(ii)$ Robust Split Conformal Prediction (RSCP) instead combines semiparametric theory with conformal risk control. Because efficient influence functions are generally non-monotone in the threshold, we first estimate the target threshold on an independent sample and freeze the threshold-dependent nuisance functions at this preliminary estimate. This restores monotonicity and allows standard conformal risk control arguments to be applied. The resulting coverage guarantees inherit the higher-order mixed-bias structure of the influence function. We develop the theory for classical, multi-stage monotone, and non-monotone missingness and illustrate the performance of the methods through simulations and a longitudinal rheumatoid-arthritis application.

papers.title: Existence and concentration of multiple solutions for the fractional logarithmic Schr\"odinger-Poisson system via the penalization method
papers.abstract:
We study positive solutions of the fractional logarithmic Schr\"odinger-Poisson system
  \[
  \begin{cases}
  \varepsilon^{2\alpha}(-\Delta)^\alpha u+V(x)u+\phi u=u\log u^2+|u|^{q-2}u, & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^3,
  \varepsilon^{2\alpha}(-\Delta)^\alpha \phi=u^2, & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^3,
  \end{cases}
  \]
  where \(\varepsilon>0\), \(3/4<\alpha<1\), and \(4<q<6/(3-2\alpha)\). We assume that the potential is continuous and nonnegative and attains its global minimum inside a bounded domain, with strictly larger values on the boundary. We work in the intersection of a weighted fractional Sobolev space and an Orlicz space, so that the logarithmic energy is finite and the associated functional is of class \(C^1\). For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\), we obtain at least as many distinct positive solutions as the relative Lusternik-Schnirelmann category of the minimum set in a small neighborhood. The global maximum points of these solutions approach that minimum set as \(\varepsilon\to0\). The proof combines penalization, an autonomous Nehari-Pohozaev argument, a local natural constraint, and category theory.

papers.title: Polynomial Transformations of Jacobi Matrices, Matrix valued Orthogonal polynomials and Random Walks
papers.authors: P. Roman, S. Menchon, Y. Yin
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study matrix valued orthogonal polynomials whose block Jacobi matrix is $\Theta(J)$, viewed in blocks of size $m=\deg\Theta$, where $J$ is a tridiagonal Jacobi matrix and $\Theta$ is a scalar polynomial. We identify their matrix measure of orthogonality intrinsically as the push-forward, under $\Theta$, of a matrix measure constructed from the original scalar orthogonal polynomials. We formulate reducibility in the push-forward variable and prove that the $2\times2$ Hermite family associated with $\Theta(x)=x^2+\alpha_1x$ is irreducible for $\alpha_1\neq0$ and reducible for $\alpha_1=0$. This problem is motivated by random walks with transition matrix $\Theta(J)$. For these models, we derive scalar and block Karlin--McGregor representations for the powers of $\Theta(J)$. We apply the construction to the mixed one- and two-ball Ehrenfest chain, obtaining explicit spectral measures, spectral multiplicities, and transition formulas, and we conclude with the corresponding $k$-ball and multi-ball extensions.

papers.title: Inverse Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials of matroids under deletion
papers.authors: Tom Braden, Luis Ferroni, Jacob P. Matherne, Nutan Nepal
papers.abstract: We provide a deletion formula for the inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomial and the inverse $Z$-polynomial of a matroid. Our formulas provide analogues to the deletion formulas of Braden--Vysogorets for Kazhdan--Lusztig and $Z$-polynomials. We discuss several consequences, which include closed formulas and recursions for these invariants on uniform matroids, projective geometries, glued cycles, and arbitrary matroids of corank $2$. As a relevant application of our deletion formula, we show the existence of a matroid of rank $19$ which disproves a conjecture of Xie and Zhang concerning a real-rootedness property of inverse Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

papers.title: Gamma Convergence and Smooth Exact-segregation Approximation for Partially Segregated Systems
papers.abstract: We study three-component Dirichlet energies subject to the partial segregation constraint \(u_1u_2u_3=0\). Our main result is a smooth approximation theorem on bounded Lipschitz domains in arbitrary dimension. For compatible nonnegative Lipschitz boundary data, every admissible \(H^1\) configuration can be approximated strongly in \(H^1\) by globally Lipschitz maps that are smooth in the interior and preserve both the prescribed boundary trace and the segregation constraint exactly. The construction combines a Lipschitz retraction, variable-radius mollification, and smooth truncation preserving existing zeros, without assumptions on interfaces or junctions. Under the weaker assumption of compatible nonnegative \(H^{1/2}\) boundary data, we establish existence of minimizers and \(\Gamma\)-convergence in \(L^2\) for the energies with product penalization \(\varepsilon^{-1}\int_\Omega(u_1u_2u_3)^2\,dx\). We also identify the exact \(L^2\) distance to the constrained class and construct segregated corrections with controlled Dirichlet energy. The resulting correction estimate has order \(\varepsilon^{1/6}\) for bounded-energy configurations; this exponent is sharp in general and improves to \(o(\varepsilon^{1/6})\) for almost-minimizers.

papers.title: Star operation, microscopic sets and porous sets
papers.abstract: This paper explores the interplay between star operations, microscopic sets, and porous sets. The study focuses on the Galvin-Mycielski-Solovay theorem, which characterizes strongly measure zero sets and their interactions with meager sets. Results include the investigation of the star operation $\mathcal{F}^*$ and its properties. The paper also examines the relationship between porous sets and microscopic sets. Additionally, the work presents constructions of families $\mathcal{F}$ in $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}), \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Z}^\omega),$ and $\mathcal{P}(2^\omega)$ that satisfy $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{F}^*$. Theorems and lemmas are provided to establish conditions under which $\mathcal{F}^{**} = \mathcal{F}$ and to analyze the implications of the Borel Conjecture and its dual. The paper concludes with a discussion of microscopic sets and their properties, including their interactions with porous sets and the non-equivalence of certain classes of sets.

papers.title: Representations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and hyperplane complements
papers.abstract: We study faithful realisations of Coxeter groups over fusion rings and study Vinberg systems associated to them. We show that they induce embeddings of hyperplane complements, which provide geometrical realisations of certain types of strong admissible (LCM) homomorphisms between Artin--Tits groups.

papers.title: On The Motivic Leray-Hirsch Theorem For Pure Tate Fibre Bundles
papers.abstract: We prove a Leray-Hirsch theorem for a smooth proper morphism over a smooth integral base whose generic fibre has a pure Tate motive. We further explore and highlight some key applications of this theorem.

papers.title: Age Optimal Sampling and Routing under Intermittent Links and Energy Constraints
papers.authors: Adem Utku Atasayar, Aimin Li, \c{C}a\u{g}r{\i} Ar{\i}, Elif Uysal
papers.abstract: Links in practical systems, such as satellite--terrestrial integrated networks, exhibit distinct delay distributions, intermittent availability, and heterogeneous energy costs. These characteristics pose significant challenges to maintaining timely and energy-efficient status updates. While link availability restricts feasible transmission routes, routing decisions determine the actual delay and energy expenditure. This paper tackles these challenges by jointly optimizing sampling and routing decisions to minimize monotonic, non-linear Age of Information (AoI). The proposed formulation incorporates key system features, including multiple routes with correlated random delays, stochastic link availability, and route-dependent energy consumption. We model the problem as an infinite-horizon Constrained Semi-Markov Decision Process (CSMDP) with a hybrid state--action space and develop an efficient nested algorithm, termed Bisec-\textsc{ReaVI}, to solve this problem. We analyze the structural properties of the solution and reveal a well-defined jointly optimal policy structure: (i) For general monotonic penalty functions, the optimal sampling policy is a piecewise linear waiting policy with at most $N$ breakpoints given $N$ routes; and (ii) under a derived Expected Penalty Ordering condition, the optimal routing policy is a monotonic threshold-based handover policy characterized by at most $\binom{N}{2}$ thresholds. Numerical experiments in a \textit{satellite--terrestrial} integrated routing scenario demonstrate that the proposed scheme efficiently balances energy usage and information freshness, and reveal a counter-intuitive insight: \textit{even routes with higher average delay, higher delay variance or lower availability can still play a critical role in minimizing monotonic functions of AoI}.

papers.title: Bayesian Ambiguity Contraction-based Adaptive Robust Markov Decision Processes for Adversarial Surveillance Missions
papers.abstract: Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCAs) are envisioned to enable autonomous Intelligence, Surveillance, and Reconnaissance (ISR) missions in contested environments, where adversaries may act strategically to deceive or evade detection. These missions pose challenges due to model uncertainty and the need for safe, real-time decision-making. Robust Markov Decision Processes (RMDPs) provide worst-case guarantees but are limited by static ambiguity sets that capture initial uncertainty without adapting to new observations. This paper presents an adaptive RMDP framework tailored to ISR missions with CCAs. We introduce a mission-specific formulation in which the CCA alternates between movement and sensing states. Adversarial uncertainty is represented by finite threat prototypes defining observation, exposure, and state-action transition models. Our approach incrementally refines policies by eliminating inconsistent threat models, allowing the CCA to move from worst-case protection toward more efficient mission policies while maintaining robustness. We establish fixed point stability, agreement with nominal planning as credible sets identify the true node-specific threat prototypes, and a conservative expected value guarantee while those prototypes remain credible. Experiments under Gaussian and non-Gaussian threat models across diverse network topologies show higher mission rewards and fewer exposure events compared to nominal and static robust planners.

papers.title: Hilbert's Basis Theorem for generalized nonassociative Ore extensions
papers.abstract: We introduce a broader class of nonassociative Ore extensions that unifies and generalizes several earlier constructions, taking subadditivity of polynomial degree under multiplication as a guiding principle. We prove generalizations of Hilbert's Basis Theorem for this class, showing that left and right Noetherianity follow from corresponding degree-reduction properties. Applications include flipped nonassociative Ore extensions, mutations, cochain twists, and depolarizations of Poisson Ore extensions.

papers.title: OFF Newton-type Methods for Unconstrained Optimization with Inexact Derivatives
papers.abstract: We study objective-function-free (OFF) Newton-type methods for smooth unconstrained optimization with inexact gradients and Hessians. We propose two methods for first- and second-order stationarity, coupling explicit step-size rules with derivative-accuracy and linear-solver residual conditions to guarantee sufficient decrease without evaluating the objective function. The OFF regularized Newton method finds an $\varepsilon$-first-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations. Under strong convexity, a local Newton variant converges with \(Q\)-order at least $1+\theta$, where \(\theta \in (0, 1]\). For second-order stationarity, we combine regularized Newton steps with approximate eigenvectors associated with the minimum eigenvalue. With high probability, the resulting method finds an $(\varepsilon, \sqrt{L_h\varepsilon})$-second-order stationary point in $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ iterations, using a total of $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/4})$ approximate gradient evaluations and Hessian-vector products. For finite-sum problems, we develop subsampling schemes that yield best-iterate convergence in expectation in the nonconvex first-order setting and local \(R\)-linear convergence with high probability in the strongly convex setting, followed by \(Q\)-order at least \(1+\theta\) once full sampling is reached. The subsampled second-order method achieves a high-probability $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ total sample-operation bound, counting component gradient evaluations and component Hessian-vector products.

papers.title: Space-time bounds for the stirring process with births and deaths
papers.authors: Panagiota Birmpa, Patr\'icia Gon\c{c}alves, Dimitrios Tsagkarogiannis
papers.abstract: We consider a one-dimensional symmetric simple exclusion process on the segment $\{-N,\ldots,N\}$, coupled to boundary dynamics that inject particles from the right reservoir and remove particles from the left reservoir, each acting on a window of size $K$. We derive sharp bounds on the space and space-time $v$-functions of arbitrary degree associated with the centered occupation variables. In particular, we establish bounds of order $N^{-1+2\zeta}$ for spatial $v$-functions of degrees $1$ and $2$, of order $N^{-1}$ for degrees $3,\ldots,K$, and of order $N^{-1-\zeta}$ for degrees at least $K+1$, for some sufficiently small $\zeta>0$. For space-time $v$-functions, we obtain bounds of order $N^{-1}$ for total degrees $2$ and $3$, together with improved bounds for higher degrees, incorporating the dependence on the time separation. These estimates provide the quantitative control needed to study the non-equilibrium fluctuations of the model.

papers.title: High-dimensional normal approximations for sums of Langevin Markov chains
papers.authors: Tian Shen, Zhonggen Su, Xiaolin Wang
papers.abstract:
Consider the well-known Langevin diffusion on $\mathbb{R}^d$ $$\mathrm{d} X_t = -\nabla U(X_t)\,\mathrm{d} t + \sqrt{2}\mathrm{d} B_t, $$ and its Euler-Maruyama discretization given by $$X_{k+1}=X_k-\eta \nabla U(X_k)+\sqrt{2\eta }\xi_{k+1},$$ where $\eta$ is the step size. Under mild conditions, the Langevin diffusion admits $\pi(\mathrm{d} x)\propto \exp(-U(x))\mathrm{d} x$ as its unique stationary distribution.
  In this paper, we mainly study the normal approximation of the normalized partial sum $$ W_n = \eta^{1/2} n^{-1/2} \left( \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i- \int_{\mathbb{R}^d} x\,\pi(\mathrm{d} x) \right).$$ To the best of our knowledge, this work provides the first dimension-explicit convergence rates in high-dimensional settings. Our main tool is a novel upper bound for the 1-Wasserstein distance $W_1(W,\gamma)$ via the exchange pair approach, where $W$ is any random vector of interest and $\gamma$ is a $d$-dimensional standard normal random vector.

papers.title: A modern perspective on Tutte's homotopy theorem
papers.authors: Matthew Baker, Tong Jin, Oliver Lorscheid
papers.abstract:
We begin with a review of Tutte's homotopy theory, which concerns the structure of a certain graph associated to a matroid (together with some extra data). Concretely, Tutte's path theorem asserts that this graph is connected, and his homotopy theorem asserts that every cycle in the graph is a composition of ``elementary cycles'', which come in four different flavors. We present an extended version of the homotopy theorem, in which we give a more refined classification of the different types of elementary cycles. We explain in detail how the path theorem allows one to prove that the foundation of a matroid (in the sense of Baker--Lorscheid) is generated by universal cross-ratios, and how the extended homotopy theorem allows one to classify all algebraic relations between universal cross-ratios. The resulting ``fundamental presentation'' of the foundation was previously established in [Baker--Lorscheid], but the argument here is more self-contained. We then recall a few applications of the fundamental presentation to the representation theory of matroids. Finally, in the most novel but also the most speculative part of the paper, we discuss what a ``higher Tutte homotopy theorem'' might look like, and we present some preliminary computations along these lines.
  The appendices include modern language translations of Tutte's proofs of the path theorem and the homotopy theorem (the latter is a contribution by Ju\v{s} Kocutar).

papers.title: Local Models for Special K\"ahler Metric Singularities Along the Discriminant Locus of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Hitchin Base
papers.authors: Zhenxi Huang, Shuo Wang, Bin Xu
papers.abstract: Freed (arXiv:hep-th/9712042) formulated the theory of special K\"ahler structures. In particular, the regular part of the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ Hitchin base $\mathcal{B}$ carries such a structure, and the associated metric $\omega_{\mathrm{SK}}$ develops singularities near the discriminant locus $\mathcal{D}\subset\mathcal{B}$. Baraglia--Huang (arXiv:1707.04975) showed that its Taylor expansion at regular points can be computed by topological recursion, and Hitchin (arXiv:1712.09928) later constructed integrable subsystems over smooth strata of $\mathcal{D}$ parametrizing spectral curves with only nodal singularities; these strata carry induced special K\"ahler structures. We show that near such strata, the special K\"ahler metric on $\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{D}$ exhibits logarithmic asymptotics in transverse directions, whereas its tangential part converges to a metric on the stratum that agrees with the one induced by Hitchin's subsystems. We also prove that the induced metric on every radial complex line through the origin and a point of such a stratum is flat with cone angle $\pi$ at the origin.

papers.title: Dynamics of Interfaces in the Two-Dimensional Wave-Pinning Model
papers.authors: Shunsuke Kobayashi, Koya Sakakibara, Taikei Uechi
papers.abstract: We study the mass-conserved reaction-diffusion system known as the wave-pinning model, which serves as a minimal framework for describing cell polarity. In this model, the interplay between reaction kinetics and slow diffusion forms a sharp interface that partitions the domain into high- and low-concentration regions. We perform a detailed asymptotic analysis and derive higher-order approximation equations governing the motion of this interface. Our results show that on a fast timescale, the interface evolves via propagating front dynamics, whereas on a slow timescale, it evolves as an area-preserving mean curvature flow. Furthermore, using the derived free boundary problem, we demonstrate that on a significantly slower timescale, an interface whose endpoints lie on the domain boundary drifts along the boundary toward regions of higher curvature. In summary, our analysis reveals that the interface dynamics in the wave-pinning model exhibit a hierarchy of three distinct timescales: wave propagation on a fast timescale, curvature-driven area-preserving evolution on a slow timescale, and motion along the boundary on a significantly slower timescale.

papers.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
papers.authors: Topias Terho, Fabricio Oliveira, Ahti Salo, Pedro Munari
papers.abstract:
Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces.
  The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

papers.title: On the rational points in conics of a cubic surface
papers.abstract: We study rational and integral points lying on finite collections of conics on non-ruled cubic surfaces over a number field. We extend the global determinant method to hypersurfaces in linear subvarieties, retaining dependence on the height of their Cayley forms. The universal Deligne pairing identifies the Chow line bundle on a residual conic pencil with three times of the universal bundle. Uniform bounds for cubic curves then control the number of conics of bounded height and give uniform estimates for their contribution to auxiliary coverings.

papers.title: Translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies
papers.abstract: In a series of papers, Weil initiated the investigation of translation invariant curvature measures of convex bodies, which include as prime examples Federer's curvature measures. In this paper, we continue this line of research by introducing new tools to study curvature measures. Our main results suggest that the space of curvature measures, which is graded by degree and parity, is highly structured: We conjecture that each graded component has length at most $2$ as a representation of the general linear group, and we prove this in degrees $0$ and $n-2$. Beyond this conjectural picture, our methods yield a characterization of Federer's curvature measures under weaker assumptions.

papers.title: On isoperimetric local-Bollob\'as-Thomason inequalities
papers.authors: Luis J. Al\'ias, Bernardo Gonz\'alez Merino, Beatriz Mar\'in Gimeno
papers.abstract: We prove the following isoperimetric-type inequality: for every convex body $K$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and some $\sigma\subset[n]:=\{1,\dots,n\}$ there exists a suitable Hanner polytope $B_K$ with the same volume as $K$ and such that the volume of each of its orthogonal projections onto every subspace whose basis is formed by the canonical vectors $\{e_i:i\in\tau\cup([n]\setminus\sigma)\}$, for every $\tau\subseteq\sigma$, bounds from below the volume of the corresponding projections of $K$.

papers.title: Construction and Decoding of Convolutional Codes with optimal Column Distances
papers.abstract: The construction of Maximum Distance Profile (MDP) convolutional codes in general requires the use of very large finite fields. In contrast convolutional codes with optimal column distances maximize the column distances for a given arbitrary finite field. In this paper, we present a construction of such convolutional codes. In addition, we prove that for the considered parameters the codes that we constructed are the only ones achieving optimal column distances. The structure of the presented convolutional codes with optimal column distances is strongly related to first order Reed-Muller block codes and we leverage this fact to develop a reduced complexity version of the Viterbi algorithm for these codes.

papers.title: Linear systems on blow-ups of Hirzebruch surfaces
papers.abstract: Motivated by various equivalent versions of the SHGH conjecture for $\mathbb P^2$ blown up at very general points, we propose a similar conjecture for Hirzebruch surfaces. We prove that this conjecture is true for the Hirzebruch surface $\mathbb F_e$ blown up at $r\leqslant e+5$ very general points.

papers.title: The Cofinality of Generating Familes
papers.abstract:
The topology of a separable metrizable space $M$ is \emph{generated} by a family $\mathcal{C}$ of its subsets provided that a set $A\subseteq M$ is closed in $M$ if and only if $A\cap C$ is closed in $C$ for each $C\in \mathcal{C}$. The \emph{sequentiality number}, $\mathop{seq}(M)$, and \emph{$k$-ness number}, $\mathop{k}(M)$, of $M$, are the minimum size of a generating family of convergent sequences, respectively compact subsets.
  Let $\mathfrak{b}$ be the minimum size of an unbounded set in $\omega^\omega$ with the mod finite order. For a cardinal $\kappa$, the \emph{covering number}, $\mathop{cov}(\kappa)$, is the minimum size of a family of countable subsets of $\kappa$ so that every countable subset of $\kappa$ is contained in an element of the family. It is shown using the Tukey order on relations that (1) $\mathop{seq}(M)=\mathop{cov}(|M|)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$, unless $M$ is locally small (every point of $M$ has a neighborhood of size strictly less than $|M|$) in which case $\mathop{seq}(M)=\lim_{\mu <|M|} \mathop{cov}(\mu)\cdot \mathfrak{b}$ and (2) $k(M)$ is in the interval $[kc(M)\cdot\mathfrak{b},\mathop{cov}(kc(M))\cdot \mathfrak{b}]$, where $kc(M)$ is the minimum number of compact sets that cover $M$.
  Solutions to problems of van Douwen's on the $k$-ness number of analytic and of co-analytic spaces are deduced.

papers.title: Strong existence for SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
papers.abstract: Let $B^H$ be a $d$-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1/2)$. We prove the existence of a strong solution to $$d X_t=b(t,X_t)d t+d B_t^H, X_0=x_0\in R^d,$$when $b\in L^q([0,T];L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)),2\le p,q<\infty$ and the subcritical Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition $\frac1q+\frac{Hd}{p}<1-H$ is satisfied. Thus, within the finite-exponent range $p,q\ge2$, the strong-existence result covers the full subcritical region, including the regime $p<2Hd$, where a uniform strong Novikov condition may fail. The proof is based on a compactness criterion for Wiener functionals. Its main ingredients are an exponentially quantitative derivative estimate for the finite-dimensional densities of fractional Brownian motion, a conditional moment estimate obtained through a martingale representation of fractional Brownian motion, and a frequency-localized truncation of the Cameron--Martin shift. These estimates yield uniform Malliavin--Sobolev bounds for smooth approximations of the equation.

papers.title: New upper bounds for the period of a negative orientable sequence
papers.authors: Chris J Mitchell, Peter R Wild
papers.abstract: Negative orientable sequences, i.e. periodic sequences with elements from a finite alphabet of size at least three in which an n-tuple or the negative of its reverse appears at most once in a period of the sequence, were introduced by Alhakim et al. in 2024. The main goal in defining them was as a means of generating orientable sequences, which have automatic position location applications, although they are potentially of interest in their own right. In this paper we develop new upper bounds on the period of negative orientable sequences which, for n>2, are significantly sharper than the previous known bound. The approach used to develop the new bounds involves examining the nodes in the subgraph of the de Bruijn graph corresponding to a negative orientable sequence, and to consider the implications of the fact that the in-degree of every vertex in this subgraph must equal the out-degree. However, despite improving the bounds, a gap remains between the largest known period for a negative orientable sequence and the corresponding bounds for every n>2.

papers.title: Sinkhorn Distributionally Robust State Estimation via System Level Synthesis
papers.authors: Yulin Feng, Xianyu Li, Steven X. Ding, Hao Ye, Chao Shang
papers.abstract: In state estimation tasks, the usual assumption of an exactly known disturbance distribution is often unrealistic and renders the estimator fragile in practice. The recently emerging Wasserstein distributionally robust state estimation (DRSE) design can partially mitigate this fragility; however, its worst-case distribution is provably discrete, which deviates from the inherent continuity of real-world distributions and results in over-pessimism. In this work, we develop a new Sinkhorn DRSE design within the system level synthesis scheme with the aim of shaping the closed-loop errors under the unknown continuous disturbance distribution. For uncertainty description, we adopt the Sinkhorn ambiguity set that includes an entropic regularizer to penalize non-smooth and discrete distributions within a Wasserstein ball. We present the first result of finite-sample probabilistic guarantee of the Sinkhorn ambiguity set. Then we analyze the limiting properties of our Sinkhorn DRSE design, thereby highlighting its close connection with the generic $\mathcal{H}_2$ design and Wasserstein DRSE. To tackle the min-max optimization problem, we reformulate it as a finite-dimensional convex program through duality theory. By identifying a compact subset of the feasible set guaranteed to enclose the global optimum, we develop a tailored Frank-Wolfe solution algorithm and formally establish its convergence rate. The advantage of Sinkhorn DRSE over existing design schemes is verified through numerical case studies.

papers.title: The Game-Theoretic Kat\v{e}tov Order and Idealised Effective Subtoposes
papers.abstract:
This paper addresses the longstanding problem of determining the structure of the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order in the Effective Topos, known to effectively embed the Turing degrees. In a surprising discovery, we show that the $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order is in fact tightly controlled by the combinatorics of filters on $\omega$, raising deep questions about how combinatorial and computable complexity interact, both within this order and beyond it.
  To make the connection precise, we introduce a game-theoretic (''gamified'') variant of the Kat\v{e}tov order on filters over $\omega$, which turns out to exhibit a striking mix of coarseness and subtlety. For one, it is strictly coarser than the classical Rudin-Keisler order and, when viewed dually on ideals, collapses all MAD families to a single equivalence class. On the other hand, the order also supports a rich internal structure, including an infinite strictly ascending chain of ideal classes, which we identify by way of a new separation technique.
  From the computability-theoretic perspective, we show that a computable (and extended) variant of the gamified Kat\v{e}tov order is isomorphic to the original $\leq_{\mathrm{LT}}$-order. Moreover, our work brings into focus a new degree-spectrum invariant for filters $\mathcal{F}$, $$\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F}):=\{\,[f\colon\omega\to\omega] \mid f\leq_{\mathrm{LT}} \mathcal{F} \},$$
  which is shown to always determine a proper initial segment of the Turing degrees. Extending this, given any non-principal $\Delta^1_1$ filter $\mathcal{F}$, we show that $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{T}}(\mathcal{F})$ is precisely the class of hyperarithmetic degrees. This significantly generalises previous results obtained by van Oosten \cite{vO14} and Kihara \cite{Kih23}.
  The proofs draw on ideas from general topology, descriptive set theory, and computability theory.

papers.title: Selberg and Brolin on value distribution of complex dynamics
papers.abstract: The Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem for iterated preimages of a given non-exceptional value and Lyubich's periodic point version of it are foundational in the study of dynamics of rational functions of degree more than one on the complex projective line, and Drasin and the author studied a quantification of the former in a formalism of Nevanlinna theory, or more specifically, with the aid of Selberg's theorem from covering theory. In this paper, we point out that the argument in that previous study has already yielded a better quantification of the Brolin-Lyubich-Freire--Lopes--Ma\~n\'e equidistribution theorem, and also point out that a similar argument also yields a quantification of Lyubich's theorem under an exponentwise version of the so called hypothesis H, which has recently been settled by Przytycki for unicritical polynomials. As an application, we sharpen the quantitative results on the value distribution of the (first) derivatives of iterated polynomials.

papers.title: Integer Cantor Sets: Arithmetic Combinatorial Properties
papers.authors: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, Michael T. Lacey, Dario Mena, Maria Carmen Reguera
papers.abstract:
Cantor sets of integers have a rich set of arithmetic combinatorial properties. We consider classical Cantor sets, with a base and a fixed set of allowed digits. For such sets, we (a) give examples of such sets that satisfy the intersective property with power savings
  (b) characterize uniform distribution, (c) establish polynomial mean ergodic theorems and (d) study metric pair correlation of Cantor sets.

papers.title: Capillary minimal slicing and scalar curvature rigidity
papers.abstract: We develop minimal slicing via capillary hypersurfaces to understand scalar curvature metric on manifolds bounded below with boundary. In particular, in dimension $4$, we prove following comparison and rigidity statement: given a compact Riemannian $4$-manifold $(M^4,g)$ with a mean convex boundary whose boundary is diffeomorphic to boundary of a connected convex domain in $\mathbb R^4$, if the scalar curvature is non-negative and the scaled mean curvature comparison holds along the boundary, then $M$ is isometric to the Euclidean domain. Moreover, we prove a comparison and rigidity result of manifolds with Listing type scaling invariant scalar and mean curvature comparison : $R g \ge -12 g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$ and $\hat{H}^{2} g \ge \hat{H}_{0} g_{\mathbb{H}^{4}}$, where $\hat{H}$ is a shifted mean curvature depending on the scale of manifold. This proves the traced version of Gromov's conjecture on comparison and rigidity of hyperbolic convex domains

papers.title: Endpoint variation and jump inequalities for rough singular integrals
papers.abstract: In this article, we prove weak type $(1,1)$ bounds for the variation and jump operators corresponding to the family of truncations of singular integrals with rough kernels. This resolves an open question raised by Jones, Seeger and Wright (Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. (2008)). Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the variational estimate, we recover the weak type $(1,1)$ boundedness of the maximal truncation operator corresponding to singular integrals with rough kernels.

papers.title: Regulator Constants and Cohomology
papers.abstract: We show how regulator constants of a finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}[G]$-module can be related to $G$-cohomology, where $G$ is a finite group. We then derive consequences of such relation for modules naturally arising in number theory, such as ring of integers and units of number fields, $K$-theory groups of ring of integers and Mordell-Weil groups of elliptic curves.

papers.title: GRAND for Gaussian Intersymbol Interference Channels
papers.abstract: Channel decoding is challenging in communication channels exhibiting memory effects. In this work, we extend the recently proposed decoding paradigm of guessing random additive noise decoding (GRAND) to channels with memory, focusing on linear Gaussian intersymbol interference (ISI) channels. To characterize error patterns (EPs) under channel memory, we introduce the concept of error bursts and define sequence reliability to quantify the likelihood of an EP. Based on sequence reliability, we develop soft GRAND for ISI channels, termed SGRAND-ISI, which generalizes SGRAND to linear Gaussian ISI channels and is equivalent to maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding. We then develop ordered reliability bit GRAND (ORBGRAND) variants based on SGRAND-ISI that replace exact sequence reliabilities with rank-based approximations to reduce online computation. The proposed framework is first established for binary-input first-order ISI channels and subsequently extended to higher-order channel memory and higher-order modulation. Numerical experiments over first- and second-order ISI channels show that the proposed algorithms achieve multiple-dB gains over GRAND algorithms that ignore channel memory and can operate within $0.1$-$0.2$ dB of the ML benchmark. Compared with the recently proposed ORBGRAND-Approximate Independence algorithm, CDF-ORBGRAND-ISI provides a gain of at least $0.5$ dB at a block error rate (BLER) of $10^{-3}$. We further evaluate the online decoding complexity of the proposed GRAND-ISI algorithms using a module-wise complexity analysis.

papers.title: Mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and their applications to boundedness of operators
papers.authors: Tengfei Bai, Pengfei Guo, Jingshi Xu
papers.abstract: We introduce the mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and obtain their preduals. The boundedness of Hardy-Littlewood maximal operator, iterated maximal operator, fractional integral operator, singular integral operator on these spaces is proved. In addition, we give a description of the dual of mixed Bourgain-Morrey spaces and conclude the reflexivity of these spaces.

papers.title: A Recognizable Substitution for the Anti-Penrose Tiling
papers.abstract: We present a substitution on six marked rhombs, called Seabed, with inflation factor $\varphi^3$. We prove that its tiling space is mutually locally derivable with the unmarked Anti-Penrose pentagrid hull. Eleven vertex patches of depth at most four recognize the parent vertices: their acceptance domains coincide with the five internally contracted windows. Matching the fine tiles around each parent rhomb to a replacement patch recovers their markings uniquely. The inverse local maps have a uniform finite radius and extend to all singular limit tilings in the hull. The construction also gives a recognizable parent hierarchy.

papers.title: Classification of Smooth Alignable Voss Surfaces
papers.abstract:
Alignable nets are grid structures that can collapse to a planar strip. This property simplifies on-site assembly and enables compact transport and storage. These structures are then deployed by a scissor motion at vertices in a desired location. In this article, we classify all non-developable surfaces supporting an alignable net that additionally have the geodesic-conjugate net property, namely, the alignable Voss surfaces. Using the surface elements and adapted frames, we show that these surfaces arise as rotation fields of either helicoidal pseudospherical surfaces or Amsler surfaces, resulting in two distinct classes.
  The first class consists of helicoidal Voss surfaces. Exploiting this helicoidal structure, we combine a kinematic interpretation with the Bour family to derive explicit immersion formulas depending on the isometric deformation and alignability parameters. Furthermore, we examine several subclasses and an extension of this result in detail. In particular, we study the notable case of infinitely many geodesic-conjugate nets on a helicoid and provide a kinematic explanation for why this phenomenon appears in computations.
  For the second class, we obtain the classification at the level of the fundamental forms and show that they correspond to certain $3$-parameter families of non-helicoidal intrinsic surfaces of revolution. These families are governed by general Painleve III solutions including both regular and nonregular solutions. Finally, a surprising feature of this class is that its members support geodesic isothermal-conjugate nets absent from Eisenhart's classification of the aforementioned nets, thereby identifying a missing case in that classification.

papers.title: On generalized covering radii of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes
papers.abstract: The generalized covering radii (GCR) of linear codes are a fundamental higher-dimensional extension of the classical covering radius. While the second and third GCR of binary primitive double-error-correcting BCH codes, $\text{BCH}(2,m)$, were recently determined, their proofs relied on highly complex combinatorial arguments, and the behavior of the GCR hierarchy for larger orders $k$ has remained largely unexplored. In this paper, we introduce the Generalized Supercode Lemma, which lower-bounds the GCR of a code using the generalized Hamming weights of an appropriate supercode. Applying this lemma, we significantly streamline and simplify the proofs for the known lower bounds of $\rho_2(\text{BCH}(2,m))$ and $\rho_3(\text{BCH}(2,m))$, and we establish a new lower bound for $\rho_4(\text{BCH}(2,m))$. Furthermore, by combining combinatorial arguments with Weil-type exponential sum estimates, we investigate the GCR hierarchy for general $k$, proving that $2k \le \rho_k(\text{BCH}(2,m)) \le 2k+1$ whenever $m$ is sufficiently large compared to $k$.

papers.title: Poly-Bernoulli numbers from shifted log-sine integrals
papers.abstract: In 1999, Arakawa and Kaneko introduced a zeta function connecting multiple zeta values with poly-Bernoulli numbers through its special values. Log-sine integrals are also known to be related to zeta values at positive integers. In this article, we study the values of a shifted log-sine integral at negative integers and establish a connection with anti-diagonal sums of poly-Bernoulli numbers. This gives a refinement of Stephan's observation on the central binomial series.

papers.title: On Stanley-Reisner Rings with Minimal Betti Numbers
papers.abstract: We study simplicial complexes with a given number of vertices whose Stanley-Reisner ring has the minimal sum of Betti numbers. We prove that every full subcomplex of them is homotopy equivalent either to a point or to a sphere. Moreover, we prove that such kind of simplicial complexes coincide with those having minimal Taylor resolutions.

papers.title: Capillary John ellipsoid theorem with applications to capillary curvature problems
papers.authors: Jinrong Hu, Yingxiang Hu, Bo Yang
papers.abstract: In this paper, we apply a capillary John ellipsoid theorem for capillary convex bodies in the Euclidean half-space $\overline{\mathbb{R}^{n+1}_{+}}$. This theorem yields a non-collapsing estimate for capillary hypersurfaces, which provides a new approach to obtaining $C^{0}$ estimates for solutions to some capillary curvature problems (including the capillary $L_{p}$ Christoffel-Minkowski problem and the capillary $L_{p}$ curvature problem), based on the corresponding gradient estimates. As an application, we study the capillary $L_{p}$ dual Minkowski problem. A gradient estimate, together with the non-collapsing estimate and a $C^2$ estimate, yields existence for every $1<p<q<\infty$ with positive smooth even data and an acute contact angle. The same estimates also yield the eigenvalue problem for $p=q>1$, with uniqueness up to dilation. We further obtain existence and uniqueness for $p>q$ without an upper restriction on $q$.

papers.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Mac\'ias Spaces of Integral Domains
papers.abstract: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Mac\'ias space $M(R)$ is the set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ endowed with the topology generated by the subsets $\sigma_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$ for $k\in R^0$. We show that the unit group is open in $M(R)$ precisely when $R$ is not semiprimitive, and characterize semiprimitive Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs) by means of the density of their irreducible and prime elements, respectively. We describe the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ in terms of the maximal ideals of $R$, and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps. Consequently, two local domains have homeomorphic Mac\'ias spaces if and only if they have the same cardinality. We characterize the pairs of Dedekind domains with homeomorphic Mac\'ias spaces in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and the relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals; in particular, two Dedekind domains with torsion class groups, such as principal ideal domains (PIDs), have homeomorphic Mac\'ias spaces if and only if their unit groups have the same cardinality and so do their sets of maximal ideals. This characterization addresses, for countably infinite semiprimitive PIDs, the homeomorphism problem raised by Mac\'ias in 2024. Under an additional hypothesis, UFDs admit an analogous characterization in terms of comaximality with prime elements. Finally, for a class of domains of characteristic zero, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Mac\'ias spaces in terms of isomorphisms of the underlying rings, partially answering a problem raised by Mac\'ias and Ortiz in 2024.

papers.title: Approximation of structures:local and global
papers.abstract: We provide a mathematically rigorous definition of local approximation and demonstrate its applicability to some interesting classes of structures. In particular, we prove that any compact simple Lie group is locally approximated by finite groups. The definition and main examples are motivated by physics but the techniques are of model theory. Namely, we introduce the ultraproduct of emerging metric structures, which generalises the ultraproduct in metric model theory.

papers.title: Caps and LCD Codes with Large Dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish a connection between linear complementary dual (LCD) codes and caps in projective space. Using this framework and the structure theory of maximal binary caps, we derive nonexistence theorems for binary LCD codes with minimum distance at least $4$, providing computation-free proofs that were previously obtained only through exhaustive search. As an application, we completely determine the optimal minimum distances for codimensions $7$ and $8$ for the first time. The framework applies to ternary LCD codes and quaternary Hermitian LCD codes, where it reduces the problem to the structure of large caps. Using known results on large caps, we determine the optimal minimum distances of ternary LCD codes of codimension $6$ for all lengths, and we explain why the phenomena behind the binary nonexistence theorems, such as the dependence on the parity of the length, have no counterpart for these codes.

papers.title: Signless Laplacian spectral radius of simplicial complexes without $r$-dimensional wheels
papers.abstract: An $r$-dimensional wheel is defined as the join of an $(r-2)$-simplex and a cycle. In this paper, we study the maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of $n$-vertex $r$-dimensional pure simplicial complexes that contain no $r$-dimensional wheels. For sufficiently large $n$, we determine the extremal complexes that attain this maximum. Our result generalizes the corresponding extremal results of signless Laplacian on graphs and provides a spectral anlogue of a theorem of Brown, Erd\H{o}s and S\'os on the maximum number of facets of simplicial complexes in the case $r=2$.

papers.title: Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
papers.abstract: We address a short-wave asymptotic for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells or anything else through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization, and something like blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

papers.title: Three-periodic helices on elliptic curves and their associated regular algebras
papers.abstract: Let $k$ denote an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X$ denote a smooth elliptic curve over $k$. Given a three-periodic elliptic helix $\underline{\mathcal{E}}$ of vector bundles over $X$ with endomorphism $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ and quadratic cover $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$, we prove that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ by a degree three family of normal elements, generalizing a result of the authors to the case in which $\operatorname{dim }(\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}})_{i, i+1}$ isn't a constant function of $i$. We then show that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is noetherian if and only if it has polynomial growth, and in this case, the ranks of any three consecutive bundles in the helix are a Markov triple. Furthermore, in this case $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ is a noetherian GK-three $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra which is ${\sf Proj }$-equivalent to an elliptic algebra. We conclude the paper by constructing several new families of elliptic helices with exponential growth.

papers.title: On nonnegative solutions of the differential inequality $\Delta_pu+ \Delta_q u+V(x)u^s\leq 0$ on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: In this paper, we are concerned with differential inequalities with $(p,q)$-Laplacian operator on Riemannian manifolds. Using a test function argument, we establish Liouville-type theorems under the manifold's geometry and the potential's behavior at infinity. Finally, we give an example showing the sharpness when $V(x)$ is a positive constant.

papers.title: Thermodynamic formalism for singular flows
papers.abstract: We prove that $C^\infty$ smooth three-dimensional flows with positive topological entropy admit only finitely many ergodic measures of maximal entropy, even in the presence of singularities (zero-velocity points). Furthermore, for flows in a $C^\infty$-open and dense subset of the space of such three-dimensional flows, every ergodic measure of maximal entropy is rapidly mixing. To prove this result, we construct a novel symbolic coding framework for singular flows, which serves as the fundamental technical tool. We then introduce the property of strong positive recurrence (SPR) for singular flows, and prove that SPR flows can be coded by suspension flows over SPR countable discrete symbolic systems. Under appropriate conditions, we further establish that such suspension flows are rapidly mixing. These frameworks can be further generalized to a broad class of flows, including star flows, and the results naturally extend to general equilibrium states.

papers.title: Fixed-point-free automorphisms of solvable Lie algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of fixed-point-free automorphisms for finite-dimensional Lie algebras. By a result of Jacobson, a Lie algebra admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism is solvable. We prove that such a Lie algebra must be even strongly unimodular. We find a necessary and sufficient criterion such that a complex almost abelian Lie algebra admits a fixed-point-free automorphism. For complex filiform Lie algebras we show that the existence of a fixed-point-free automorphism is equivalent to not being characteristically nilpotent.

papers.title: Hybrid Multiport Receivers for Slow Fluid Antenna Multiple Access
papers.authors: Jos\'e P. Gonz\'alez-Coma, Jos\'e David Vega-S\'anchez, F. Javier L\'opez-Mart\'inez
papers.abstract: We propose a novel receiver architecture that preserves the performance benefits of multiport selection in fluid-antenna systems while requiring only a very small number of radio-frequency (RF) chains. The resulting fluid-antenna hybrid multiport (FAHM) receiver effectively decouples port selection from signal combining by integrating a low-complexity analog combining network similar to those used in conventional hybrid multiantenna designs. We develop an effective-port criterion to determine the selected-port dimension before hybrid combining, thereby limiting the performance loss associated with port selection, and then design the hybrid combiner for a given RF-chain budget. The FAHM architecture is evaluated in a multiuser set-up operating under slow fluid-antenna multiple access (FAMA). In this scenario, a FAHM implementation with only 2 RF chains showcases a performance comparable to a fully-digital conventional multiport scheme with a much larger number of RF chains. Additionally, the proposed Rank-1 implementation attains a reduction in average GEPort execution time by about two orders of magnitude.

papers.title: On weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics
papers.abstract: The notion of weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics extends the classical notion of Calabi's extremal K\"ahler metrics, but includes many well-studied objects in K\"ahler geometry such as K\"ahler-Ricci solitons and Sasaki-Einstein metrics. In this paper, after explaining how this notion grew out, we will try to survey recent works concerning the YTD conjecture on weighted extremal K\"ahler metrics.

papers.title: On $4$-perfect-matching covers of cubic graphs with two adjacent odd circuits in a $2$-factor
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a cubic graph admitting a $2$-factor consisting of exactly two odd circuits, and let the complementary $1$-factor contain precisely three spokes (along with an arbitrary number of chords). We show that four perfect matchings can cover $G$. As a consequence, $G$ fulfils the $7/5$-Conjecture of Alon and Tarsi.

papers.title: Beyond Polynomials: Optimal Locally Recoverable Codes from Good Rational Functions
papers.authors: Hengfeng Liu, Sihem Mesnager, Chunming Tang, Xuemin Zheng
papers.abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) play an important role in distributed and cloud storage systems. The celebrated Tamo--Barg construction of optimal LRCs is based on the notion of \emph{good polynomials}. In this paper, we introduce the notion of \emph{good rational functions} as a natural generalization of good polynomials and develop a more general framework for constructing optimal LRCs. Since the attainable code lengths depend on the number of fibers of maximal size, we study this quantity using algebraic function field theory and Galois theory, identifying it with the number of totally split rational places in the associated function field extension. By analyzing the Galois closure, we establish an exact counting formula and derive sharp upper bounds for the number of ramified places and the genus, leading to explicit lower bounds for the number of totally split rational places. When the extension is Galois, we further characterize the number of totally split rational places in terms of the action of the Galois group on the projective line. Explicit constructions of good rational functions in both Galois and non-Galois settings are also presented. These rational functions yield optimal LRCs with lengths exceeding those attainable from good polynomials of the same degree, demonstrating the advantage of our framework over the classical Tamo--Barg construction.

papers.title: A min-max gap characterization of minimal foliations on the torus
papers.abstract: We extend an energy introduced by Mather to the setting of Almgren-Pitts min-max theory and obtain a parametric, higher-dimensional analogue of Mather's variational barrier theory for twist maps and geodesics on tori. We use this energy to establish several criteria for the existence of foliations of the $n$-torus by minimal hypersurfaces. We show that for a generic metric, whenever a lamination by area-minimizing hypersurfaces of the $n$-torus contains a gap, there exists a minimal hypersurface inside the gap that is not area-minimizing. This hypersurface is a higher-dimensional analogue of the secondary minimax orbit appearing in Aubry-Mather theory.

papers.title: Solutions for Hecke Sum Questions of Banerjee and Bringmann
papers.authors: George E. Andrews, Mohamed El Bachraoui
papers.abstract: We previously conjectured a Hecke-type identity for a series arising from two-color partitions. Banerjee and Bringmann proved the conjecture using modular methods and asked for a direct proof using Bailey pairs. They also suggested investigating the odd part of the series. We answer both questions by applying Bailey's transform to a Bailey pair of Andrews and a conjugate Bailey pair of Lovejoy. Our main theorem gives formulas for the even and odd parts of a series $P_a(q)$ depending on a parameter $a$. The specialization $a=1$ gives the conjectured formula and a companion formula for the odd part.

papers.title: Schur positivity of the nabla operator on two-column modified Hall--Littlewood polynomials
papers.abstract: Bergeron, Garsia, Haiman, and Tesler (1999) introduced two Schur positivity conjectures concerning the action of the $\nabla$ operator on modified Hall--Littlewood polynomials. Although the proofs of the celebrated compositional shuffle conjecture and its rational generalization, along with various symmetric function identities, have largely resolved these conjectures in the affirmative, we provide an elegant alternative proof driven by $q$-series techniques. Through this approach, we derive explicit Schur function expansions for two-column partitions and extend our results to arbitrary positive powers $\nabla^k$.

papers.title: Weak rank rigidity for groups with a navigable path system
papers.authors: Cornelia Drutu, Davide Spriano, Stefanie Zbinden
papers.abstract:
We show that groups with a mild form of non-positive curvature (a navigable path system) satisfy the weak rank rigidity conjecture: they either have linear divergence or a Morse element. This class includes discrete groups of projective automorphisms of open convex cones, Helly groups (answering a question of Genevois), Coxeter groups, weak Garside groups (in particular Deligne's groups and fundamental groups of Salvetti complexes of oriented matroids), hierarchically hyperbolic groups, and other examples. Along the way, we show that those groups satisfy the Morse local-to-global property, providing a unified proof for the whole class.
  In the metric setting, the same condition of non-positive curvature allows to provide a local definition (that is, in a sense, optimal) of rank one/Morse geodesics, mirroring the one using parallel Jacobi fields from Riemannian geometry; to deduce linearity of divergence from linearity on a sequence; to obtain new cases in which Morse geodesics are strongly contracting.
  The main new tool introduced is the generalised contraction space, a hyperbolic space that encodes the negative curvature of a given space.

papers.title: Homogeneous spaces with transcendental Brauer--Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle
papers.abstract: Over any number field with sufficiently many roots of unity, we construct homogeneous spaces of $\mathbf{SL}_n$ with finite geometric stabilizers of nilpotency class $2$, whose unramified algebraic Brauer group consists only of constant classes, and which has no rational point but has local points in every completion of the ground field. This provides the first known examples of failures of the Hasse principle for homogeneous spaces of connected linear algebraic groups that are detected only by transcendental Brauer classes. The construction builds on the failure of a global--local principle for cup-product decomposition, based on a previous idea of Borovoi and Kunyavskii.

papers.title: The Weyl-orbit embedding and a representation-theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy
papers.abstract: Bu, Gu, and Jaffe introduced the quantum uniformity measures to analytically characterize the Clifford hierarchy. We prove that the quantum uniformity measures are the pullbacks of the matrix-valued uniformity functionals of Gowers and Hatami under the map $U\mapsto(a\mapsto W_aUW_a^*)$, which we call the Weyl-orbit embedding. We study the structure of the Weyl-orbit embedding, and among other results, establish a canonical decomposition of the ambient matrix-valued uniformity space into uniformity preserving twisted copies of the quantum uniformity space. The Weyl-orbit embedding identifies the Clifford hierarchy with Leibman polynomial maps. This identification yields a representation theoretic characterization of the Clifford hierarchy in terms of unitary representations of the universal polynomial groups introduced by the first author and Thom.

papers.title: Online Feedback Optimization for Constrained Stochastic Problems with Decision-Dependent Distributions
papers.abstract: Online feedback optimization (OFO) leverages real-time output measurements to optimize the operation of networked systems without requiring full knowledge of system dynamics or disturbances. We develop an OFO approach for constrained stochastic optimization problems in which the distribution of the system's random parameters shifts in response to the control actions. We propose a projected primal-dual algorithm where the true dual constraint sets are replaced by surrogate sets. Our main result is an upper bound on the mean-square tracking error, which decomposes into four interpretable terms reflecting: (i) the stochasticity of the problem, (ii) output measurement errors, (iii) time-variability of the problem, and (iv) the mismatch between surrogate and true dual constraint sets. The theory is illustrated in a numerical experiment for power grids with price-responsive assets.

papers.title: Higher Accuracy Modular Data Assimilation for the Navier-Stokes Equations
papers.abstract:
This paper develops an accurate and effective combination of second order backward differentiation time discretization (BDF2) with modular, 2-step nudging-based data assimilation  egin{align} 	ext{Forecast step: } \quad & rac{3\widetilde{v}^{n+2}-4v^{n+1}+v^n}{2\Delta t}+\widetilde{v}^{n+2} \cdot

Stability and error estimates for the BDF2 scheme are presented along with their proofs. Numerical experiments are conducted to assess the performance of BDF2 modular assimilation algorithm. The results of the experiments support the conclusion that modular data assimilation has comparable accuracy to standard, fully coupled data assimilation while greatly reducing computational complexity and cost.

papers.title: Sharp coefficient, logarithmic and Schwarzian estimates for $\alpha$-convex functions on the real line
papers.authors: V\'ictor Bravo, Pablo Carrasco, Rodrigo Hern\'andez, Osvaldo Venegas
papers.abstract: The class $M_\alpha$ of $\alpha$-convex functions, introduced by Mocanu in 1969, interpolates between starlike ($\alpha=0$) and convex ($\alpha=1$) mappings and has traditionally been studied only for $\alpha\geq0$. We show that several of its sharp invariant estimates in fact extend to the entire real line. Our main result characterizes $M_\alpha$ for every real $\alpha\neq0$ through an explicit pointwise inequality, generalizing a theorem of Chuaqui, Duren and Osgood from the convex case, and we determine the sharp value of $\beta$ for which $M_\alpha\subset C_\beta$ when $\alpha\geq1$; we also show that the reciprocal inclusion $C_\beta\subset M_\alpha$ fails for every $\alpha>1$. Building on this, we obtain a sharp Fekete--Szeg\H{o} inequality, valid for every $\alpha\notin\{0,-1,-1/2\}$, and sharp bounds for the first two logarithmic coefficients of $M_\alpha$, which recover the classical values for starlike and convex functions as special cases. We also determine the order of $M_\alpha$, establish a piecewise sharp bound for its Schwarzian norm together with an explicit quasiconformal extension criterion via the Ahlfors--Weill theorem, and compute the Schwarzian norm of the $\alpha$-Koebe function explicitly for $\alpha=1/n$, $n\in\mathbb N$, verified for $n\leq9$ and numerically supported for $n<50$, leading to a conjecture for the general case. Finally, we propose a conjectural sharp bound for the second Hankel determinant of $M_\alpha$, consistent with the known values $1$ and $1/8$ for the starlike and convex subclasses.

papers.title: On Automorphism Groups of (1,2)-Surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a minimal surface of general type with $K_S^2=1$ and $p_g(S)=2$, called a $(1,2)$-surface. We give a geometric recovery and refinement of D. Wen's bound $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200$ using the canonical genus-two fibration and the double-cover model over the Hirzebruch surface $\Sigma_2$. Computing $\mathrm{Aut}(\Sigma_2)$ from its Cox ring separates the action on the base $\mathbb{P}^1$ from the vertical kernel. If $\overline K_0$ denotes the vertical image on $\Sigma_2$, then $\overline K_0$ is cyclic of order $5$, $4$, $2$, or $1$, and we prove the respective sharp bounds $|\mathrm{Aut}(S)|\leq 200, 192, 48, 80$. The proof combines singularity indices of genus-two fibrations with invariant divisors arising from the branch equation. We also construct admissible branch divisors attaining all four bounds and show that their full automorphism groups are, respectively, $(C_{10}\times C_{10})\rtimes C_2$, $(BO_{48}\times C_8)/\langle(-I,J^4)\rangle$, $(BT_{24}\times C_4)/\langle(-I,J^2)\rangle$, and $C_{40}\times C_2$. Here $BO_{48}$ and $BT_{24}$ denote the binary octahedral and binary tetrahedral groups, respectively, and $J$ denotes a generator of the corresponding cyclic factor.

papers.title: Spectral deferred corrections parallelized across the method for differential-algebraic equations
papers.abstract: In this work, the performance of different spectral deferred corrections (SDC) methods applied to initial value problems for differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) of index one is analyzed. The SDC method solves a series of correction equations, and after each iteration, the numerical solution is corrected by adding the obtained approximation of the error. The formulation of the SDC method allows for a parallelization across the method to obtain small-scale parallelism, for which a number of processes equal to the number of collocation nodes can be used. Recently, an analytical approach to finding optimal diagonal coefficients for parallel SDC was proposed. So far, no analysis with the new coefficients for parallel SDC applied to DAEs was done. We demonstrate that parallel SDC methods solve DAE problems with high accuracy faster than the associated sequential SDC schemes, obtaining speedup in a small-scale parallel regime.

papers.title: An infinity-categorical TQFT from instantons
papers.abstract: In this paper, we lift the instanton TQFT from ordinary categories to the $\infty$-categorical setting by constructing a functor $CI:\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}\longrightarrow\mathsf{D}$ from an $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ for instantons to an $\infty$-derived category $\mathsf{D}$ of $2$-periodic chain complexes. The construction of $\mathrm{BI}^{\partial}$ is a modification of the $\infty$-cobordism category $\mathrm{Bord}_4$ introduced by Lurie and by Calaque--Scheimbauer using complete Segal spaces. The target $\infty$-category $\mathsf{D}$ is obtained via the dg nerve of the dg category of $2$-periodic chain complexes of finitely presented projective $\mathbb{Z}$-modules. The information encoded by the functor $CI$ was already developed by Kronheimer--Mrowka using families of metrics on cobordisms. Our reinterpretation in terms of $\infty$-categories conceptually simplifies the construction of the hypercube complexes underlying the link spectral sequence. This viewpoint also clarifies hyperbox complexes and compression in Manolescu--Ozsv\'{a}th's work, and possible $A_\infty$-structures, especially their signs and higher coherence. In addition, we lift the generalized cap product $\mu$-operators in instanton Floer homology to the chain level and construct explicit homotopies and higher homotopies establishing the commutativity of multiple $\mu$-operators in even degrees.

papers.title: AirPASS: Over-the-Air Federated Learning via Pinching Antenna Systems
papers.authors: Seyed Mohammad Azimi-Abarghouyi, Christopher G. Brinton
papers.abstract: This paper investigates over-the-air federated learning (AirFL) in wireless systems where the access point is equipped with a multi-waveguide pinching antenna system (PASS). We adopt the widely studied learning-oriented AirFL formulation, which seeks to maximize the number of selected devices while keeping the aggregation distortion below a prescribed threshold. The resulting joint optimization of device selection, receive beamforming, and pinching-antenna placement is highly nonconvex due to the intricate coupling among these system variables. To address this challenge, we develop AirPASS, an alternating optimization framework with two main components: a homotopy-Riemannian margin-consolidation method for device selection and receive beamforming under a fixed PASS configuration, and a homotopy-assisted geometry optimization method for updating the pinching-antenna positions under fixed selected devices and beamformer.

papers.title: On $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient ratios for complex parameters
papers.abstract: We prove local asymptotics for near-central complex $(p,q)$-binomial coefficient modulus ratios allowing an imaginary parameter perturbation of order $n^{-3/4}$ at a $\sqrt{n}$ length scale from the centre. Moreover, we obtain ratio asymptotics for a smaller imaginary perturbation of order $n^{-5/4}$ at the length scale $n^{3/4}$. These results were obtained by reducing the two-parameter coefficients to just one parameter, giving a branch-free logarithmic representation of the second-order ratio and, hence, uniform complex curvature asymptotics for near-central ratios.

papers.title: Quartic Fourier-Laplace limits for $(p,q)$-Rogers-Szeg\H{o} polynomials
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic formulae for $(p,q)$-Rogers--Szeg\H{o} polynomials with positive real parameters when the leading quadratic term in the logarithmic expansion about the middle coefficient vanishes. For coefficient indices whose distance from $n/2$ is of order $n^{3/4}$, the coefficient ratios have a quadratic--quartic exponential limit. A uniform bound valid for all indices allows the ratios to be summed and gives locally uniform convergence of the centred and normalised generating polynomials to a Fourier--Laplace integral. We also obtain an asymptotic formula for the sum of the coefficients, convergence of all rescaled moments, weak convergence of the normalised coefficient measures, and convergence with multiplicity of the zeros near $w=1$ for which $n^{3/4}\log w$ remains bounded.

papers.title: Some homotopy coherent finite group actions on spheres
papers.abstract: We provide some examples of homotopy coherent smooth finite group actions on spheres which do not arise from strict actions.

papers.title: The shifted symplectic geometry of derived higher groupoids
papers.authors: Miquel Cueca, Florian Dorsch, Reyer Sjamaar, Chenchang Zhu
papers.abstract: The main goal of this work is to introduce derived Lie n-groupoids and their shifted symplectic structures. We further define shifted lagrangian structures and prove that their composition is well defined under suitable conditions. As an application, we show that our framework incorporates several reduction procedures at critical values, including: classical Hamiltonian reduction, group valued moment maps, Poisson Lie group valued moment maps and Mikami-Weinstein for proper symplectic groupoids.

papers.title: The stability landscape in wave-packet scattering: geometric rigidity and sharp Sobolev thresholds
papers.abstract: A central problem in harmonic analysis is to understand how frequency resolution constrains stability under nonlinear changes of coordinates. Motivated by Mallat's wavelet scattering theory, we establish a sharp resolution--robustness principle for nonlinear representations built from two-dimensional wave-packet systems, showing that the transverse geometry of the frequency channels determines the critical Sobolev regularity. Whenever the channels are thinner than in the wavelet regime, arbitrarily small smooth deformations can move high-frequency mass between adjacent channels, producing instability already at the level of the linear filter bank and the first scattering layer. We match this obstruction with scale-sharp commutator estimates propagated through the full scattering cascade, obtaining Lipschitz stability at the critical regularity threshold. Together, the results provide the first intrinsic deformation-stability theory for non-wavelet Euclidean scattering transforms and identify a microlocal transport mechanism governing robustness across nonlinear multiscale representations.

papers.title: On the Realizability of Edge-Girth Sequences
papers.authors: Lilian Marey, Paul Hilaire, Charlotte Laclau
papers.abstract: The edge-girth of an edge $e$ in a simple connected graph is the length of a shortest cycle containing $e$, with $g_e = \infty$ if no such cycle exists, and the edge-girth sequence of a graph is the nondecreasing sequence of the edge-girths of its edges. We characterize the sequences that are realizable as the edge-girth sequence of a simple connected graph. A constant sequence $(g^{(m)})$ with $g$ finite and $m \geq 1$ is realizable if and only if $m = g$ or $m \geq \lceil 3g/2 \rceil$. Otherwise, writing $S = S_0 \uplus (g^{(m)})$, where $g$ is the maximum value of $S$ and $m$ its multiplicity, we prove that $S$ is realizable if and only if $S_0$ is realizable and $m$ lies in an explicit set determined by $g$ and by the maximum diameters of the graphs realizing $S_0$, alone or extended by fewer than $g$ edges of edge-girth $g$. The proof rests on a chaining lemma, which turns a shortest cycle of a realization into a lower bound on the maximum diameter of the realizations of a shorter sequence.

papers.title: Geometric Properties of Higher Dimensional Solenoidal Attractors
papers.authors: Daniele Galli, Eleonora Passaglia, Andrea Ulliana
papers.abstract:
We study the skew product systems $T: \mathbb{S}^1\times\mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{S}^1 \times\mathbb{R}^d$, \begin{equation*}
  T(x,y)=(\ell x, A y+\phi(x)), \end{equation*} where $\ell\geq 2,$ $A \in GL_d(\mathbb{R})$ with $\rho(A)<1$, and $\phi \in C^r(\mathbb{S}^1, \mathbb{R}^d)$, with $r>(d+3)/2. We allow the fibers to have any dimension and $A$ to be non-conformal. We show that: when $|\det(A)|\ell<1$, for almost every $\phi$, the Hausdorff dimension of the solenoid attractor and the SRB measure equal 1+ the affinity dimension; when $|\det(A)|\ell>1$, for almost every $\phi$, the SRB measure is absolutely continuous. In the latter case we investigate the Sobolev regularity of the density of the SRB measure. We introduce a derivative dispersion condition, replacing the usual transversality condition.

papers.title: Geometry of Unimodular Random Hyperbolic Polyhedra
papers.authors: Huabin Ge, Yangxiang Lu, Chuwen Wang, Tian Zhou
papers.abstract:
We develop a geometric and probabilistic theory of unimodular random infinite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra in $\mathbb{H}^3$, allowing ordinary, ideal, and hyperideal vertices. Our results relate local dihedral geometry to global conformal type and random-walk behavior.
