A central role is played by a geometric characteristic $L_f(P)$, determined by the dihedral angles incident to a face $f$. We establish the unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity $$ \mathbb E[L_f(P)]=2\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}\mathbb E[deg(f)]. $$ Together with circle-pattern uniformization, this yields a sharp parabolic-hyperbolic dichotomy governed by the expected geometric characteristic. We also introduce polyhedral soficity and prove that admissible Benjamini-Schramm limits of finite trivalent hyperbolic polyhedra are parabolic.
  We further establish a quantitative Ring Lemma for regular circle patterns, providing degree-sensitive geometric control without assuming bounded degrees. Combined with unimodular probability methods, this estimate enables us to identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Our results extend the geometric-characteristic theory beyond ideal polyhedra, connecting three-dimensional geometry, unimodular Gauss-Bonnet theory, and stochastic boundary behavior.

papers.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
papers.abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.

papers.title: Risk-Aware Unit Commitment in District Heating Networks: Chance-Constrained and CVaR Optimization Under Demand Uncertainty
papers.authors: Annika Buchholz, Janina Zittel, Thorsten Koch
papers.abstract: While district heating networks are a key component of the energy transition, their operational planning is challenging due to substantial uncertainty in heat demand. We study how unit-commitment schedules can account for this uncertainty and what reliability costs. By adapting chance-constrained programming (CC) and conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) optimization to the mixed-integer unit-commitment problem for district-heating networks, we can compute optimal unit-commitment schedules under demand uncertainty. We generate heat demand scenarios using a Bayesian model, which explicitly quantifies forecasting uncertainty and yields predictive distributions as input to the network optimization. To handle the inherent uncertainty in heat demand, we apply two stochastic optimization approaches that exploit this distribution: chance-constrained programming limits the probability of unmet demand, and in our scenario-based setting reduces to a deterministic MIP in which demand is replaced by an empirical quantile, while CVaR optimization penalizes severe shortfalls in the tail of the distribution. We evaluate the approaches both on real-world data from the Berlin district heating network and on a benchmark set of synthetic, realistically parameterized instances of varying sizes. The results show that the two methods are complementary: CC cheaply traces the high-reliability end of the cost--reliability trade-off and reveals the physical reliability limit of the network, whereas CVaR covers the low-cost, risk-tolerant regime at considerably higher computational effort.

papers.title: Central limit theorem in R\'enyi divergence for lattice random variables
papers.abstract:
Let $\{X_i\}_{i=1}^n$ be independent, identically distributed lattice random variables with zero mean, unit variance, and maximal span $h>0$. Let $S_n=(X_1+\cdots+X_n)/\sqrt n$. Let $Z_n$ denote the quantization of a standard Gaussian random variable on the support lattice of $S_n$. We show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\alpha(S_n\|Z_n)$ of order $1<\alpha<\infty$ tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if $D_\alpha(S_{n_0}\| Z_{n_0})<\infty$ for some integer $n_0$ and a sub-Gaussian condition holds. Furthermore, we derive an Edgeworth-type asymptotic expansion of the divergence to arbitrary order. We also show that the R\'enyi divergence $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)$ of infinite order tends to 0 as $n\to\infty$ if and only if a sub-Gaussian condition, a curvature condition, and a uniform separation condition hold.
  These results constitute lattice counterparts of R\'enyi entropic central limit theorems for continuous random variables obtained by Bobkov, Chistyakov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{47} (2019), 270--323) and Bobkov and G\"{o}tze (\emph{Ann. Probab.} \textbf{53} (2025), 453--477). Uniform separation is an additional assumption beyond the sub-Gaussian and curvature conditions used in the continuous setting. The failure of uniform separation may cause an exponentially tilted version of $X_1$ to concentrate on a sublattice of max span $kh$ for some integer $k>1$, which yields the lower bound $D_\infty(S_n\|Z_n)\ge\log k$, and hence a failure of the entropic central limit theorem.

papers.title: When Is Two-Stage Sample Robust Optimization Asymptotically Optimal? A Simple Perspective
papers.abstract: Two-stage sample robust optimization with linear decision rules is a standard data-driven approach to two-stage stochastic linear programs with unknown distributions. \cite{bertsimas2022two} established that this approach is asymptotically optimal under several conditions. Most conditions are mild, but one imposes a technical requirement on the recourse system. Whether this condition is implied by the others was left as an open question. We resolve this open question through a geometric feature of the support set: simpleness, the property that every vertex is incident to exactly as many edges as the dimension of the support. For simple support sets, the technical condition is automatic, and asymptotic optimality holds under the remaining standard assumptions. For every non-simple support, we construct a recourse system that is feasible everywhere in the support but violates the technical condition, and this construction resolves the open question. We further characterize the simpleness of one-sided and two-sided budgeted uncertainty sets and identify when budget perturbations can restore simpleness. We also develop a polynomial-time algorithm that certifies the technical condition at a given vertex using its incident edge directions. Numerical experiments on newsvendor and network lot-sizing problems illustrate the characterization and the effectiveness of the verification algorithm.

papers.title: Measure rigidity for regular polynomial endomorphisms and applications
papers.abstract: We classify regular polynomial endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^k$ with the same equilibrium measure under some mild condition on the dynamics at infinity. In particular, for $f$ in a Zariski dense open subset of the parameter space and any $g$ of the same degree, $\mu_g=\mu_f$ if and only if $f=g$. We also establish finiteness results for maps with a prescribed equilibrium measure. Our approach rests on the stable manifold structure near the hyperplane at infinity. Applications include a Tits-type alternative, results on iterated centralizers, and an arithmetic non-density theorem.

papers.title: A proof of the 3-Decomposition Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the 3-Decomposition Conjecture: every finite connected cubic loopless multigraph decomposes into a spanning tree, a 2-regular subgraph, and a matching. The proof rests on a new theorem on matching complements in subcubic graphs. Let H be a finite connected bridgeless simple graph of maximum degree three, and let S be its set of degree-two vertices, with |S| = k >= 2. We show that H has a matching of size equal to its cyclomatic number, |E(H)| - |V(H)| + 1, whose deletion leaves a single tree containing all of S, together with cycles disjoint from S. The proof is by induction on k.

papers.title: Information Percolation and cutoff for Potts Glauber Dynamics
papers.abstract:
We prove cutoff with an $O(1)$ window for the continuous-time heat-bath Glauber dynamics of the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model on the discrete torus $\Lambda_n=(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z)^d$ at sufficiently high temperature. More precisely, for every fixed $d\ge2$ and $q\ge3$, there exists $\beta_0=\beta_0(d,q)>0$ such that, for $0<\beta<\beta_0$, the cutoff occurs in an optimal $O(1)$ window centered at \[ t_\star=t_\star^{(n)}:=\frac{1}{2\mathfrak{r}}\log |\Lambda_n|, \] where $\mathfrak{r}\in(0,1)$ is the exact exponential decay rate of the one-site color bias. Thus, the mixing time is determined up to an additive \(O(1)\). It is characterized by the time at which the macroscopic color-density bias from the monochromatic initial condition enters the scale of equilibrium fluctuations. Moreover, our proof shows that the monochromatic initial condition uniquely maximizes the color bias.
  This is the first implementation of information percolation to prove cutoff for a non-monotone spin system. On a transitive graph, information percolation naturally gives an upper bound on the mixing time of one half of the grand coupling time which is sharp for the Ising model. However, for many non-monotone systems including the Potts model, this misses additional averaging over the update histories giving an upper bound that is off by a constant multiplicate factor. We develop a new framework that treats the information percolation histories as random polymers and show how to average over them to give the effective bias from the initial condition. This accounts for all the additional mixing, recovering a sharp upper bound and cutoff. We believe this approach will be applicable in a much wider range of settings.

papers.title: Kronecker Products, Polarity Quotients and Large Graph Constructions
papers.authors: Kelly Isham, Kartik Lakhotia, Laura Monroe, Fabrizio Petrini
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we establish a structural compatibility between the Kronecker product of bipartite graphs that admit polarity and their polarity quotients, and provide a sharp upper bound on the diameter of these graphs. We use these properties to construct new families of graphs, all of which have orders that asymptotically approach the Moore bound.
  We show that the bipartite compatibility graphs have a natural polarity, and that the corresponding polarity quotients comprise a new family of graphs of any even diameter $2k$ with degree $(q+1)^k$ for any prime power $q$, much smaller than those of other known families of that diameter and field order $q$. These families generalize the Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi-Brown polarity graphs. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of any even diameter for every pair of prime powers $q,r$.
  Certain generalized polygons are known to admit polarity with polarity quotients approaching the Moore bound asymptotically. Kronecker products of these polarity quotients give another new family of graphs of diameters $2$, $3$ and $5$, including a diameter-$3$ degree-$18$ graph of order larger than any previously known for that degree and diameter.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous NLS in negative Sobolev spaces via Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces
papers.authors: Divyang G. Bhimani, Diksha Dhingra, Vijay Kumar Sohani
papers.abstract: The purpose of this work is to provide a broader framework for analyzing the 1D mass-subcritical inhomogeneous nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (INLS) \[iu_t + u_{xx} \pm |x|^{-b}|u|^{\alpha-1}u=0, \quad 1<\alpha< 5-2b\; \text{and}\; 0< b\leq 1/4.\] in Sobolev spaces of negative order, reaching almost critical Sobolev spaces by working in Fourier-Lebesgue and modulation spaces. More precisely, we establish low-regularity well-posedness in the Fourier-Lebesgue $\widehat{L}^{p}$ spaces for $4/3<p<8$. Primarily, we prove global well-posedness for arbitrarily large initial data via the data decomposition method adapted for the Fourier-Lebesgue spaces, with generalized Strichartz estimates for $p<2$ and classical Strichartz estimates for $p>2$. Furthermore, we obtain analogous results for (INLS) in modulation spaces $M^{p,p'}$ for $4/3<p<2$.

papers.title: Lipshitz-Sarkar refines mirrors more than Khovanov
papers.abstract: Lipshitz and Sarkar asked in an ICM 2018 question whether their homotopy-theoretic refinement of Khovanov homology can detect mirror reflection when ordinary integral Khovanov homology cannot. We give an affirmative answer by presenting a prime knot whose integral Khovanov homology agrees with that of its mirror in every bidegree, including torsion, and yet over $\mathbb{F}_2$, the second Steenrod square has rank one for the knot and rank zero for its mirror in a specified bidegree. We also give a composite example. The construction, search and computations are done with the help of {\it chat-GTP 5.6 sol Pro} combing over the {\it Regina Census} of knots.

papers.title: On The Rational Realization of Even-dimensional Spheres and Products of Eilenberg--MacLane Spaces as Classifying Spaces
papers.authors: Yang Bai, Xiugui Liu, Jiaxi Zha
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization problem for the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$. We prove that if $S^{2n}$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected space $X$, then $X$ is $\pi$-infinite and has vanishing rational Gottlieb elements above degree $2n-1$. In particular, even-dimensional spheres cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$. We also prove that, for all $n\geq 2$ and $s,t\geq 1$, the product of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces $K(\mathbb{Q}^s,n)\times K(\mathbb{Q}^t,n+1)$ cannot be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for any simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$. Moreover, we prove that if $r\geq 2$, $n\geq 3$ and $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n)$ is realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)_{\mathbb{Q}}$ for a simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$, then $X$ has the rational homotopy type of $K(\mathbb{Q}^r,n-1)$. The proofs are based on two structural results for Gottlieb elements in the derivation Lie algebra of a Sullivan minimal model, which provide a uniform method for these realization problems.

papers.title: Primes are Complete for a Class of Cantor Spectral Pair
papers.authors: Zi-Chao Chi, Jian-Feng Lu, He-Xiang Wang
papers.abstract: We study the complete number problem for a class of self-similar spectral measures on the real line. We say that a real number $t$ is complete for a spectral pair $(\mu,\Lambda)$ if $(\mu,t\Lambda)$ is also a spectral pair. In this paper we consider the partial homogeneous Cantor measure $\mu_{N^r,\mathcal D}$ and its canonical spectrum. Our main result fully characterizes all prime powers $p^n$ that are complete for $p>N$. In particular, we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for an arbitrary prime $p$ to be complete. {We further establish a connection between the problem and certain Diophantine equations}, including the Nagell--Ljunggren equation, and obtain complete number results for a class of related models. As applications, known solutions of the Nagell--Ljunggren equation provide complete and incomplete prime-power examples.

papers.title: Weighted Laplace Spaces for Spectral Measures and Rational Approximation
papers.authors: Stefan Jakobsson, Alice Kozakevicius, Stig Larsson
papers.abstract: We introduce the weighted Laplace space $H_w$, an RKHS of Laplace transforms on $(0,\infty)$, and study spectral measures in its dual space $H'_w$. For conforming FEM discretizations of the Dirichlet Laplacian on bounded Lipschitz domains, we prove the dual-norm inequality $\|\mu_h\|_{H'_w} \leq \|\mu\|_{H'_w}$, where $\mu = \sum_k\delta_{\lambda_k}$ and $\mu_h = \sum_k \delta_{\lambda_{k,h}}$. The proof combines min-max monotonicity of FEM eigenvalues with a heat-trace representation of the dual norm. We then analyze $H_w$-adapted rational approximation of shifted symbols $\phi(x)=(x+\kappa^2)^{-\beta}$ and give a conditional transfer principle for estimates proved in the corresponding weighted Laplace pre-image norm. Via dual pairing, the norm inequality yields uniform bounds for finite spectral sums and related transformed observables.

papers.title: Classification of finite-dimensional Nichols algebras of rank two in twisted Yetter--Drinfeld categories
papers.abstract: Let \(G\) be a finite non-abelian group, let \(\Phi\in Z^3(G,\mathbb C^\times)\) be normalized, and let \(V,W\) be finite-dimensional simple objects of \({}_G^G\mathcal{YD}^{\Phi}\). We classify, up to interchange, the braided-indecomposable pairs \((V,W)\) whose supports generate \(G\) and for which \(\mathcal B(V\oplus W)\) is finite-dimensional. The classification consists of eight cases with five possible support quandles. In every case the Cartan graph is standard of type \(A_2\), \(B_2\), or \(G_2\), and the dimension is determined explicitly. A new phenomenon occurs {in the \(\Gamma _2\) case}: the twisted setting admits a family of type \(G_2\) absent from the ordinary \(\Gamma _2\) classification and we construct an explicit example over a non-abelian group of order \(16\).

papers.title: Connected irregular cospectral graphs with distinct Lov\'{a}sz numbers
papers.abstract: For every integer $n \geq 11$, we construct connected, irregular, nonisomorphic graphs on $n$ vertices with equal adjacency, Laplacian, signless Laplacian, normalized Laplacian, and Seidel spectra and equal independence, clique, chromatic, complement chromatic, and maximum-cut numbers, but distinct Lov\'{a}sz $\vartheta$-numbers. We join each graph in a fixed cospectral, nonisomorphic regular pair on ten vertices, due to van Dam and Haemers (2003), with $K_{n-10}$. We prove that these joins preserve equality of the five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants, and leave the respective Lov\'{a}sz numbers unchanged. We derive exact expressions for these numbers and prove that they are distinct. We also determine the cardinality-constrained maximum-cut profiles of both base graphs and their complements, yielding exact formulas and equality of maximum-cut numbers for the joins of either the base graphs or their complements with $K_{n-10}$. For $n=10$, we present a regular pair satisfying all stated properties except irregularity, followed by a connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair satisfying all properties. An exhaustive computer search finds no connected, irregular, nonisomorphic pair on at most nine vertices sharing the first four spectra and all stated integer-valued invariants. Thus, ten is the smallest possible order, and such pairs exist for every $n \geq 10$. This extends and strengthens Sason's (2024) result for \emph{even} $n \geq 14$, which used the neighbors splitting join operation and did not address Seidel matrices, complement chromatic numbers, or maximum-cut numbers of the graphs or joins of their complements. Thus, the Lov\'{a}sz number efficiently certifies nonisomorphism even when all five spectra and stated integer-valued invariants coincide.

papers.title: Recent Advances on a Model for the Electromagnetic Dirac Field at Thermal Equilibrium
papers.abstract: We review recent progress on a model for the relativistic electron-positron field interacting with a classical electromagnetic field at positive temperature. The ultimate goal is to advance our comprehension of how thermal backgrounds affect polarisation mechanisms of this quantum system.

papers.title: Moments Comparison Inequalities for Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow, Polymers and GMC
papers.abstract: We employ a Gaussian convex inequality developed in [AC15], [Che26], [Gue22], and [FUMPC26] to establish (one sided) moment comparison inequalities for Gaussian multiplicative chaos, directed polymers in Gaussian environment and, in particular, the Critical 2d Stochastic Heat Flow (SHF), including upper bounds on negative moments, as well as similar lower bounds for $p$-th moments with $p\in (0,1)$. For the Critical 2d SHF, averaged over small balls, we also obtain the matching (up to multiplicative constants) complementary bounds. We establish the complementary bounds using a bootstrap argument inspired by [DS10] and a geometric decomposition introduced in [GT26]. Specifically, we prove that for locally averaged SHF, for every $p\in\mathbb R$, the $p$-th moment is, up to multiplicative constants, bounded in both sides by the $\frac{p(p-1)}{2}$-th power of its second moment.

papers.title: Worse Routes, Fresher Information: Preemption Redefines Which Route is Best
papers.authors: Adem Utku Atasayar, Aimin Li, Elif Uysal
papers.abstract: This paper studies joint sampling, route activation, and preemption control over $N$ heterogeneous transmission routes under a long-run objective combining Age of Information (AoI) with sampling and transmission costs. We formulate the problem as an average-cost impulse-control model, derive a vector-form integral average-cost optimality equation over a hybrid state space, and establish structural reductions on the state. We consider a two-route case and compute optimized policies using discretized policy iteration. Surprisingly, the results show that preemption can reverse routing preferences: the optimized policy may exclusively use a route with both a larger mean delay and a larger delay variance while avoiding the seemingly superior route. Relative to baselines that do not allow preemption, the proposed policy reduces average AoI by up to $96\%$.

papers.title: Jacobian estimates and geometric inequalities under intermediate Ricci curvature
papers.authors: Kwok-Kun Kwong, Jihye Lee, Fabio Ricci
papers.abstract: We prove a Jacobian estimate underlying both the Heintze--Karcher comparison and the Alexandrov--Bakelman--Pucci method for submanifolds of arbitrary codimension. The estimate retains the contributions of ambient curvature along geodesics emanating from the submanifold and requires no curvature sign assumption. As applications, we obtain a quantitative Fenchel--Willmore inequality with explicit curvature remainders under nonnegative $n$-intermediate Ricci curvature, Michael--Simon Sobolev and isoperimetric inequalities under nonnegative $(n-1)$-intermediate Ricci curvature, and corresponding extensions under quadratic curvature decay. In each result, the required intermediate Ricci curvature condition depends only on the dimension of the submanifold and is independent of its codimension.

papers.title: Yang-Baxter permutation group actions on distributive Yang-Baxter algebras
papers.abstract: Let $(X,r)$ be a finite square-free distributive set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation, and let $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ be its associated Yang-Baxter algebra. We prove that $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ is isomorphic to a skew polynomial algebra and explicitly compute its Nakayama automorphism. We study the natural faithful action of the permutation group $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ on $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. We characterize when $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ is a reflection group and, in that case, describe the invariant subalgebra $\mathcal{A}(X,r)^{\mathcal{G}(X,r)}$ together with its Jacobian, reflection arrangement, and discriminant. We further establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the noncommutative Auslander theorem to hold for the permutation group action on a distributive Yang-Baxter algebra. Finally, for a class of non-trivial distributive Yang-Baxter algebras, we obtain a lower bound for the pertinency of the permutation group action.

papers.title: Optimal Deterministic First-Order Oracle Complexity for Nonconvex-Concave Minimax Optimization
papers.authors: Siyu Pan, Taoli Zheng, Jiajin Li
papers.abstract: We study the deterministic first-order oracle complexity of smooth nonconvex-concave minimax optimization over a bounded convex dual domain under two notions of stationarity: optimization stationarity (OS) and game stationarity (GS). OS concerns stationarity of the value function, viewed as a structured nonsmooth objective obtained by maximizing over the dual variable. GS concerns the joint first-order optimality conditions for both primal minimization and dual maximization, each with the other variable held fixed. Existing upper bounds on the oracle complexity of first-order methods for finding $\epsilon$-OS and $\epsilon$-GS points have different dependence on $\epsilon$, but whether this difference reflects an intrinsic separation in computational hardness remains unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing worst-case lower bounds for arbitrary deterministic first-order methods: $\Omega(\epsilon^{-3})$ oracle queries for finding an $\epsilon$-OS point and $\Omega(\epsilon^{-5/2})$ for finding an $\epsilon$-GS point, with the remaining problem parameters fixed. These bounds match existing upper bounds up to logarithmic factors. To close the remaining logarithmic gap, we introduce Tracked-FOAM, a new first-order algorithm whose oracle complexity matches our lower bounds for both OS and GS. Together, these results establish an intrinsic separation between OS and GS in the optimal accuracy dependence of deterministic first-order oracle complexity.

papers.title: Optimal Network Dependence in Distributed Stochastic Optimization via Tree Routing
papers.abstract: Communication is a central bottleneck in distributed optimization, but its effect is often summarized by the spectral gap of a chosen mixing matrix. Since this gap depends on link weights as well as topology, it can obscure the intrinsic effect of the network. We clarify this distinction by relating graph diameter to the inverse spectral gap. We establish a universal one-sided bound that is tight up to constant factors, while constructions across several graph families show that no topology-only converse or universal two-sided scaling law exists. This motivates a class-based view of network optimality: diameter-dependent guarantees can be assessed uniformly over graph classes, whereas spectral-gap optimality requires both the graph--matrix pair class and the admissible algorithm class to be specified. Based on the resulting diameter-based minimax benchmark, we introduce Tree-Routed Gradient Tracking (Tree-RGT), a distributed method for stochastic nonconvex optimization. The method pipelines model dissemination and gradient aggregation over a rooted shortest-path spanning tree. Each iteration uses one round of one-hop communication and one stochastic-gradient evaluation per agent, without inner consensus or multi-gossip. Under smoothness and unbiased bounded-variance oracles, Tree-RGT achieves uniformly optimal network dependence over connected graphs of prescribed size and diameter. It recovers centralized stochastic scaling after $\mathcal{O}(nD_{\mathcal{G}}^2)$ transient iterations, where $n$ is the number of agents and $D_{\mathcal{G}}$ is the graph diameter. This network-dependent transient-iteration bound improves upon or matches those reported for representative distributed methods. Thus, topology-aware routing attains diameter-optimal guarantees without relying on a prescribed mixing matrix.

papers.title: Relaxation and Steady-State Entropy Production for Langevin SPDEs: A Dirichlet-Form Approach
papers.authors: Shuyuan Fan, Yuanke Chen, Lifei Wang, Jinqiao Duan
papers.abstract: We develop a Dirichlet-form framework for relaxation and steady-state entropy production in preconditioned Langevin stochastic partial differential equations. In infinite dimensions, the usual Fokker--Planck calculations based on ambient Lebesgue densities and the corresponding probability-current densities are generally unavailable. For the detailed-balance class, a quasi-regular symmetric Dirichlet form on the Gibbs state space yields an exact de Bruijn entropy-dissipation formula for regular densities and an integrated inequality for arbitrary finite-entropy initial laws. Self-adjointness gives detailed balance and stationary path reversal, while a coordinate-martingale criterion identifies the associated process with the prescribed SPDE. For the one-dimensional $\Phi^4_1$ and convex Allen--Cahn-type Gibbs dynamics, we combine the established strong well-posedness theory with direct verification of the logarithmic derivatives, form closure, quasi-regularity and form--SPDE correspondence, and obtain relative-entropy decay bounds with exponents $2$ and $2(1-\lambda/m)$, respectively, with $m>\lambda$ in the latter case. Away from detailed balance, bounded skew-adjoint linear forcing preserves a Gaussian invariant law without requiring commutation between the forcing and covariance. We identify the antisymmetric action on cylinder observables and its Cameron--Martin current and prove that the squared current energy equals the steady-state entropy-production rate defined by forward--reverse path-space relative entropy per unit time, as well as the monotone limit of the Galerkin rates. Under commutation, we additionally obtain an explicit transient Onsager decomposition after a mass quench. Exclusion processes and Gaussian rotors provide finite-state and Gaussian benchmarks.

papers.title: Maximal common divisors in monoid algebras
papers.authors: Grant Blitz, Felix Gotti, Darren Han, Hengrui Liang
papers.abstract: A commutative cancellative monoid has the MCD property if every nonempty finite subset has a maximal common divisor, and it has the MCD-finite property if every such subset has only finitely many maximal common divisors up to associates. We study these properties in monoid algebras. We first identify atomic and antimatter families of rank-$1$ torsion-free MCD monoids. We then prove that, for a field $F$ and a torsion-free monoid $M$, the MCD property ascends from $M$ to $F[M]$ whenever the group algebra $F[\mathcal{G}(M)]$ satisfies the ascending chain condition on principal ideals ($\mathcal{G}(M)$ denotes the Grothendieck group of $M$). We also record the pre-Schreier case as a consequence of classical GCD ascent. In contrast, for every prime $p$, we construct a reduced rank-$3$ MCD monoid $M$ such that $\mathbb{F}_p[M]$ is not an MCD domain, and an atomic rank-$1$ MCD monoid whose algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is not atomic. We further prove that the prime reciprocal monoids considered here are MCD-finite and that MCD-finiteness ascends to polynomial extensions. Finally, for every prime $p$, we construct a rank-$1$ torsion-free q-GCD monoid whose algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is not q-GCD, where the q-GCD property requires at most one maximal common divisor up to associates for every nonempty finite subset.

papers.title: Simple Cayley permutations
papers.abstract: We propose a notion of simplicity for Cayley permutations that is compatible with inflation and agrees, under a natural relational encoding, with indecomposability in the sense of Schmerl and Trotter. We establish a substitution decomposition analogous to that of permutations, in which the components are modules of the associated relational structure. We use it to enumerate simple Cayley permutations as well as simple restricted growth functions.

papers.title: New link between the fractional p-Laplacian operators and a class of McKean-Vlasov flight type processes
papers.abstract: We prove the existence of a McKean--Vlasov stochastic process with jumps associated to the nonlinear parabolic equation $\partial_t u = \Delta_p u + \Delta_p^s u$ in $\mathbb{R}^N\times(0,\infty)$, where $\Delta_p$ is the $p$-Laplacian and $\Delta_p^s$ is the fractional $p$-Laplacian. Our approach is the following: first, after proving the existence of a solution for the PDE presented earlier, we rewrite it as a nonlinear Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equation whose measure-valued solution is guaranteed when $p\ge4$. Then we solve the martingale problem associated to our FPKE via a new superposition principle for non-local Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations, which only requires an integrability condition on the local coefficients. Finally, thanks to the martingale solution obtained, we derive the existence of a weak solution for the McKean-Vlasov's type SDE with jumps whose infinitesimal generator is a << hybrid version >> of the operator $\Delta_p+\Delta_p^s$.

papers.title: On the Geometry of Wasserstein Barycenter II: Riemannian Rigidity, Essential Non-Branching, and Finsler Models
papers.abstract:
Wasserstein barycenters provide a notion of weighted mean for probability measures on a metric space. We prove that the barycenter curvature-dimension condition ${\rm BCD}(K,N)$ is equivalent to ${\rm RCD}(K,N)$ for $K\in \mathbb R$ and $1<N<\infty$. This gives a new characterization of Riemannian curvature-dimension spaces by entropy inequalities at barycenters of finite families of measures.
  As a byproduct, we introduce an almost ${\rm BCD}$ condition that allows an additive error in the entropy inequality. It is stable under measured Gromov-Hausdorff convergence and implies essential non-branching when the error is sufficiently small. The resulting class contains non-Riemannian Finsler spaces. Within the ${\rm BCD}$ framework, this answers an open problem posed by Ambrosio in his 2018 ICM survey. We further bound the failure of the parallelogram identity for cotangent norms in terms of the entropy error.

papers.title: Extended dynamic mode decomposition with Fourier dictionaries: Error bounds and fast implementation
papers.authors: Felix Bartel, Sandra Ritter, Manuel Schaller, Karl Worthmann
papers.abstract: The Koopman operator has gained considerable attention in dynamical systems due to its capability to provide a linear viewpoint for nonlinear systems using data-driven methods such as extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD). In this work, we propose an EDMD-variant with a Fourier dictionary on the $d$-dimensional torus, where the data are sampled on an equispaced tensor grid. We show that the EDMD regression problem admits a unique closed-form solution and coincides with trigonometric interpolation of the Koopman image. This identification has two consequences. First, using Koopman invariance of Sobolev spaces, we transfer approximation-theoretic results for trigonometric interpolation to derive $L^p$-error bounds, $2 \le p \le \infty$, on approximations of the Koopman operator. In particular, the established bounds are of optimal order with explicit constants. Second, the EDMD matrix never has to be assembled, since its action reduces to (nonequispaced) fast Fourier transforms such that the EDMD-approximation can be evaluated matrix-free with quasi-linear cost in the dictionary size. We illustrate the results for the Kuramoto model of coupled oscillators and for the chaotic ABC flow with dictionaries of up to $10^7$ modes.

papers.title: Erd\H{o}s-S\'{o}s via random cyclic orderings
papers.abstract: We present a simplified proof of the Erd\H{o}s-S\'os conjecture on trees in graphs, which is based on its recent resolution by GPT-6 Astra. At the same time, we also give another proof of the corresponding conjecture for antidirected trees in digraphs, posed by Addario-Berry, Havet, Linhares Sales, Reed, and Thomass\'e, and we simplify recent proofs of Kalai's conjecture for tight trees in hypergraphs. Our proof uses the language of random cyclic orderings in order to take advantage of symmetries that were obscured in the original argument, and we hope that the reader will find it intuitive. We also characterize the extremal examples for Kalai's conjecture, and we generalize it to the setting of so-called fully directed $r$-uniform hypergraphs, whose edges are ordered $r$-tuples.

papers.title: An improvement of the large sieve for square moduli under Hooley's hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums
papers.abstract: Let $S(Q,M,N,(a_n))=\sum_{q\le Q}\sum_{a\bmod q^2,(a,q)=1}|\sum_{M<n\le M+N}a_ne(an/q^2)|^2$ be Zhao's large sieve sum with square moduli. Zhao conjectured that $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N)\sum|a_n|^2$. The bound of Baier and Zhao (2008) exceeds this conjecture by a factor which reaches $Q^{1/2}$ at the critical point $N=Q^3$, and there the exponent $1/2$ has not been lowered since. We prove that, under Hooley's Hypothesis $R^*$ for short Sali\'e sums, $S\ll(QN)^\epsilon(Q^3+N+Q^{4/3}N^{2/3})\sum|a_n|^2$. This replaces the excess over Zhao's conjecture by its $2/3$-th power throughout the range $Q^{5/2}<N<Q^4$; at $N=Q^3$ it gives $S\ll Q^{1/2-1/6+\epsilon}N\sum|a_n|^2$. The proof is short. Following Zhao's original treatment, we approximate the point under consideration by fractions $b/r$ with denominators up to $Q^{2/3}N^{1/3}$, which for $N<Q^4$ is beyond the customary $\sqrt{N}$. If the approximation is poor, an elementary count suffices. If it is good, the analytic part of the problem disappears: after Poisson summation in both variables the count is expressed through quadratic Gauss sums, and their exact evaluation at every modulus turns the sum over the dual variable into short Kloosterman and Sali\'e sums, to which Hypothesis $R^*$ applies and gives the square root of the elementary count. At odd moduli the hypothesis is needed only in the form of Conjecture (C*) of Friedlander and Iwaniec. The Gauss-sum evaluations, including even moduli and coefficients sharing a factor with the modulus, are proved in full. This version supersedes earlier versions, which obtained the exponent $1/2-1/28$ at $N=Q^3$ by a much longer route through sums of modular square roots. The paper was prepared in collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).

papers.title: The Limits of Arithmetical Pluralism: Incompleteness, Large Cardinals, and Graded Non-Pluralism
papers.abstract: G\"odelian incompleteness yields arithmetical sentences \(A\) such that \(\mathsf{PA}+A\) and \(\mathsf{PA}+\neg A\) are both consistent. Are such extensions equally legitimate? I propose graded epistemic arithmetical non-pluralism: justification for choosing between them varies with the set-theoretic strength of \(A\). I defend \(\mathsf{PA}+\mathsf{Con}(\mathsf{PA})\) and show that Friedman's concrete incompleteness results pose a serious challenge to non-pluralism about first-order arithmetic. Resolving the selection problem for such sentences turns on justifying large cardinals. Defending graded non-pluralism thus engages G\"odel's programme and the justification of very large cardinals.

papers.title: Exact Sign Recovery for PCA Connectivity Analysis in Mixture Models
papers.abstract: We study exact sign recovery for PCA connectivity analysis in mixture models, using the projection onto the first $(K-1)$ principal components. For any fixed number of components with affinely independent means, we derive the oracle signal projection explicitly. Under anisotropic sub-Gaussian noise, with a random number of observations in each component, a rowwise eigenspace bound yields a sufficient condition, governed by the weakest signal direction, for recovering all connectivity signs without requiring a bounded condition number of the nonzero signal spectrum. Under isotropic Gaussian noise, when the configuration of the component means is fixed up to scaling and orthogonal transformations, we identify an asymptotically sharp threshold for the signal strength: exact sign recovery succeeds above the threshold and fails below the threshold, with probability tending to one when the signal strength stays a fixed relative distance from the threshold. The threshold has an explicit formula when the mixing proportions are equal and the means form a regular simplex.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning and Operational Research: A Review of Methodological Integration and Research Directions
papers.authors: Yahan Lu, Dongyang Xia, Nursen Aydin, Shadi Sharif Azadeh
papers.abstract: The growing demand for real-time, data-driven decision-making in complex and dynamic systems is placing increasing pressure on Operational Research (OR) methodologies. Sequential decision-making under uncertainty has long been studied in OR through Markov decision processes, dynamic programming, and their approximations, and reinforcement learning (RL) provides simulation-based methods for learning decision policies in such problems. Recent research shows an increasing interest in integrating RL with OR to address dynamic decision-making problems and enhance heuristic and exact methods for combinatorial optimization. The overarching goal across these efforts is to improve solution quality, computational efficiency, and robustness. Given the diversity of integration approaches and application settings, there is a clear need for a systematic and technically detailed review of how RL empowers OR methods. To address this gap, this paper presents a structured review of two methodological roles of RL in OR. The first concerns sequential decision problems in dynamic environments, where states evolve and decisions are repeated over time. The second concerns static combinatorial optimization problems, where inputs are fixed before the solution process begins and RL either constructs solutions or supports heuristic and exact algorithms. Digital twins provide an optional deployment and evaluation layer for training, testing, and validating these methods. We critically synthesize recent advances across these roles and uses, highlighting their advantages, implementation requirements, limitations, and challenges. Finally, we consolidate guidance on when the reviewed approaches may be considered and outline directions for future research on the methodological and practical integration of RL and OR.

papers.title: Abelian maximal pattern complexity and extremal words
papers.authors: Qingcheng Zeng, Yumei Xue, Cheng Zeng
papers.abstract:
In this paper, we study the Abelian maximal pattern complexity $p_{\alpha}^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)$, introduced by Kamae, Widmer and Zamboni, of infinite words $\alpha \in \mathbb{A}^{\mathbb{N}_{0}}$ over finite alphabets $\mathbb{A}$.
  For recurrent aperiodic words, we determine a lower bound and prove its sharpness. We further give a structural characterization of the words with minimal Abelian maximal pattern complexity.
  In the general case, we prove that an infinite word $\alpha $ is aperiodic if and only if $\binom{p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)}{2}\geq k$ for every $k.$ For aperiodic words over $\ell \geq 2$ letters, each occurring infinitely often, we further prove that $p_{\alpha }^{\ast \mathrm{ab}}(k)\geq m$ whenever $\binom{m}{2}\leq (\ell -1)(k-\ell +2)$, for all $m,k$. Together with a matching construction, this shows that the minimum Abelian maximal pattern complexity in this class is $\sqrt{2(\ell -1)k}+O_{\ell }(1)$.
  We call a word an Abelian pattern Sturmian word if, at every $k$, its Abelian maximal pattern complexity is the least positive integer $m$ satisfying $\binom{m}{2}\geq k$. We show that a word is Abelian pattern Sturmian if and only if, after relabeling its alphabet, it is the characteristic word of an infinite set $E\subset \mathbb{N}_{0}$ for which the bipartite graph on two disjoint copies of $\mathbb{N}_{0}$, with a left vertex $r$ adjacent to a right vertex $s$ exactly when $r+s\in E$, is a forest.

papers.title: $\mathbb{A}^1$-connectedness of moduli of vector bundles on a stacky curve
papers.authors: Sujoy Chakraborty, Saurav Holme Choudhury, Rakesh Pawar
papers.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{C}$ be a projective stacky curve over an infinite field $k$ with the coarse space $C$, a geometrically connected smooth projective curve, together with a generating sheaf $\mathcal{E}$ on $\mathfrak{C}$. We consider the moduli stack of $\mathcal{E}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and multiplicities on $\mathfrak{C}$, and show that it is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected if and only if it admits a $k$-rational point. We show that this holds whenever genus of $C$ is at least $2$ and $C(k)\neq \emptyset$. As a consequence, we conclude that, for any system of weights $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$, the moduli stack of parabolic $\boldsymbol{\alpha}$-semistable vector bundles of fixed determinant and quasi-parabolic data on a geometrically connected smooth projective curve is $\mathbb{A}^1$-connected.

papers.title: Chv\'atal's conjecture: a proof from The Book
papers.authors: David Ellis, Yuval Filmus, Ehud Friedgut
papers.abstract:
Chv\'atal conjectured that every downset has a maximum-size intersecting family which is a star, that is, consists of all members of the downset containing a fixed element.
  Recently, Chang, Liu and Liu gave a proof of this conjecture, which follows as a corollary of more general results such as Kleitman's conjecture and a version of Kahn's conjecture (which they also prove). We give a short, direct (spectral) proof of Chv\'atal's conjecture, and a proof of Kleitman's conjecture along the same lines. We also prove a strengthening of Chv\'atal's conjecture concerning the projection packing number. Finally, we propose two spectral Chv\'atal conjectures which are motivated by extensive numerical experiments.

papers.title: Formalization of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for Local Epsilon Factors
papers.abstract: We describe the Lean 4 formalization of Langlands's Second Main Lemma for local epsilon factors over nonarchimedean local fields, in mixed and equal characteristic. The lemma compares the induction expressions attached to compatible characters of the intermediate fields of a bicyclic extension of prime-square degree. We explain the mathematical constructions and comparisons that constitute the proof, and identify their Lean declarations.

papers.title: On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the (uniform) Yau-Tian-Donaldson Conjecture for transcendental K\"ahler classes in the case of trivial automorphisms. Indeed, we show the existence of Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations of big cohomology classes associated to big test configurations, establishing the equivalence between the uniform $K$-stability and the strengthened version for models. More generally, we show that any big cohomology class on a compact K\"ahler manifold admits such Special K\"ahler Fujita Approximations: the volume and the analogue of the Riemann-Roch coefficient of the big class are both approximated by those of K\"ahler classes on higher compactifications.

papers.title: Proper circular arc graphs are $e$-positive
papers.abstract: We prove an $e$-positive formula for the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs solving the $q=1$ case of a conjecture of Ellzey and of Alexandersson and Panova. In doing so, we provide a new proof of the $e$-positivity of unit interval graphs, which alongside Guay-Paquet's reduction gives a new proof of the Stanley--Stembridge conjecture. We define color matrices, which count proper colorings, and tableau matrices, whose entries are nonnegative rational numbers and ratios of elementary symmetric functions. We prove the two matrices are related by a single family of change of basis matrices, which become invertible after restricting to finitely many colors, and we show the chromatic symmetric function of proper circular arc graphs comes from taking the trace of these matrices. Using Hikita's tableaux, this gives an explicit formula for the chromatic symmetric function of a proper circular arc graph as a weighted sum over tableaux whose first and last $k$ vertices lie in the same columns.

papers.title: On orbits of the automorphism group of toroidal spherical varieties
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the orbits of the automorphism group on a toroidal spherical variety. In the affine case, we prove that two points lie in the same orbit of the identity component if and only if the kernels of the homomorphisms from the divisor class group to their local divisor class groups coincide. These kernels are described in terms of $B$-stable prime divisors. For a smooth complete toroidal spherical variety, we obtain a similar criterion using the monoids generated by the classes of $B$-stable prime divisors that do not contain a given $G$-orbit.

papers.title: Strongly Pseudoperfect Numbers
papers.abstract: A positive integer $n$ is said to be strongly pseudoperfect if there is a subset $S$ of the positive divisors of $n$ such that $d \in S$ if and only if $n/d \in S$, and $\sum_{d \in S} d = 2n$. We construct new infinite families of strongly pseudoperfect numbers, and also prove new restrictions on when a positive integer $n$ can be strongly pseudoperfect.

papers.title: Spin and scalar curvature on punctured four manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that a closed spin four-manifold with nonzero signature, even after being punctured along a finite graph, does not admit a complete metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature. We also show that this implies Schoen's conjecture on $L^{\infty}$-metrics with non-negative scalar curvature for these manifolds. This is in contrast to higher dimensions. A key new observation, which could be of independent interest, is that Gromov's $\mu$-bubbles are a convenient class of boundaries for the APS boundary value problem for the Dirac operator.

papers.title: The Maximal Robust Positively Invariant Set for Linear Difference Inclusions
papers.abstract: This article develops a systematic characterization and exact computational framework for the maximal robust positively invariant set of linear difference inclusions. The maximal set is characterized as the greatest fixed point of the robust predecessor operator, leading to three equivalent set iterations for its computation. Under uniform exponential stability and bounded disturbances, the Kuratowski upper limit of the disturbance-reachable sets yields a necessary and sufficient condition for the maximal set to be nonempty under closed state constraints. Sufficient conditions for its finite determination are also established, together with an explicit bound on the determination index. For polyhedral state constraints, bounded disturbances, and finite or polytopic matrix families, exact half-space implementations of the three iterations are derived. Although these algorithms generate the same set sequence, complexity analysis and numerical experiments reveal substantial differences in their computational performance.

papers.title: Deep Truncated FBSDE Method for High-Dimensional Nonlinear PDEs and Fully Coupled FBSDEs
papers.authors: Xinyu Cheng, Yunzhang Li, Weiran Xiong
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a deep truncated forward-backward stochastic differential equation (FBSDE) method for high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) and fully coupled FBSDEs. The proposed method combines gradient-truncated iterative decoupling with fictitious-play averaging to separate the forward and backward processes in a coupled framework. This preserves the coupled dynamics while reducing the unstable feedback induced by parameter-dependent forward paths during optimization. Furthermore, we incorporate a pathwise consistency term to create explicit local gradient shortcuts, thereby providing a structural mechanism that may mitigate gradient vanishing. We also derive a residual-based error estimate and establish conditional convergence of the fully discrete numerical approximations under suitable conditions, in which the pathwise consistency loss is not required. Our approach is particularly effective for convection-dominated equations, where the coupled formulation provides a stable representation of nonlinear transport without introducing singular terms into the BSDE. Numerical experiments demonstrate improved accuracy and stability in both low- and high-dimensional problems and robust performance for strongly coupled problems.

papers.title: The sixth moment of a degree two $L$-function of arbitrary level
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a primitive holomorphic cusp form of arbitrary weight, level and nebentypus. We prove $\int_0^T|L(1/2+it,f)|^6\,dt\ll_{f,\epsilon}T^{2+\epsilon}$, extending Jutila's level-one theorem. The new ingredient is a large sieve comparing the stationary phases in the Booker-Milinovich-Ng transformation at different heights. Applications include moments of order $T^{1+\epsilon}$ on every line to the right of the critical line, $\Omega(T^{4/35-\epsilon})$ simple zeros, zero density estimates, and bounds for cubic-field power sums, shifted convolution sums and the general divisor problem.

papers.title: Unipotent representations and the categorical trace of Frobenius
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the classification of unipotent representations for split finite groups of Lie type. To do this, we first construct an (infinity, 2)-categorification of Lusztig's map from the Hecke algebra to the asymptotic algebra. Then we use the theory of weights to show that it induces an isomorphism after applying trace of Frobenius.

papers.title: Explicit twists of the Carlitz module and of its tensor powers with unbounded analytic rank
papers.abstract: Grishkov and Logachev have asked (Problem 1.4 of their recent survey) whether, for a fixed finite field F_q, the analytic ranks of the twists of the Carlitz module are bounded. We answer this in the negative for every q >= 3. For q = p^s and n >= 1 put P_{q,n} = (theta^{q^n} - theta)^{q-2}. We show that the directed graph of the matrix M(P_{q,n},1,k) of Grishkov-Logachev has a completely explicit set of circuits: they are pairwise disjoint, none of them meets an entry involving t, and they are in bijection with the orbits of E^n under cyclic rotation, where E = {l in [0,q-2] : p does not divide l+1}. Consequently L(C_{P_{q,n}},t,T) does not depend on t, factors as a product of one term 1 - wt(nu) T^{per(nu)} per orbit, and the analytic rank equals the sum of p^{v_p(per(nu))} over the orbits of weight 1. When n is a power of p this equals (q/p)^n (p-1)^{n-1}, which is unbounded. The argument also answers questions 3.6.1-3.6.4 of the survey for this family. We then compute the L-function for arbitrary nonzero coefficients on supports of the same shape: taking all coefficients equal to -1 multiplies the rank by p-1, and the full support gives twists of degree (q-2)q^n and analytic rank (q-1)^n, the largest rank attainable on such supports. The same method applies to the tensor powers of the Carlitz module: for 1 <= e <= q-2 we obtain twists of the e-th tensor power of analytic rank (q-e)^n, and by a formula of Grishkov and Logachev the same holds for every exponent e = c q^j with 1 <= c <= q-2, with rank (q-c)^n; in particular these analytic ranks are unbounded as well.

papers.title: Quantitative Gowers uniformity of the primes in intervals of length $X^{5/8+\varepsilon}$
papers.abstract:
We prove the first quantitative bounds for the Gowers norms of the von Mangoldt function minus a Siegel corrected model function in short intervals. The result applies to intervals $(X,X+H]$ with $H\geq X^{5/8+\varepsilon}$ and gives quasipolynomial savings for the $U^k(X,X+H]$ norm. The main new ingredient is an efficient non-abelian Type II inverse theorem with explicit dependence on the nilsequence dimension. We prove this inverse theorem by applying Leng's efficient equidistribution theorem directly to an unweighted corner correlation in four variables, hence replacing the factorisation and subgroup argument in the non-abelian Type II proof of Matom\"aki, Shao, Tao and the author.
  In joint work with Florian Richter, we use this quantitative result as one ingredient in proving the existence of infinitely many sum-product patterns of the form $\{x,x+y,xy\}$ in the shifted primes $\mathbb{P}-1$.

papers.title: Clifford Actions and the Algebra of Double Forms
papers.abstract: Let $V$ be an oriented Euclidean vector space and let $\D(V)=\Lambda V^*\otimes\Lambda V^*$ be the algebra of double forms. The two exterior factors carry natural factorwise exterior and interior multiplication operators and therefore two commuting Clifford actions. The central result of the paper is an intrinsic realization of these Clifford actions inside Greub's composition algebra. For $a\in V^*$ we introduce the inhomogeneous double form \[ \chi_a=((1\otimes a)-(a\otimes1))e^g, \] prove that the $\chi_a$ satisfy the Clifford relations for the composition product, and establish the exact regular-action formulas \[ C_R(a)\omega=\chi_a\circ\omega, \qquad C_L(a)\omega=-\omega\circ\chi_a. \] For $h\in\D^{1,1}$ this yields a canonical four-component decomposition of the coupled left--right Clifford action into exterior multiplication, double contraction and two generalized Bianchi operators. For the metric double form $g$ these four operators generate two commuting $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ actions. The construction extends canonically to arbitrary bidegree. In bidegree $(2,2)$ its degree-preserving component admits a direct comparison with the double-form extension of the sharp product: for every $R\in\D^{2,2}$, \[ \Gamma_{1,1}(R)(\omega)=\frac14R\#\omega. \] The point of this identity is not a new definition of $R\#$, which is already constructed from Clifford commutators, but the fact that it appears canonically as the central homogeneous component of the higher left--right Clifford transform. As an application, the algebraic quadratic map $\mathcal Q(R)=-\frac14R\#R$ satisfies \[ \mathcal Q(R)=-\Gamma_{1,1}(R)R, \] and its linearization at $R$ is the operator $-2\Gamma_{1,1}(R)$. For curvature tensors this is the sharp contribution to the Ricci-flow reaction term.

papers.title: Dunkl--BMO functions representable in terms of generalized balayage of Carleson measures and an application
papers.abstract:
We characterize compactly supported functions $f$ in Dunkl--BMO spaces as those that can be written as \begin{equation*}
  f=g+\widetilde{S}_{\mu,\mathcal{P}}, \end{equation*} the sum of some bounded function $g$ and the generalized balayage $\widetilde{S}_{\mu,\mathcal{P}}$ of a Carleson measure on $\mathbb{R}^{N}\times(0,\infty)$ associated with the Dunkl--Poisson semigroup. As a direct application of this representation of Dunkl--BMO functions, we establish a new characterization of the Hardy space in the Dunkl setting via a principal value integral related to $\widetilde{S}_{\mu,\mathcal{P}}$. Moreover, analogous conclusions hold for the Dunkl--heat semigroup as well.

papers.title: Strong freezing in binary perceptron models
papers.abstract: The binary perceptron model concerns the set of solutions obtained by intersecting random half-spaces. One of the most striking physics predictions for this model, going back to Krauth and M\'ezard [KM89] and sharpened in [HWK13, HK14], is strong freezing: typical solutions are at Hamming distance of order $n$ from every other solution. This phenomenon has attracted a lot of attention over the years, partly because of its intricate connections to statistical physics and computational complexity. We prove strong freezing at every positive constraint density for a general class of perceptron models and for any disorder with independent entries of mean zero and unit variance. More precisely, with probability at least $1-e^{-c\sqrt n}$, all but an $e^{-c\sqrt n}$ fraction of the solutions have no other solution within Hamming distance $\delta n$. In particular, our result includes the asymmetric binary perceptron at every margin, for which strong freezing has been a long-standing open problem [KM89,HWK13,HK14], and the symmetric binary perceptron, for which we recover the strong freezing results of Perkins and Xu [PX24] and of Abbe, Li and Sly [ALS21]. Our proof crucially relies on replacing the number of constraints by a Poisson variable, which makes the numbers of constraints cutting out different subsets of the hypercube independent. Since each constraint can only remove solutions, the FKG inequality then decouples the partition function from the event that two nearby configurations are both solutions.

papers.title: On weak commutativity between $n$ isomorphic groups, $n \geq 2$
papers.authors: Said N. Sidki, Nora\'i R. Rocco, Ricardo N. de Oliveira, Dmytro Savchuk
papers.abstract: The Weak Commutativity Group was defined by the first author in the early 1980's as $ \chi(H) = \langle H, H^\psi \mid [h,h^\psi] = 1, \ \forall h \in H \rangle $ where $H$ and $H^\psi$ are isomorphic groups under an isomorphism $\psi$, and proved that $\chi(-)$, seen as a group operator, preserved the classes of solvable groups, finite groups, finite $p$-groups, and perfect groups. The list has grown considerably since then (see references). It is clear that the iterated operator $\chi^n (-)$ also preserves the same classes. However, we observe that for $n \geq 2$ many of the $2^n$ $H$-generating copies of $\chi^n (H)$ fail to weakly commute among themselves. We introduce in this paper the "$n$-ary Weak Commutativity Group" generated by $n$ copies of $H$ which weakly commute among themselves; that is $ \chi_n (H) = \langle H, H^\psi, \dots, H^{\psi_{n-1}} \mid [h^{\psi_i}, h^{\psi_j}] = 1, \ \forall h \in H, \ 0 \leq i < j \leq n-1 \rangle $ (by definition, $H^{\psi_0} = H, H^{\psi_1} = H^\psi$). We study quotients of $\chi^n (H)$ which are also simultaneously quotients of $\chi_{2^n} (H)$; we refer to them as Hybrid $\chi^n (H)$ - $\chi_{2^n} (H)$ groups. For $n=2$ we determine the largest common quotient $Q(H)$ of $\chi^2(H)$ and $\chi_4(H)$, that is, the largest hybrid $\chi^2(H)$-$\chi_4(H)$ group. A related class of groups in our study is $\chi(n,H)$, a quotient of $\chi_n(H)$, previously introduced by the third named author in his 2007 doctoral thesis. We prove that this class of groups continues to preserve finiteness, nilpotency and perfectness, and we provide detailed information about their structure. In contrast, $\chi_n(H)$ behaves differently: $\chi_3(C_2 \times C_2)$ is infinite, while $\chi_3(C_{p^t} \times C_{p^u})$ is finite for $p$ odd.

papers.title: On S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy's Local Extrema Conjectures
papers.abstract: Let $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow (0,\infty)$ be a multiplicative function, and let $\omega > 0$. We consider the frequency with which patterns of the form $$ f(n) > \omega \max\{f(n-1),f(n+1)\}, \quad f(n) < \frac{1}{\omega}\min\{f(n-1),f(n+1)\} $$ occur in the sequence $(f(n))_n$, and give necessary conditions on $f$ so that the set of occurrences of at least one of these patterns has logarithmic density $0$. This includes a complete classification of all such completely multiplicative functions. As a particular application, we characterise (up to prime powers $p^k$, $k \geq 2$) all multiplicative functions $f: \mathbb{N} \rightarrow \mathbb{N}$ that have either finitely many local maxima, or finitely many local minima. This answers, in a strong form, two conjectures of A. S\'{a}rk\"{o}zy from 2001. \\ The proof is based on a natural ``pretentiousness'' dichotomy for additive functions. Key tools in the analysis include an analogue of the Matom\"{a}ki-Radziwi\l\l theorem for additive functions, due to the author, as well as a new bound for the concentration of the gaps $g(n+1)-g(n)$ of an additive function $g$, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: On wave operators for Hardy operators with and without perturbations
papers.abstract: We prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators in time-dependent scattering theory which intertwine the ordinary or fractional Laplacian and the corresponding Hardy operator, i.e., the fractional Laplacian with an added subcritical or critical Hardy potential, whenever the Hardy potential is short-range. Moreover, we prove asymptotic completeness of the wave operators intertwining Hardy operators with and without external short-range perturbations. We also show the nonexistence of the considered wave operators when the Hardy or external potentials are long-range. We arrive at these results using three different approaches. The first approach uses an abstract semigroup framework for asymptotic completeness of wave operators for Fourier multipliers with short-range potentials. The second approach uses Kato smoothness theory. In the third approach, we develop and apply new propagation estimates for Hardy operators with and without perturbations.

papers.title: On the maximum degree and order of $K_t$-minor-free graphs with positive Lin--Lu--Yau curvature
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent results on the order of connected graphs with positive Lin--Lu--Yau Ricci curvature under forbidden minor or forbidden subgraph conditions and minimum degree assumptions, we prove that, for every integer $t\ge 5$, every locally finite graph $G$ with no $K_t$ minor, minimum degree at least $t-1$ and positive Lin--Lu--Yau Ricci curvature on every edge satisfies \[ \Delta(G)=O(t^5\log^{3/2}t). \] The minimum degree condition $t-1$ is best possible. Moreover, if $G$ is connected, then $G$ is finite and \[|V(G)|<2t\Delta(G)^6=O(t^{31}\log^9 t). \]

papers.title: Sum of Squares and Non Sum of Squares Regimes for the Toeplitz Bottcher Wenzel Form
papers.abstract: Toeplitz matrices are among the simplest structured models of translation invariance, arising naturally in convolution, stationary covariance models, and discretizations of translation-invariant operators. For a pair of real matrices, the B\"ottcher--Wenzel form (BW form) is a nonnegative quartic measuring the gap in the corresponding commutator inequality. L\'aszl\'o conjectured that, when both matrices are Toeplitz, this quartic is a sum of squares for every matrix order. We show that the conjecture is false. More precisely, we identify an explicit family of corner-supported Toeplitz pairs, retaining only the outermost diagonals on the two sides, for which the associated BW form is not a sum of squares at all sufficiently large orders. The proof reduces the complete family of Gram representations to a finite complex test: its Gram-invariant part develops a strictly negative limiting direction, while the remaining Gram-dependent contribution vanishes. We also give an explicit sufficient threshold for the matrix order. The negative result is complemented by two positive regimes. If either Toeplitz factor is symmetric or skew-symmetric, then the corresponding BW form is SoS for every order, with the other factor allowed to be an arbitrary real Toeplitz matrix. For unrestricted Toeplitz pairs, we further prove SoS representability for every $2\le N\le50$, with formal Lean~4 verification through order 20. The large-order non-SoS theorem, including the explicit sufficient threshold, has also been formally verified in Lean 4.

papers.title: Positive-measure intersections of Bedford-McMullen carpets under similitudes
papers.authors: Ding-Kun Hu, Huo-Jun Ruan, Jian-Ci Xiao
papers.abstract: Let $K=K(n,m,\Gamma)$ be a Bedford-McMullen carpet with $n>m\geq2$ and $1<\#\Gamma<nm$, and let $\mu$ be a self-affine measure on $K$ with strictly positive weights. We prove that every similitude $f(z)=rOz+a$ satisfying $\mu(K\cap f(K))>0$ has a diagonal or anti-diagonal orthogonal part $O$, without any arithmetic restrictions on the defining bases. Under the same intersection hypothesis, we also show that $r\in n^{\mathbb{Q}}\cup m^{\mathbb{Q}}$ whenever $K$ is not a segment. For isometries satisfying this hypothesis, we further prove that $f(K)$ is simply a translate of $K$, thereby establishing a strengthened form of the 2010 conjecture of Elekes, Keleti and M\'ath\'e in this planar self-affine context.

papers.title: Coanalytic subfields and bases of prescribed dimension
papers.abstract: Assuming $V=L$, we construct proper coanalytic subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ and coanalytic Hamel and transcendence bases of every possible Hausdorff dimension, uniformly in the relevant parameters. There is a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ set $G\subseteq[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ whose sections $A_\alpha$ are proper subfields with $\dim_{\mathrm H}A_\alpha=\alpha$, form a strictly increasing chain, and satisfy $A_\alpha=\bigcup_{\beta<\alpha}A_\beta$ for $\alpha>0$. For every $n\ge1$, every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ and every $s\in[0,n]$, we construct a coanalytic Hamel basis of $\mathbb{R}^n$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. Likewise, for every countable subfield $K\subseteq\mathbb{C}$ and every $s\in[0,2]$, we construct a coanalytic transcendence basis of $\mathbb{C}$ over $K$ of Hausdorff dimension $s$. In each case, the bases are sections of a single lightface $\Pi^1_1$ relation, uniformly in codes for the coefficient field and in the prescribed dimension, as well as in $n$ for Hamel bases. More generally, we prove a uniform theorem for suitably coded families of pregeometries on Euclidean spaces. The constructions combine Cantor sets of controlled dimension with hyperarithmetic coding and coanalytic transfinite recursion. The complexity is optimal: proper subfields of $\mathbb{R}$ of positive Hausdorff dimension and bases of the stated kinds cannot be analytic.

papers.title: A curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form of a regular surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and its applications
papers.abstract: We study a Monge normal form of a surface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ based on the principal axes of its curvature ellipse. The curvature-ellipse-based Monge normal form is obtained using only Euclidean motions of the ambient space and local reparameterizations of the surface, and preserves the Euclidean invariants of the curvature ellipse, including its semi-axis lengths up to their ordering. We also give applications of this normal form to the $2$-jet geometry of surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^4$ and to the geometry of their orthogonal projections.

papers.title: On Densities in the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer Distance Problems over the Integers
papers.abstract: Motivated by the classical Erd\H{o}s and Falconer distance problems and Magyar's work on distance sets in $\mathbb Z^d$, we study discrete analogues of the Erd\H{o}s-Falconer unpinned and pinned distance problems over the integers. We ask how the discrete Hausdorff dimension of a set $A\subseteq\mathbb Z^d$ influences the size of its squared-distance sets, measured by generalized upper natural density and upper discrete mass dimension. We propose conjectures for both problems and prove the unpinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2,3$ and the pinned conjecture in dimensions $d=1,2$. For the unpinned problem in higher dimensions, we obtain explicit lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets using elementary integer sphere counting, results on the Erd\H{o}s distinct distances problem, and $\ell^p$-improving inequalities for discrete spherical averages. For the pinned problem, we obtain lower bounds for the dimensions of distance sets for some or every pin. We also establish more general results involving upper discrete mass dimension, upper discrete Banach dimension, and affine dimension, including bounds on the affine dimension of the exceptional set of pins. We construct examples showing that both conjectures are sharp in low dimensions. Further examples demonstrate how the distinctions among discrete Hausdorff dimension, upper discrete mass dimension, and upper discrete Banach dimension lead to different phenomena in the unpinned and pinned distance problems, including limitations on the nontrivial upper bounds these dimensions can provide for the dimensions of distance sets.

papers.title: Exponential decay of fractional moments in the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$
papers.abstract: For the $H^{2|2}$ model on $\mathbb Z^2$, we show that, at energy zero, the fractional moments of Green functions, $\mathbb E[ G(x,y)^s]$ decay exponentially in the distance between $x$ and $y$, for every constant edge weight $W>0$ and every $0<s<1/2$. Here $ G$ is the infinite-volume Green function of the associated random Schr\"odinger operator. The main ingredient is a quantitative lower bound on the derivative of the mean effective conductance with respect to the edge weights.

papers.title: Discorrelation of the M\"obius function with linear phases in short intervals
papers.abstract:
We introduce a new approach to studying correlations between arithmetic functions and linear phases with respect to highly irrational frequencies over short intervals. As an application, we prove that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H}\mu(n) e(n\alpha)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-1/3+\varepsilon } \] whenever $x^{0.58+\varepsilon }\leq H\leq x$. In the same range of $H$ we also show that \[ \Big|\sum_{x<n \leq x+H} \Lambda (n) e(n\alpha)\Big| \ll H(\log x)^{-A} \] for arbitrarily large $A>0$ unless there exists an integer $1\leq q\ll (\log x)^{O_A(1)}$ such that $\|q\alpha \| \ll x (\log x)^{O_A(1)}/H^2$. This breaks the $3/5$ barrier in Theorem 1.5 of arXiv:1911.09076v2 and Theorem 2 of [T. Zhan, "On the representation of large odd integer as a sum of three almost equal primes," Acta Mathematica Sinica 7.3 (1991), 259-272].
  Moreover, by our method, any improvement in large value estimates for character-twisted Dirichlet polynomials on the critical range would lead to a corresponding improvement in the lower bound for $H$.

papers.title: A complete classification of the rational realization of gap-two products of Eilenberg--MacLane spaces as classifying spaces
papers.authors: Yang Bai, Xiugui Liu, Jiaxi Zha
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the rational realization of the gap-two product $K(\mathbb{Q},n)\times K(\mathbb{Q},n+2)$ as the classifying space $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$ for a simply-connected $\pi$-finite space $X$ with rational homology of finite type. We prove that $K(\mathbb{Q},n)\times K(\mathbb{Q},n+2)$ can be realized as $B\mathrm{aut}_1(X)$ up to rational homotopy equivalence if and only if $n=3,4$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$. Moreover, we determine all their minimal Sullivan models up to isomorphism. The rational homotopy type of such $X$ is unique for $n=3$ or $4m+2$ for $m\geq 1$; there exist infinitely many rational homotopy types of such $X$ for $n=4$.

papers.title: Tur\'an densities of hypergraph augmentations
papers.authors: Oleg Pikhurko, Jiabao Yang, Xiutao Zhu
papers.abstract:
For a $t$-graph $F$ and an integer $r\ge t$, the \emph{$r$-augmentation} $F(r)$ is the $r$-graph obtained by adding the same set of $r-t$ new vertices to every edge of $F$. We investigate the behaviour of the \emph{Tur\'an density $\pi(F(r))$}, which is the asymptotically maximum edge density of a large $F(r)$-free $r$-graph, as a function of $r\to\infty$.
  Let $H_k^r$ be the $r$-augmentation of the complete $(k-1)$-graph on $k$ vertices; equivalently, $H_k^r$ is the (unique up to isomorphism) $r$-graph with $r+1$ vertices and $k$ edges. This paper determines the Tur\'an density of each $r$-graph $H_k^r$ within a constant factor and estimates the lower bounds on $\pi(H_k^r)$ coming from the circular construction of Sidorenko. In particular, it is shown that if $k/\log r\to\infty$ then $\pi(H_k^r)=(1+o(1))k/r$.
  Also, we consider augmentations of graphs (that is, the case $t=2$) and prove that $\pi(F(r))\ge(\log r)^{-1-o(1)}/r$ for every 3-chromatic graph $F$, which comes close to the known upper bound $1/r$. Note that, for all other graphs $F$, the function $\pi(F(r))$ is known to be either identically 0 or uniformly bounded away from 0.

papers.title: Facets of nondegeneracy: central type factor groups, Heisenberg representations and Hadamard matrices
papers.authors: Pierre Bieliavsky, Victor Gayral, Sergey Neshveyev, Lars Tuset
papers.abstract: Given a pair of complementary subgroups $P$ and $N$ of a finite group $G$, we first discuss how the same type of functions $\mathbb E\colon P\times N\to \mathbb T$, which we call bi-$1$-cocycles, appear naturally in the study of projective representations of $G$ of Heisenberg type and second cohomology of $G$ and of its dual quantum group $\widehat G$. We show then that such representations are irreducible and the corresponding ordinary and dual $2$-cocycles are nondegenerate if and only if the matrix $(\mathbb E(p,n))_{p,n}$ is invertible, if and only if it is Hadamard. We illustrate the result with examples arising from symplectic nilpotent Lie algebras over finite fields with two complementary Lagrangian subalgebras.

papers.title: Geodesically Convex Optimization in Hyperbolic Space: Matching Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Wendao Wu, Haihan Zhang, Chenheng Zhang, Yanyi Li, Chunyuan Zheng, Cong Fang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin
papers.abstract: We establish matching lower bounds for deterministic first-order optimization of globally Lipschitz geodesically convex functions on hyperbolic space. A global minimizer lies within distance $r$ of a known point, each query returns an exact function value and a selected Riemannian subgradient, and the target objective gap is $\varepsilon Lr$, where $L$ is the Lipschitz constant. For sectional curvature $-k^2<0$, let $\rho=kr$ and $\zeta=\rho/\tanh\rho$. The optimal worst-case query complexity $Q^\star$, taken uniformly over dimensions, satisfies $Q^\star(\rho,\varepsilon)=\Theta(\zeta\varepsilon^{-2})$ for every $\rho>0$ and $0<\varepsilon\le1/64$. The new lower bound covers arbitrary adaptive deterministic queries and arbitrary outputs, matching the projected-subgradient upper rate of Zhang and Sra (2016). It removes the geodesic-span and historical-halfspace restrictions of earlier matching lower bounds. The construction extends a radial source from a convex carrier with boundary. A small residual cut selects minimizer candidates while an exact hyperbolic persistence inequality keeps every historical contact valid under future carrier growth. One fixed globally convex objective and one fixed subgradient selection consequently realize all exact replies simultaneously. Each query consumes $O(\varepsilon^2)$ of a geometric potential whose available budget is $\Theta(\zeta)$, yielding the product lower bound in a dimension linear in the query horizon.

papers.title: Unbounded Helson Forms with a Moment Representation
papers.authors: Tengfei Ma, Yufeng Lu, Chao Zu
papers.abstract: We study the positive Helson form $h_0[a,b]=\sum_{m,n\ge1}\alpha(mn)a_n\overline{b_m}$ on the finitely supported sequences $c_{00}\subset\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$, where $\alpha(n)=\int_{\mathbb{R}}n^{-s}d\mu(s)<\infty$ for a finite positive Borel measure $\mu$. Under the Carleman condition $\sum_{k\ge1}\alpha(4^k)^{-1/(2k)}=\infty$, closability of $h_0$ is equivalent to $\sqrt{n}\alpha(n)\to0$, and hence to $\mu((-\infty,1/2])=0$. For measures concentrated on $(1/2,\infty)$, we identify the closure of the operator $N_0a=\sum_{n\ge1}a_nn^{-s}$, defined on $c_{00}$, with its maximal realization from $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$ to $L^2(\mu)$. We further prove that the sequences $a\in c_{00}$ satisfying $\sum_{n\ge1}a_n/\sqrt{n}=0$ form an operator core for the positive self-adjoint operator associated with the closure of $h_0$.

papers.title: Asymptotic Root Dynamics under Repeated and Fractional Integration
papers.abstract: Fix a polynomial $P(x)=\sum_{j=0}^m a_jx^j$ of degree $m$, and let $I_kP$ be its $k$-fold antiderivative with all integration constants zero. Borwein, Chen, and Dilcher proved that, after $x=ky$, the nonzero zeros of $I_kP$ converge to the nonzero zeros of $L[P](y)=\sum_j a_j j! y^j$.
